Initial commit: Claude Code baseline + release workflow

Brings up create-baseline as a Node CLI scaffolder (npx create-baseline
<target>) that materializes a 22-hook, 1-subagent, 36-skill governance
baseline into any project. Build pipeline at scripts/build-template.sh
rebuilds obj/template/ from src/*.template.* + .claude/ on every npm pack.

Includes the manually-triggered release workflow at .github/workflows/
release.yml: workflow_dispatch with mode in {release, docs-only} and
bump_type in {major, minor, patch}; four-job pipeline (build-verify ->
publish-npm -> {deploy-pages, push-bump, install-smoke}); OIDC trusted
publishing with --provenance; every third-party action SHA-pinned and
verified at run time via scripts/verify-action-shas.mjs; harden-runner
audit-mode first in every job; concurrency: cancel-in-progress: false.

Operational runbook at docs/runbooks/npm-publish.md covers the automated
path and the manual fallback (Snyk-aligned workstation hygiene sweeps).

Tests: 197 across tests/*.test.mjs covering the CLI, build pipeline,
publish-check chain, workflow YAML invariants, install-smoke verifier,
SHA authenticity verifier (opt-in VERIFY_ACTION_SHAS=1), every hook
and skill contract. Dependabot configured for weekly GitHub Actions
SHA bumps.
last_commit_message:
feat(document): reflective public-site trigger + feature-value register

Club B — two /document Step 2 gaps, both observed live.

7b3e (user feedback): /document routed site-src/** prose through the
reference register only, so a public page got its mechanism described but
not its user-facing feature value. Step 2 now routes every public-site
surface through TWO registers — documentation (reference: what/how) AND
prose in the persuasive/copywriting register (the feature value) — per
the standing guidance to describe the feature, not just the behavior.

5e07: Step 2 classified by file PRESENCE, so a change that alters behavior
an existing public page describes — but touches no site-src file — was
treated as "no site work," backwards. A new read-only helper,
.claude/skills/document/public-site-reflect.mjs, exports
findDescribedSurfaces({changedPaths, root}): it derives the skill / hook /
command tokens the diff touches and word-boundary-greps site-src/**/*.njk
for pages that name them, returning the described pages even when no site
file is in the diff. Step 2 runs it and routes each returned page through
both registers above. Surface-only: the page and registers are
identified; the prose still flows through the prose delegate (humanizer
always), and no site-src content is written by /document itself.

The trigger was dogfooded on this very change: run against the diff it
correctly surfaced the three public pages that name the document phase
(index, skills/core, workflows) with no site file in the diff; judged no
user-facing delta here, so no site edit.

New test: document-public-site-reflect (reflective match, no false
trigger, read-only, SKILL.md documents both registers). Suite 693/693;
audit PASS.

Feature/gesture based sync (#129)

* docs: Add gesture-based sync strategy task (Task 19)

Comprehensive analysis of current full-blob API endpoints and proposed
gesture-based alternatives:

Current problematic endpoints:
- PUT /clips/{id} sends full crop_data, segments_data, timing_data
- PUT /overlay-data sends full highlights_data array
- PUT /annotations sends full annotations array

Proposed solution:
- POST /actions endpoints with atomic operations
- Each user gesture = one API call (add_keyframe, delete_region, etc.)
- Version numbers for conflict detection
- Enables future merge of non-conflicting edits

This addresses same-session data overwrites and provides foundation
for Task 17 (stale session detection).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <<redacted>>

* feat: Implement gesture-based overlay sync (Task 19 Phase 1)

Replace full-blob overlay saves with atomic action endpoints.
Each user gesture (add region, update keyframe, etc.) is now sent
as an individual action, preventing data overwrites.

Backend changes:
- Add POST /overlay/actions endpoint with atomic handlers
- Support create_region, delete_region, update_region, toggle_region
- Support add_keyframe, update_keyframe, delete_keyframe, set_effect_type
- Add overlay_version column for future conflict detection
- Accept client-generated region_id for optimistic updates

Frontend changes:
- Create overlayActions.js API client
- Wrap all overlay handlers to dispatch actions immediately
- Local state updates optimistically, backend sync is fire-and-forget
- Keep full-blob save on beforeunload/navigation as safety net

Benefits:
- No overwrites from concurrent component edits
- Efficient (only sends what changed)
- Version tracking enables future conflict detection

Tests: 7 new tests for overlay actions, all passing

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <<redacted>>

* feat: Implement gesture-based framing sync (Task 19 Phase 2)

Add atomic action endpoints for framing modifications instead of full-blob saves:

Backend (clips.py):
- Add POST /projects/{id}/clips/{id}/actions endpoint
- Implement 9 action handlers: add/update/delete/move crop keyframes,
  split/remove segment, set segment speed, set/clear trim range
- Add proper error handling with 400 status codes for validation errors
- Fix remove_segment_split logic to work with any boundary

Frontend (FramingContainer.jsx):
- Add framingActions.js API client with all action methods
- Modify handlers to dispatch actions alongside local state updates
- Handlers affected: handleCropComplete, handleKeyframeDelete, handleAddSplit,
  handleRemoveSplit, handleSegmentSpeedChange, handlePasteCrop, handleTrimSegment,
  handleDetrimStart, handleDetrimEnd

Testing:
- Add test_framing_actions.py with 11 tests (all passing)
- Fix test isolation issue in test_annotations_aggregates.py (reset user context)
- All 333 backend tests pass, 349 frontend unit tests pass, 33/34 E2E pass

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <<redacted>>

* updated .mds, created skills

* fix: Only show framing unsaved dialog when working video exists

With gesture-based sync, framing data is auto-saved to the database.
The "unsaved changes" dialog was showing when navigating to project-manager
even when there was no working video to invalidate.

Now the dialog only appears when there's actually a working video that
would be out of sync with the framing changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <<redacted>>

* fix: Restore trim data saved in export format without segments array

The auto-save path saves trim data using getExportData() which returns
{ trim_start: X, trim_end: Y } (export format). When there are no speed
changes, no segments array is created.

Previously, restoreState() only checked for trim_start/trim_end when a
segments array was present (export format detection). Without segments,
it fell into the internal format branch which only looked for trimRange
key, causing trim data to be lost on project reloa

feat(asvs-verify): package engine as `asvs` uv command, drop raw python

Turn the raw `python3 .claude/skills/asvs-verify/scripts/asvs.py …`
invocation into a single named command, `asvs`, run via uv — the
spec-kit `specify`-with-uv UX. Easier to use and no longer exposes
raw Python or a fragile script path.

  (hatchling, stdlib-only, empty deps — uv provides the named command,
  not dependency management).
- Move scripts/asvs.py -> asvs_verify/ package; resolve bundled data via
  importlib.resources instead of `__file__/../references`, so it works
  under a built wheel / uvx / uv tool install and from any cwd.
- Make the package data (asvs-5.0.0.json, tool-map.json) the single
  source of truth (removes the duplicate references/ copies).
- Add `python3 -m asvs_verify` offline fallback and a .gitignore for
  build artifacts.
- Sweep all docs (SKILL.md, README.md, CLAUDE.md, GOALS.md, levels.md,
  attestation template, worked example) to the `asvs` command and state
  the uv prerequisite plainly.

Verified from a foreign cwd: level counts match the original engine
(L1=70, L2=253, L3=345), scaffold→report round-trips, uv tool install
puts `asvs` on PATH, and the integrity check still rejects evidence-free
PASS.

description: Force a full rebuild of the memory index with the active embedding provider/model. Use when the user sends /memory-rebuild, memory_search returns 'index metadata is missing', the status shows identity=missing or mismatch on an agent that has data, or after a model swap in the gateway config. This is the documented recovery path for DarojaAI/openclaw-gateway#21.
first_commit_message:
feat(gateway): post-deploy memory-index verification gate + memory skills (#35)

* feat(gateway): post-deploy memory-index verification gate

Addresses DarojaAI/openclaw-gateway#21: memory_search returns
'disabled: true, unavailable: true, error: index metadata is missing'
when the on-disk index sidecar is missing or was written by a different
embedding provider/model. The deploy pipeline was silently green
because the existing health check (/healthz + gateway process)
does not look at the memory index — the disable message only
surfaces when an agent actually calls memory_search.

The root-cause upstream race lives in openclaw/openclaw#90361 and
PR #90453 is the mergeable closing PR (owned by upstream
maintainers — L3b does not duplicate the fix). This commit adds
the L3b-side detection + deploy-gate integration that catches
regressions of the same shape at the deploy boundary.

What ships:

1. scripts/lib-parse-memory-status.py
   Pure decision logic. Reads JSON from stdin (the output of
   'openclaw memory status --json') and emits TSV rows
   (agent_id<TAB>verdict<TAB>reason). Verdicts:
     ok            identity=ok
     warn-fresh    identity missing/mismatch but no data yet
     warn-swap     provider != requestedProvider
     warn-unknown  unrecognized identity state (forward-compat)
     fail          identity missing/mismatch AND data present

2. scripts/post-deploy-verify-memory-index.sh
   Bash wrapper that runs the probe, classifies rows, and decides:
     exit 0 = healthy (or fresh install)
     exit 1 = degraded index on an agent that has data (deploy gate fails)
     exit 2 = probe failure (openclaw not on PATH, JSON parse error)
   Honors SKIP_POST_DEPLOY_MEMORY_CHECK=1 (opt-out) and
   MEMORY_CHECK_FAIL_ON_FRESH=1 (promote fresh-install WARN to FAIL).

3. scripts/install/deploy.sh
   Wires the verify script in as section 7 (post-deploy verification,
   called immediately before 'OpenClaw Gateway installation complete').
   Exit 1 fails the deploy gate; exit 2 is soft-warned (don't block
   deploy on missing CLI).

4. tests/post-deploy-verify-memory-index.bats
   19 cases covering: healthy / fresh / regression / mismatch /
   multi-agent / MEMORY_CHECK_FAIL_ON_FRESH / provider swap /
   unknown state / skip / openclaw-not-on-PATH / invalid JSON /
   empty output / no agents / parser existence / parser inline-
   python-free / parser exit codes / deploy.sh wiring.

5. docs/troubleshooting/memory-index-disabled.md
   Symptom / diagnose / recover / why / prevention matrix /
   forward-compat notes. Cross-links to upstream issue #90361 and
   the mergeable closing PR #90453.

Verification:
- bats tests/post-deploy-verify-memory-index.bats: 19/19 pass
- shellcheck --severity=warning: clean on both new bash scripts
- pre-commit run --files <all>: clean
- python3 -m py_compile: clean on the parser lib

Refs:
- DarojaAI/openclaw-gateway#21
- openclaw/openclaw#90361 (root cause)
- openclaw/openclaw#90453 (upstream closing PR)

* feat(skills): add memory-status and memory-rebuild slash commands

Brings the recovery flow for DarojaAI/openclaw-gateway#21 out of the
SSH-only domain and into Discord. Both skills are wired into the
existing skill-sync phase of scripts/install/deploy.sh (section 6) —
no extra deploy wiring is needed.

Two skills:

1. memory-status (/memory-status)
   Reads 'openclaw memory status --json' and produces a per-agent
   table with: agent, identity (ok/missing/mismatch), provider,
   chunks, notes. Surfaces the L3b deploy gate's verdict matrix
   (warn-fresh / warn-swap / fail) so the user knows whether a
   rebuild is required, or whether the index is empty and will
   rebuild on first-use.

2. memory-rebuild (/memory-rebuild)
   Runs 'openclaw memory index --force' and reports the result.
   Lists the documented failure modes (auth error, EACCES,
   model-not-in-catalog) and the recovery steps for each. Warns
   before rebuilding blindly — does not auto-rebuild on unknown
   identity states.

first_commit_message:
Add Codex plugin packaging for ToolUniverse (#249)

* Add Codex plugin packaging

* Wire Codex plugin into skill-sync + release pipeline; bring to parity

The Codex plugin packaging lived outside the Claude plugin's release flow, so its
bundled skills and version drifted (134 skills @ 1.2.4 vs Claude's 136 @ 1.2.18).
This puts both packagings on one pipeline:

- plugin/sync-skills.sh now rebuilds BOTH plugin/skills/ (Claude) and
  plugins/tooluniverse/skills/ (Codex) from the canonical skills/ tree; Codex
  drops Claude-Code-specific skills (tooluniverse-claude-code-plugin).
- scripts/release-plugin.sh now also bumps plugins/tooluniverse/.codex-plugin/
  plugin.json on release, so Codex's version tracks Claude's.

One-time parity:
- Codex skills resynced (135 = 136 user-facing minus the Claude-only skill);
  adds tooluniverse-peptide-target-deorphanization, drops stale entries.
- Codex plugin.json 1.2.4 -> 1.2.18 to match the current release.
- Restored skills/tooluniverse-custom-tool/references/json-tool.md: PR #194 edited
  only the Claude plugin copy, leaving the source missing the API-key declaration
  docs, which any resync would otherwise drop.

Codex auto-upgrades owner/repo Git marketplaces on startup, so this reaches Codex
users on next launch; Claude users get it via the version bump.

* Fix Codex skill sync: delegate to the Codex-specific normalizer

The prior pipeline commit rebuilt plugins/tooluniverse/skills/ with the same
filter as the Claude copy, which left in the disable-model-invocation marker
(rejected by Codex validation; 133 skills) and descriptions over Codex's
1024-char limit (4 skills). Have plugin/sync-skills.sh delegate the Codex copy to
scripts/sync-codex-plugin-skills.sh — which strips the marker and compacts long
descriptions — instead of duplicating and diverging from that logic. Also add an
evals/ exclude to the Codex sync so dev eval scaffolding does not ship, matching
the Claude filter.

* Run the Codex plugin packaging test in CI

tests/test_codex_plugin.py lived at the tests/ top level, outside pytest.ini's
testpaths (tests/unit, tests/integration, tests/tools), so CI never collected it
— its per-skill assertions (description <= 1024 chars, disable-model-invocation
not set) silently never ran, which is why the earlier broken Codex skill regen
passed CI. Move it under tests/unit/, fix the repo-root parents[] depth, and mark
it unit so the Codex skill set is validated on every run.

* Rename Codex marketplace from tooluniverse-local to tooluniverse

The catalog name/displayName carried a 'local' suffix left over from local-dir
testing, but this is the published GitHub marketplace users add via
`codex plugin marketplace add mims-harvard/ToolUniverse`. Drop the misleading
'local' so it lists as 'tooluniverse' / 'ToolUniverse'.

* Update Codex plugin README: add install steps, point sync at the shared script

- Add an Install section (codex plugin marketplace add mims-harvard/ToolUniverse
  + codex plugin add tooluniverse) — the README had no end-user install steps.
- Point the Development sync at plugin/sync-skills.sh, the unified entry point
  that rebuilds BOTH the Claude and Codex skill copies; the old instruction ran
  only the Codex-specific sync, so following it left the Claude copy stale.

* Version plugins as <package MAJOR.MINOR>.<plugin revision>

Tie both plugin versions to the PyPI package's MAJOR.MINOR while letting them
carry an independent PATCH (the plugin revision). release-plugin.sh now derives
the next version from pyproject.toml's MAJOR.MINOR and bumps the plugin PATCH
(resetting to .0 when the package's MAJOR.MINOR advances), instead of bumping the
plugin's own semver freely. This keeps Claude + Codex plugin versions coherent
with the package they serve while a skill-only change ships as a PATCH bump —
without forcing an empty PyPI package release.

* Update RELEASING.md for the package-tracked plugin version scheme

Document the <package MAJOR.MINOR>.<plugin revision> schem

tests/test_codex_plugin.py lived at the tests/ top level, outside pytest.ini's
testpaths (tests/unit, tests/integration, tests/tools), so CI never collected it
— its per-skill assertions (description <= 1024 chars, disable-model-invocation
not set) silently never ran, which is why the earlier broken Codex skill regen
passed CI. Move it under tests/unit/, fix the repo-root parents[] depth, and mark
it unit so the Codex skill set is validated on every run.

* Rename Codex marketplace from tooluniverse-local to tooluniverse

The catalog name/displayName carried a 'local' suffix left over from local-dir
testing, but this is the published GitHub marketplace users add via
`codex plugin marketplace add mims-harvard/ToolUniverse`. Drop the misleading

Tie both plugin versions to the PyPI package's MAJOR.MINOR while letting them
carry an independent PATCH (the plugin revision). release-plugin.sh now derives
the next version from pyproject.toml's MAJOR.MINOR and bumps the plugin PATCH
(resetting to .0 when the package's MAJOR.MINOR advances), instead of bumping the
plugin's own semver freely. This keeps Claude + Codex plugin versions coherent
with the package they serve while a skill-only change ships as a PATCH bump —
without forcing an empty PyPI package release.

feat: full armor + ammo system from #1929 (damage profiles + armor design stats) (#1932)

5 armor models × 9 ammo types with profile-driven damage. Each ammo carries a damage profile (HiExp / ArmPen / Frag / Tandem / Elec); armor behavior is a per-type stats table (plateDamage_* / penetration_* + singleUsePlates + deflectsSurfaceEffect) resolved through ArmorDesignState.response() → bypass | block | engage. The central damage-matrix.ts lookup module is deleted.
Ship configs are self-contained literals: armor is declared by name (type: 'composite' | 'whipple' | 'hardened' | 'reactive' | 'faraday' + mandatory withFaradayLayer), resolved via the armorModels registry in makeArmor. No stat imports/spreads in configs.
Exhaustiveness by construction: per-type fields are mapped types over WeaponDamageType / AmmoType (armor stats, chaingun/tube use_*, magazine max_*), tables are as const satisfies Record<...> — adding a damage or ammo type fails compilation until every consumer takes a stance. Conventions recorded in docs/standards/standards-code-structure.md (+ -principles.md).
Polymorphic damageType on SpaceObjectBase (overridden by Projectile/Explosion) replaces instanceof checks; collisions carry the explicit 'Collision' member of SpaceDamageType = WeaponDamageType | 'Collision' — no null sentinel.
Damage-manager phase pipeline: takeWeaponDamage / takeCollisionDamage; unconditional surface scrape (gated only by deflectable × deflectsSurfaceEffect); one applyExposedSystemDamage over (system, exposure) candidates covers bypass/engage/electronics/per-area. Elec applies once per hit at worst exposure; Reactive pops exactly one cell per hit and consumes the defeated round (Tandem survives the pop).
Acronym-free ammo names (HiExpShell, ArmPenMissile, …) under one vocabulary: ammoTypes / ammoDesigns / AmmoType end-to-end. Literal numbers instead of abstract scales; heat-per-shot in ProjectileDesign; isElectronics/isInternal inherent SystemState properties; typed magazine accessors.
Design docs as contract: docs/design/mechanics/damage-model-spec.md states player-observable outcomes (per-second explosion damage, curve shape and roll scheme are tuning/implementation choices); decision records 006–011 cross-linked; known deviations documented (Reactive per-tick pop → spec §11).

this repo's genuinely local/personal state, not build output.

Pre-existing files unique to .claude/ (a handful of hooks/rules/agents
core/ doesn't have) were intentionally left in place, not deleted, since

[Architecture 1] Adopt XcodeGen for project generation (#4233)

* refactor: adopt XcodeGen for project generation [Architecture 1]

Replace the hand-maintained VultisigApp.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj with an
XcodeGen-generated project driven by VultisigApp/project.yml. Covers parent
issue #4208 and sub-issues #4209-#4213 in one branch.

What changed
------------
- VultisigApp/project.yml — XcodeGen spec for all 3 targets (VultisigApp,
  Tests, UITests). Preserves platform matrix (iOS 17.0+, macOS 15.0+),
  signing (team 5BP27CHH4Y, automatic), entitlements, 9 remote SPM
  packages + Mediator local + SwiftLintPlugins build-tool plugin, and the
  4 embedded xcframeworks (Tss, godkls, goschnorr, vscore).
- VultisigApp/scripts/bootstrap.sh — `xcodegen generate` wrapper;
  `--install` flag installs XcodeGen via Homebrew if missing.
- .gitignore — untrack the generated project.pbxproj and xcschemes; keep
  Package.resolved tracked for reproducible deps.
- .github/workflows/objective-c-xcode.yml — run xcodegen before build.
- README.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE_MIGRATION.md,
  .github/ISSUE_GUIDE.md, .claude/skills/create-issue/SKILL.md — drop the
  `/add-xcode-files` protocol; describe the XcodeGen workflow.
- .claude/hooks/protect-files.sh — redirect pbxproj edit attempts to
  project.yml instead of the removed skill.
- .claude/skills/add-xcode-files/ — deleted (obsolete).

Dead-code cleanup surfaced by the migration
-------------------------------------------
The legacy pbxproj silently excluded 10 Swift files from its Sources
build phase. XcodeGen's glob-all-swift behavior caught them:

- VultisigApp/Features/Wallet/Models/GroupedChain.swift (duplicate of the
  class in CoinsGrouped.swift)
- VultisigApp/Features/Keysign/Views/KeysignTestView.swift (broken; refs
  CurrentScreen, Chain.Bitcoin — old APIs)
- VultisigApp/Features/Wallet/Views/BackupVaultNowView.swift
- VultisigApp/Features/Wallet/Views/BackupVaultWarningView.swift
- VultisigApp/Features/FunctionCall/Views/FunctionCallDetailsView.swift
- VultisigApp/Features/FunctionCall/Views/FunctionCallVerifyView.swift
- VultisigApp/Features/MoonPay/Views/MoonPayDepositView.swift
- VultisigApp/Features/Onboarding/ImportVault/KeyImport/OnboardingVaultSetupScreen.swift
- VultisigApp/Blockchain/Swaps/Common/SwapServiceFactory.swift
- VultisigApp/Features/Defi/ThorchainPoolListView.swift

All had zero external references.

Three additional test files were also orphaned in the legacy target —
preserved on disk but excluded via project.yml for now:

- VultisigAppTests/Services/KyberSwapServiceTests.swift
- VultisigAppTests/Services/SwapPercentageTests.swift (type error)
- VultisigAppTests/Chains/ThorAddressValidationTests.swift

Fix or remove these in a follow-up.

Local verification
------------------
- `xcodegen generate --spec project.yml` succeeds
- iOS simulator build: ** BUILD SUCCEEDED **
- macOS build:         ** BUILD SUCCEEDED **
- Test build (scheme): ** TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED **

Follow-ups (deliberately deferred)
----------------------------------
- xcframework `expectedSignature` attributes are not yet surfaced by
  XcodeGen. Verify in Xcode (General → Frameworks) that each xcframework
  still shows "Do Not Embed" and signature tags match before release.
- Fastlane `increment_build_number` mutates the generated pbxproj; the
  bump is lost on next generation. Parameterize CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION
  via env var or a separate file.

* chore: add Makefile wrapping xcodegen + xcodebuild commands

Introduce a repo-root Makefile as the single entry point for common
dev tasks, so local dev and CI converge on the same commands.

Targets
-------
- make bootstrap  — install XcodeGen + SwiftLint via Homebrew and
  generate VultisigApp.xcodeproj. Idempotent.
- make generate   — regenerate the xcodeproj from VultisigApp/project.yml.
- make test       — build + run unit tests (VultisigApp scheme).
- make ui_test    — build + run UI tests (VultisigAppUITests scheme).
- make help

<redacted>

* feat(test): runtime DOM overflow detector for mobile audit

Exports findOverflow() — walks document.body, returns elements whose
right edge exceeds the viewport AND aren't bounded by a scrollable
ancestor. Standalone (no imports), so it serializes through
page.evaluate() to Playwright and can be pasted into DevTools.

* fix(css): wrap h1 + button resets in @layer base

Element selectors outside any cascade layer beat Tailwind utility
classes by source order, so <h1> rendered at 3.2em and <Button>
components had their font-size coerced to 1em regardless of text-*
utilities. Layer wrap lets utilities win.

* fix(i18n): trust <html lang> first in resolveLocale

Old order (?lang= → cookie → <html lang>) let the client pick a different
locale than the SSR-blessed one when the cookie wasn't forwarded to the
server (proxy header stripping, prerendered routes, etc.). New order
trusts <html lang> first — guarantees server and client see identical
text on first paint, preventing React 19 hydration mismatch.

* feat(i18n): post-hydration cookie locale sync on prerendered routes

When <html lang> is the build-time fallback (prerendered /, /about) but
the user has a cookie-stored preference, switch after hydration so the
initial DOM stays SSR-consistent but the user's preference still wins
on subsequent renders.

* test(mobile): overflow + hydration audit specs for iPhone-SE/iPhone-13

Tagged @cicd so 'just test::pw::cicd' picks them up. Runs at both
mobile-pixel5 and mobile-iphone13 viewports via testMatch. Test data
sourced via getTournamentByKey/getEventsTestData (no hardcoded PKs).
Tests will fail until Task 6's per-offender fixes land.

* fix(i18n): guard resolveLocale against SSR document access

Task 4's import of `i18n` into root.tsx pulls client.ts into the server
bundle, where its module-init resolveLocale() crashed reading
document.documentElement.lang. Return FALLBACK_LOCALE early on the
server; client hydration still picks <html lang> first.

* chore(git): ignore playwright screenshots dir

Run output, not source.

* feat(ui): shared PageHeader for entity detail routes

Compact mobile-first header — title is text-base font-semibold on mobile,
scales up to text-4xl font-bold at lg. Centered on mobile, left-aligned
at sm+. Inline slot for a state badge beside the title; subtitle and
actions slots stack below.

Drop the stale verbose block comment above the h1 @layer wrap in app.css
(class names + commit history convey the cascade-layer rationale).

* feat(navbar): mobile-first responsive layout (#252)

- Move desktop nav from md: (768px) to lg: (1024px). The mobile drawer now
  covers tablet portrait too, avoiding the squish where 9 icon-only links
  fought 768px of width with the centered page-nav dropdown.
- Push the subtitle/vertical-stack pivot from xl: (1280px) to 2xl: (1536px)
  so 9 items don't crowd 1280-1535px viewports.
- Add explicit horizontal padding to the navbar (px-3 sm:px-4 lg:px-6)
  so the hamburger and login button aren't flush against the viewport.
- Collapse the Discord login button to icon-only below sm: so the
  centered page-nav dropdown doesn't clash with it on iPhone-SE width.
- Wrap the mobile drawer link list in shadcn ScrollArea so it scrolls
  cleanly on short phones instead of clipping.

* refactor(events,tournament): use shared PageHeader on detail pages

Event detail (#233) and Tournament detail (#232) were both rendering
oversized titles that overflowed iPhone-SE width and wrapped awkwardly
mid-word. Replace ad-hoc h1 + state-badge + date pill markup with the
shared PageHeader so the compact mobile-first sizing applies uniformly.

description: How to drive the OpenHands CLI headlessly as ola's `oh` backend — subprocess invocation, the agent_settings.json config it loads, the --JSON Event- stream format, and post-hoc metrics. Load whenever changing the `oh` backend.
first_commit_message:
oh: drive the OpenHands CLI in a subprocess instead of the in-process SDK

The in-process OpenHands SDK serialized every LLM call on a class-level
_litellm_modify_params_lock held across the whole network round-trip, so
the `oh` backend could only ever have one in-flight request per process
regardless of agent count — no real parallelism. Replace it with a
subprocess driver of the standalone `openhands` CLI (one process per task,
like cc/cx), which has its own litellm globals and lock, so the fan-out is
real.

- run() spawns `openhands --headless --json --override-with-envs -f <task>`
  with OPENHANDS_PERSISTENCE_DIR pointed at the per-task state dir (the
  cc/cx CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/CODEX_HOME equivalent) and OPENHANDS_WORK_DIR.
- Writes a per-task agent_settings.json (a serialized SDK Agent: kind + full
  llm block from LLM_* env + an LLMSummarizingCondenser) for full config
  fidelity, and still passes --override-with-envs so the rotating model/key/
  url always win and a corrupt file degrades to an env-built agent.
- Parses the CLI's `--JSON Event-` stream with raw_decode (not json.loads,
  which would choke on the trailing Rich console box and drop the final
  event — often the ConversationErrorEvent). Treats only a
  ConversationErrorEvent as fatal; headless exits 0 even on error, so
  success = returncode 0 AND no fatal event.
- Recovers token economics post-hoc from base_state.json (full, non-snapshot
  ConversationStats). No streaming-only timings (ttft_ms=0, streamed=False)
  like ct; llm_ms uses the real per-call response_latencies.
- Drops warm_up/SDK imports/_TTFTTracker/Laminar/the lock monkeypatch.
- No network-policy injection — pass the prompt verbatim and rely on the
  sandbox proxy, same as cc/cx/ct (delete NETWORK-POLICY.md).

Drop openhands-sdk/-tools from pyproject (the CLI is installed separately via
`uv tool install openhands`, not a Python dependency). De-stale the scheduler
warm_up comment and the ola.sh oh-config comments (agent_settings.json is no
longer an SDK-ignored side-channel). Rename the openhands-sdk skill to
openhands-cli (2.0.0) and rewrite it for the CLI; update CLAUDE.md and README.
Rewrite tests for the new parser, settings builder, event helpers, and
disk-based stats extraction.

chore(.claude): resync .claude/ from core/ via build-release.sh (item #4)

Resolves the core/.claude drift flagged in the earlier architecture
review. Investigation found .claude/ is not a personal sandbox — it's
this repo's own dogfood install target (plugin.json's install.target is
".claude/", and core/scripts/build-release.sh packages core/ into a zip
explicitly meant to be unzipped into a target project's .claude/, this
repo included). It had drifted badly: .claude/skills/ had only 402 of
core/'s 1990 skill dirs, several hooks/scripts/rules existed on only one
side, agents count differed by one.

Ran build-release.sh (which gates on a 100% hook-test pass — see the
separate hook-portability-fixes commit that unblocked it), then unzipped
the resulting pack over .claude/{agents,commands,config,docs,gates,hooks,
prompts,rules,scripts,skills,templates,tests}/ as a pure overlay (adds/
updates, does not delete). .claude/assistant/, .claude/state/, and
.claude/settings.json were excluded from the source zip already (not part
of build-release.sh's include list) and are confirmed untouched — that's
this repo's genuinely local/personal state, not build output.

Pre-existing files unique to .claude/ (a handful of hooks/rules/agents
core/ doesn't have) were intentionally left in place, not deleted, since
this pass didn't establish whether those are stray drift or deliberate
local additions — a separate decision, not blocking this resync.

Verified: bash .claude/tests/hooks/run-hook-tests.sh → 104/104 pass.

first_commit_message:
Add dejavu-onboarding and dejavu-error-triage skills

Round out the skill set so each step of the Dejavu lifecycle has a
purpose-built skill:

- dejavu-onboarding (197 lines) — adds Dejavu to a project from scratch:
  prerequisite check, gradle dependency for Android or KMP, first
  Modifier.testTag placement, smallest possible passing test, gradle run
  command. Hands off to dejavu-test-writer once installed.

- dejavu-error-triage (83 lines) — one-shot diagnosis of a single
  UnexpectedRecompositionsError. Reads the error in the prescribed
  order from docs/error-messages.md, matches against an 8-row signal
  → fix table (subset of perf-loop's decision tree, focused on triage
  rather than iteration), and recommends one fix. Escalates to
  dejavu-perf-loop when iteration is needed.

Cross-references between all four skills so the agent flows naturally:
onboarding → test-writer → (error-triage | perf-loop). README, CLAUDE.md,
and the docs site (getting-started.md, index.md, use-cases.md) updated to
list all four. CHANGELOG.md unreleased entry expanded.
last_commit_message:
Address self-review findings on the four skills

dejavu-test-writer:

- Augmentation rule swap now branches by factory. The previous "drop-in
  swap" instruction broke for tests using createComposeRule() (no Activity
  — used for mainClock control / pure-Compose modules). Replaced with a
  three-row table covering createAndroidComposeRule (drop-in to
  createRecompositionTrackingRule), createComposeRule (no public drop-in;
  migrate to runRecompositionTrackingUiTest OR keep the rule and call
  Dejavu.enable / Dejavu.disable manually in @Before / @After), and
  runComposeUiTest (drop-in to runRecompositionTrackingUiTest +
  setTrackedContent).

- Replaced the malformed grep example. The previous regex
  ("onNodeWithTag\(.<your-tag>.\)") had broken escapes that didn't match
  what was intended, and src/*Test* didn't glob in standard Android/KMP
  layouts. Replaced with a working invocation against the canonical test
  source set names.

- Added a one-paragraph intro to the Workflow section telling the agent
  which numbered steps apply to each path (new test vs augment).

- Step 5 (mid-test reset) example was using opaque tag names from the
  Dejavu demo (select_0_btn, select_all_btn, derived_banner). Replaced
  with generic setup_action / measured_action / target so a reader without
  the demo context can follow.

dejavu-onboarding:

- KMP smallest-test example used setTrackedContent { MyScreen() }, which
  assumed the user has a top-level wrapper composable. Changed to
  setTrackedContent { StaticTitle() } — calls the composable from step 5
  directly, matching the "smallest possible" claim.

- KMP gradle dependency snippet now shows BOTH forms: the Kotlin 2.0+
  accessor DSL (commonTest.dependencies { ... }) and the older
  val commonTest by getting form. Plenty of Kotlin 2.0+ projects haven't
  migrated their gradle scripts yet, so a single snippet was a copy-paste
  trap.

fix: ruff cleanup, type safety, frontend UX hardening, verifier self-test

Engineering review actions.

Backend — ruff/lint
  - `uvx ruff check --fix` resolved 128 issues (mostly I001 import-sort
    across 21 files + a couple W291 trailing-whitespace).
  - Manual fixes:
      * models/world.py + models/playthrough.py: moved `from app.models.base
        import Base` to the top so it's no longer an E402 module-level
        import after the helper definitions.
      * models/memory.py: `class MemoryType(str, Enum)` → `MemoryType(StrEnum)`
        per UP042.
      * engine/verifier.py: stripped a trailing-whitespace W291.
  - Added `E712` to pyproject.toml's ignore list. `Model.col == True` is the
    canonical SQLAlchemy filter idiom — `is True` returns a Python bool, not
    a SQL expression. 11 false-positives silenced.
  - Final `uvx ruff check` is clean.

Backend — self-test
  - tests/test_verifier.py: two new tests guarding the "silent verifier
    disabled" failure mode that the review flagged. One verifies that with
    no PM / no deaths / no location move every dimension short-circuits
    without an LLM call. The second loads PM with a known death + a
    narrative mentioning that character alive — asserts `dead_resurrection`
    is NOT in `skipped`, AND that the verifier either reached the LLM
    (llm_called=True) or recorded a setup error. Catches "verifier silently
    returned no violations" regressions.

    `DIRECTION_VARIANT: Record<string, BadgeVariant>` map; removed

    every consumer imports from there).

    `(data: Record<string, unknown>)`.

    and `detail` plus a `userMessage` getter that maps HTTP status to a
    UI-ready string (401 → key invalid, 404 → not found, 429 → rate
    limited, 5xx → server). ApiClient.fetch throws ApiError instead of
    a generic Error.

Resolves the core/.claude drift flagged in the earlier architecture
review. Investigation found .claude/ is not a personal sandbox — it's
this repo's own dogfood install target (plugin.json's install.target is
".claude/", and core/scripts/build-release.sh packages core/ into a zip
explicitly meant to be unzipped into a target project's .claude/, this
repo included). It had drifted badly: .claude/skills/ had only 402 of
core/'s 1990 skill dirs, several hooks/scripts/rules existed on only one
side, agents count differed by one.

Ran build-release.sh (which gates on a 100% hook-test pass — see the
separate hook-portability-fixes commit that unblocked it), then unzipped
the resulting pack over .claude/{agents,commands,config,docs,gates,hooks,
prompts,rules,scripts,skills,templates,tests}/ as a pure overlay (adds/
updates, does not delete). .claude/assistant/, .claude/state/, and
.claude/settings.json were excluded from the source zip already (not part
of build-release.sh's include list) and are confirmed untouched — that's
this repo's genuinely local/personal state, not build output.

Pre-existing files unique to .claude/ (a handful of hooks/rules/agents
core/ doesn't have) were intentionally left in place, not deleted, since
this pass didn't establish whether those are stray drift or deliberate
local additions — a separate decision, not blocking this resync.

Verified: bash .claude/tests/hooks/run-hook-tests.sh → 104/104 pass.

## 🌰 Summary

Shifts code quality enforcement from reactive (pre-commit hooks fail, CI fails) to proactive (agents validate before committing) by adding two new skills, mandating validation in `AGENTS.md`, and wiring pre-flight checks into submission and triage workflows.

## 📝 Details

- Add `validate-code` skill: instructs agents to run `nx affected --target=analyze-code --configuration=write/check` before declaring any task complete, with a quick-reference table of all covered tools
- Add `typescript-conventions` skill: converts `documentation/conventions/typescript.md` into an active skill that agents load when writing/modifying `.ts`/`.tsx` files (strict mode flags, explicit return types, `no-any`, naming conventions, import extensions)
- Update `AGENTS.md`: add a prominent "Code Quality & Validation" section with the universal mandate that every coding agent MUST run validate-code before completing any implementation task
- Update `submit-changes` skill: add Phase 0 pre-flight validation that must pass before any branch/commit operations begin
- Update `triage-submission` skill: add "Root Cause & Prevention" section that instructs agents to remind users to use validate-code proactively after fixing any pre-commit failure
- Update `triage-deployment` skill: same prevention reminder appended to the end of triage workflows

pnpm exec nx run monorepo:sync-agent-skills:check
pnpm exec nx run monorepo:analyze-code --configuration=check
```

refactor(conformance): ♻️ refactor modules and add command option routing (#82)

## 🌰 Summary

Refactored the `tools/conformance` tool from a static Nx generator plugin into a canonical NestJS command application using `nest-commander`. All generator templates are now dedicated command modules following the `nestjs-command-module` pattern, with a separate validator command module for conformance checking. The application includes interactive command selection via CLI prompts. Conformance validation is now properly wired into lint-staged and GitHub Actions CI/CD.

## 📝 Details

- **Generator Modules**: Migrated 9 Nx generators as individual command modules (jupyter-notebook-application, nestjs-command-application, nestjs-command-module, nestjs-dataloader-module, nestjs-graphql-application, nestjs-graphql-module, nestjs-service-file, nestjs-service-module, react-component)
- **Validator Module**: Created dedicated validator command module following `nestjs-command-module` template with Python validators organized in `modules/validator/python/` subdirectory
- **Logger Service**: Added canonical logger module matching `nestjs-service-module` and `nestjs-command-application` templates
- **Command Routing**: Implemented `@Option` decorator in main conformance-generator command with CLI prompt for interactive command selection via DiscoveryService
- **Conformance Validation Integration**: Wired `conformance:validate` command into lint-staged for pre-commit checks and GitHub Actions validate-conventions workflow for CI/CD validation
- **Dependency Fix**: Moved `@types/mdast` to devDependencies in lexico-ingestion (TypeScript-only, not runtime)
- **Code Organization**: Removed unused generator module wrapper, cleaned up dead code (repl.ts)

## 🧪 Testing

All validation targets pass:

```bash
# Run conformance validation (now used in lint-staged and CI)
nx run conformance:validate

# Run conformance tests  
nx run conformance:test

# Run all generators to verify they work
nx run conformance:start -- --command=nestjs-command-application
nx run conformance:start -- --command=validator
```

To test conformance validation locally when generator templates or instances change:
```bash
# Lint-staged will automatically run this on commit
pnpm exec nx run conformance:validate

# GitHub Actions runs this in validate-conventions.yml workflow

this repo's own dogfood install target (plugin.json's install.target is

explicitly meant to be unzipped into a target project's .claude/, this

the resulting pack over .claude/{agents,commands,config,docs,gates,hooks,
prompts,rules,scripts,skills,templates,tests}/ as a pure overlay (adds/
updates, does not delete). .claude/assistant/, .claude/state/, and
.claude/settings.json were excluded from the source zip already (not part
of build-release.sh's include list) and are confirmed untouched — that's
this repo's genuinely local/personal state, not build output.

Pre-existing files unique to .claude/ (a handful of hooks/rules/agents
core/ doesn't have) were intentionally left in place, not deleted, since
this pass didn't establish whether those are stray drift or deliberate
local additions — a separate decision, not blocking this resync.

first_commit_message:
perf: enable ISR on /watch/[slug] via generateStaticParams=[]

Root cause: Next.js 16 treats dynamic [slug] routes as fully dynamic by
default when no generateStaticParams is exported. The revalidate = 86400
was dead code — every watch page hit triggered a fresh PG query + full
render with no cache.

Evidence: responses carried "Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store"
and no x-nextjs-cache header. Build output showed /watch/[slug] as ƒ
(dynamic) instead of ● (static with ISR).

Fix: export generateStaticParams = async () => [] + dynamicParams = true.
This tells Next.js to pre-render zero params at build time (so Docker
builds without PG succeed) but cache on-demand renders for 86400s. After
the fix, /watch/[slug] is ● (SSG) and repeated hits serve from the ISR
cache in <10ms instead of re-querying PG every time.

Also added /audit/ and /.agents/ to .gitignore to exclude local skill
exploration artifacts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <<redacted>>

feat: decouple blocked state from the blocked-by dependency list

Split the single coupled `blocked-by: {refs, reason}` concept into two
orthogonal ones:

- `blocked` stays a manual state but now carries a free-form `block-reason`
  only (mirroring `closed`/`close-reason`). Leaving `blocked` clears it.
- `blocked-by` becomes an independent, status-agnostic list of canonical
  `<epic-id>/<n>` references to the tickets that block this one. It never
  gates or is cleared by a state change; a blocker must exist (its own state
  is irrelevant, cross-epic allowed) and cannot be the node itself.

Managed via a new node-only `ticket blocked-by (add|remove|set|clear|list)`
family that accepts `<n>` or `<epic-id>/<n>` and stores the canonical form.
`ticket status --blocked` now requires only `--reason`.

Output: `--json` `blocked-by` is now an array plus a `block-reason` scalar;
the list tag/summary field is `blocked-by` (dependency refs, shown in any
state).

Storage: format bumped to major 1 with a registered 0->1 migration that
splits the old map into the new list + block-reason.

Specs and the bundled skill are updated to match.

feat(022): bounded keypath section anchors; ratify 015-022 (#24)

* feat(022): bounded keypath section anchors for first-party structured config

Widen sections.rs so a { kind: section, file, anchor } unit can name a
bounded mapping keypath on the three structured-config shapes spec-spine
has a first-party reason to parse:

- workflow YAML (.github/workflows/*.yml): top-level keys, parent.child
  (on.merge_group, jobs.<name>), and jobs.<name>.<key>, plus the bare job
  alias for back-compat. The motivating ASI boundaries are permissions:
  (GITHUB_TOKEN scope) and on/on.merge_group (trigger + merge-queue).
- Cargo.toml: table keypaths to depth 4 via toml_edit spans, subtree-inclusive.
- package.json: object-member keypaths to depth 2 via a brace-depth scan.

Eligibility is a hard predicate (D1): foreign configs (deny.toml, Helm
values.yaml) never receive keypath treatment, so the gate never binds to a
schema spec-spine does not own. The anchor field is already a free string, so
this is permissive-additive: no frontmatter or JSON-schema edit, no schema
version bump (D2). Resolved keypaths carry a LineSpan, so their backing file
folds into the index content hash automatically (staleness, no new code).

Implements spec 022.

* chore(specs): flip 015-019 from draft to approved

These specs carry implementation: complete and their claimed units all
resolve in the codebase index (0 error diagnostics) with the full test
suite green, so the shipped behavior matches the spec text. Ratify them.

* chore(derived): regenerate registry and index

Reflects spec 022 (new), the 015-019 draft->approved flips, and the
keypath resolutions now backing spec 022's section units.

* fix(022): address review (block-scalar awareness, skip dotted-key tables)

Two latent issues found in adversarial review, both safe in the current
corpus but tightened to match spec intent:

- The workflow scanner now tracks YAML block scalars (`run: |` / `>`,
  including `- run: |` step items) and skips their literal content, so a
  stray `echo "permissions: ..."` line is never parsed as a mapping key.
- cargo_toml_sections skips dotted-key pseudo-tables (`version.workspace =
  true`), which toml_edit models as tables but are not [header]-delimited
  sections, so they are not addressable keypaths (\xc2\xa73.3). Implicit header
  tables (from a deeper [a.b.c]) are still resolved.

Adds regression tests for both.

* chore(022): flip to approved and regenerate derived

022 is implemented, adversarially reviewed, and verified (gate green); its
design decisions D1-D5 are resolved and recorded in the spec's section 6.
Ratify it. The corpus is now fully approved (23/23).

* chore: commit agent tooling (.claude/ agents, rules, skills) and AGENTS.md

CLAUDE.md and the /init protocol already reference .claude/rules/* and
AGENTS.md as checked-in, but they were never tracked. Commit the curated
cross-agent setup so a fresh clone has it. Per-agent learned memory
(.claude/agent-memory/) stays local (gitignored): it is session-generated
state, like the user's own out-of-repo memory dir.

chore(.claude): resync .claude/ from core/ via build-release.sh (item #4)

Resolves the core/.claude drift flagged in the earlier architecture
review. Investigation found .claude/ is not a personal sandbox — it's
this repo's own dogfood install target (plugin.json's install.target is
".claude/", and core/scripts/build-release.sh packages core/ into a zip
explicitly meant to be unzipped into a target project's .claude/, this
repo included). It had drifted badly: .claude/skills/ had only 402 of
core/'s 1990 skill dirs, several hooks/scripts/rules existed on only one
side, agents count differed by one.

Ran build-release.sh (which gates on a 100% hook-test pass — see the
separate hook-portability-fixes commit that unblocked it), then unzipped
the resulting pack over .claude/{agents,commands,config,docs,gates,hooks,
prompts,rules,scripts,skills,templates,tests}/ as a pure overlay (adds/
updates, does not delete). .claude/assistant/, .claude/state/, and
.claude/settings.json were excluded from the source zip already (not part
of build-release.sh's include list) and are confirmed untouched — that's
this repo's genuinely local/personal state, not build output.

Pre-existing files unique to .claude/ (a handful of hooks/rules/agents
core/ doesn't have) were intentionally left in place, not deleted, since
this pass didn't establish whether those are stray drift or deliberate
local additions — a separate decision, not blocking this resync.

Verified: bash .claude/tests/hooks/run-hook-tests.sh → 104/104 pass.

Fix/frontend docker missing public dir (#105)

* fix(frontend): ship empty public/ so the Docker build can copy it (#103)

The standalone Dockerfile runner stage does
`COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public`, but the template shipped no
`public/` directory. Next.js does not create one when there are no static
assets, so `make dev-frontend` failed with:

    failed to compute cache key: "/app/public": not found

Add `frontend/public/.gitkeep` so the directory always exists in the build
context. It is not matched by .dockerignore/.gitignore and the backend-only
empty-dir cleanup in the post-gen hook leaves it untouched.

first_commit_message:
Team-relative ring + pit planner, flag override, chart fixes, session rollover

Team dashboard gets its own Track Position card (the shared table ring
is disabled there via TimingTable's new ring prop):
- Karts colored relative to the followed driver: red = more laps
  completed, blue = fewer, green = you; legend adapts.
- Pit-stop planner: a seconds input (persisted per browser) draws a
  dashed rejoin marker on the ring at (current fraction + pit time /
  pace) with a "+N L" label when the stop spans whole laps — for
  timing stops to avoid rejoining in traffic. Pace = mean of non-pit
  laps, falling back to the last lap.
- Clicking a kart on the ring opens an info panel relative to your
  driver: delta laps, their/your last and best, pit state, and the
  estimated on-track gap in seconds (shortest arc distance x pace).

Race Control can override the session flag (Track/Green/Yellow/Red/
Finish) for organizers without track-system access: EventState keeps
a flag_override applied to snapshots and driver views (source state
untouched), POST /e/{slot}/api/admin/flag sets/clears it with an
immediate broadcast, and dashboards follow within a second.

Gap-to-leader chart rebuilt on crossing wall times: gap at lap N is
own ts(N) minus leader ts(N) (+ = behind). The old cumulative-sum
approach was off by whole laps whenever series' histories started on
different lap numbers. Lap history entries now expose ts via
/api/laps. Both chart legends are click-to-toggle per line.

Session rollover: when the venue starts a new session (run name
changes or a quorum of karts' lap counts regress), EventState clears
lap history, pit/stint bookkeeping and session best so charts and
stats restart immediately instead of freezing until a manual
reconnect. Single-kart glitches don't trigger it.

Adds .claude/skills/werace-dev — the project development guide
(architecture map, verified protocol facts, workflows, checklists)
to keep updated as the project evolves.

copier sourcing pre-generated assets from plugins/spectre-codex/. This

npm-packed artifact self-sufficient for user-scope installs in any

- Add scripts/sync-codex.cjs + translators that regenerate the Codex tree

  Skill() shims so canonical workflow content lives in one place.
- Migrate hook scripts from CommonJS (.cjs) to ESM (.mjs) and drop the
  PreCompact hook. SessionStart now wires three hooks (bootstrap,
  handoff-resume, load-knowledge) that resolve plugin root from script
  path rather than CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, so they run from any cwd.
- Knowledge injection writes into the managed AGENTS.override.md
  spectre-knowledge block instead of emitting hookSpecificOutput
  additionalContext, keeping continuity outside hook JSON.
- Rewrite src/lib/install.js as a copier; src/lib/config.js merges
  generated hooks.json into Codex hooks.json while preserving unrelated
  hooks; src/lib/doctor.js verifies the new hook layout and renames the
  feature flag from codex_hooks to hooks.
- Add src/pack.test.js to assert the packed npm artifact contains no
  file:// leakage and installs from the generated tree.

refactor(client): IPv4-literal vite proxy targets + /ws observability (Refs #1211) (#1218)

* refactor(client): make vite proxy targets IPv4-literal, add /ws observability

Docker dev stack's backend binds IPv4-only, so `localhost` resolving to
::1 first requires an implicit HTTP fallback that the /ws proxy path
doesn't get. Using 127.0.0.1 literals removes that ambiguity for both
/api and /ws, giving deterministic behavior in Docker and non-Docker
dev environments alike.

Also add permanent error/open/close logging to the /ws proxy so a
future connection failure surfaces a signal instead of a silent hang.

This does not fix the /ws hang reported in #1211 (root cause remains
open, deferred per issue comment) — it ships only the parts of that
investigation with standalone hygiene/observability value. Documents
the current Docker /ws limitation in dev-environment-quirks skill.

Refs #1211

* fix(client): add missing proxyReqWs log to /ws proxy instrumentation

Architect review caught the omission: proxyReqWs is the only signal
that distinguishes "vite never dispatched the upgrade" from "vite
dispatched it but the connection stalled downstream" -- exactly the
ambiguity that cost a full investigation round on #1211. Without it,
a future debugger re-investigating this hang would have to redo that
isolation step from scratch.

Refs #1211

refactor: rename frontend tier to reverse-proxy (ADR-032)

Part 3 of the three-tier rename per ADR-032 §Decision outcome —
`frontend/` → `reverse-proxy/`. The nginx role / config / SPA-static-
serve behavior is unchanged; this rename makes the topology name match
what the tier actually does (nginx reverse-proxy + cache + static), per
the four-routing-rules + gzip + DNS-late-binding surface enumerated in
ADR-031.

Surface changes:
- Directory: `frontend/` → `reverse-proxy/`
- npm package: `dashboard-chat-frontend` → `dashboard-chat-reverse-proxy`
- Container name: `dashboard-frontend` → `dashboard-reverse-proxy`
- Compose service name: `frontend:` → `reverse-proxy:`
- Docker image: `dashboard-chat/frontend:bazel` → `dashboard-chat/reverse-proxy:bazel`
- Bazel labels: `//frontend:...` → `//reverse-proxy:...`
- Workspace member (root package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml): `frontend` → `reverse-proxy`
- CI workflow job: `test-frontend` → `test-reverse-proxy`
- npm scripts: `test:frontend`/`lint:frontend` → `test:reverse-proxy`/`lint:reverse-proxy`
- agent/tsconfig.json path alias: `frontend/src/lib/raqb` → `reverse-proxy/src/lib/raqb`
- e2e/run-e2e.sh: `bazel-bin/frontend/image_tar.sh` → `bazel-bin/reverse-proxy/...`
- system prompts + skill docs referencing `@frontend/...` paths

Things deliberately NOT renamed:
- Generic prose mentions of "the frontend" / "frontend tier" / "frontend
  component" — these are the natural English word for the UI tier role,
  which is unchanged (nginx + Vue SPA + four routing rules).
- The `<redacted>` plugin name in
  .claude/settings.json (external plugin namespace).

against its own schemas inside the render loop (zero extra renders);
the stale post-golden block that re-validated the canonical render is
removed. Live docs (skills, vault) updated to reflect the closed gap.

* build: pin datreeio CRDs-catalog to commit SHA in lint gate

Closes helm-factory-t7u. CRD_CATALOG_REF pins schema downloads to
34cef0f (2026-07-11); bump deliberately when new CRD schemas are needed.

* fix: fail closed when certificate and tlsSelfSigned are both enabled

Closes helm-factory-866. Both generators target the <fullname>-tls
Secret; enabling both now fails at render time with a prescriptive
message, backed by a negative test in the lint gate.

* feat: rotate tlsSelfSigned cert near expiry via not-after annotation

Closes helm-factory-665. Generation stamps platform/tls-not-after
(RFC3339, computed from validityDays — sprig cannot parse x509);
lookup-reuse is skipped within the new tlsSelfSigned.renewBeforeDays
window (default 30). Legacy Secrets without the annotation regenerate
once. Golden updated: single hunk, the redacted annotation line.

* chore(beads): sync issue log for handover session

Closes helm-factory-1ay, -uaw, -t7u, -866, -665.

* docs(handover): refresh operating layer for n-2 window and moved anchors

Main tightened the K8s support window to 1.34-1.36 and shifted line
numbers in _capabilities.tpl and lint-library.sh. Skills, manual, and
vault re-anchored and re-ranged against the rebased tree; the
k8s-version-bump touch list rewritten for the n-2 policy.

* fix: reconcile kubeconform gate with vendored schemas after rebase

Rebasing onto #23 (vendored schemas) left two artifacts of the CDN era:
the per-version kubeconform call still passed -cache "$KUBECONFORM_CACHE",
whose definition went away with the CDN block — an unbound variable under
set -u — and it still wrapped the call in a retry/backoff loop for transient
jsdelivr 403s. Schema fetches are now hermetic reads from tests/schemas/, so
there is nothing to rate-limit and nothing to retry; a kubeconform failure is
now always a real validation failure and fails on the first attempt.

Also drops the CHANGELOG entry for CRD_CATALOG_REF: pinning the datreeio
catalog to a commit SHA existed to stop upstream from silently altering the
gate, which vendoring subsumes entirely. That commit's diff is now empty.

first_commit_message:
fix(settings): self-target lockout (#397/#403) + /release skill + env hardening (#437)

* fix(settings): close self-deletion lockout in Settings → Users (#397, #403)

Settings → Users rendered a Remove button next to the currently
authenticated operator's own row, and DELETE /api/settings/users/:name
did not check the URL target against the caller's session. Confirming
the hx-confirm dialog dropped the only usable credential on the
running server, locking every operator out until the process was
restarted against its on-disk config.

Fix lands both halves because a hand-crafted HTTP DELETE bypasses the
dashboard:

- render_users_fragment() now takes the caller's session username and
  emits an italicised "Current user" badge (no button, no hx-delete)
  for the matching row. Every call site
  (GET /fragments/settings/users, POST /api/settings/users, DELETE
  /api/settings/users/:name) resolves the session via auth_fn_ and
  threads the name through.

- The DELETE handler resolves session = auth_fn_(req, res) after the
  admin_fn_ gate passes, compares session->username against the URL-
  captured target, and rejects matches with HTTP 403 + a "Cannot
  delete your own account" toast HX-Trigger. The rejected attempt is
  logged at warn level so operators chasing a lockout incident can see
  it in the server log.

User-manual entry rewritten to document the guard and tell operators
how to remove the account they are signed in as (create a second
admin, log out, sign in as the second admin, delete the original).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <<redacted>>

* test(server): add settings_routes Users HTTP coverage for #397/#403

First test file for the Settings routes layer. Stands up a real
httplib::Server on a random port with SettingsRoutes bound to an
AuthManager seeded with two accounts (admin + bob), mocks the
auth_fn/admin_fn/perm_fn/audit_fn callbacks, and exercises the full
HTTP surface with httplib::Client.

Five cases:

- DELETE /api/settings/users/<self> as admin returns 403 with the
  "Cannot delete your own account" toast HX-Trigger; the account
  remains in AuthManager::list_users() afterwards (#397 handler
  guard, observable behaviour).
- DELETE /api/settings/users/<other> as admin still returns 200 and
  the account is removed (no regression on the legitimate path).
- DELETE /api/settings/users/<self> as a non-admin is rejected by the
  admin_fn_ gate before the self-delete guard runs, so non-admins
  cannot infer the guard via response shape.
- GET /fragments/settings/users renders no
  hx-delete="/api/settings/users/admin" attribute for the self row,
  still emits hx-delete for every other row, and renders the
  "Current user" badge in its place (#403 UI guard).
- POST /api/settings/users success path re-renders the fragment with
  the same self-row guard applied (regression cover for the call-site
  threading of self_name through render_users_fragment()).

Harness pattern mirrors test_rest_api_tokens.cpp — random port,
unique_temp_path() fixture root, mock session callbacks read from
mutable harness fields so individual tests can switch perspective
without rebuilding the server. Future Settings-routes regression
coverage has a template to reuse.

Wired into tests/meson.build under the server suite.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <<redacted>>

* fix(settings): close sibling self-demotion lockout + audit chain (#397/ca-B1)

Hardening round on top of 0a87473 self-deletion fix, addressing
governance Gate 4-6 BLOCKING findings.

allowed an admin to demote themselves to role=user via a self-

that 0a87473 closed. Add a self-demotion guard that rejects with
HTTP 403 + "Cannot change your own role" toast when
(username == session->username && new_role != session->role).
Self-password-change (same role) is explicitly allowed.

chore(changelog): move unreleased entries to per-PR fragment files (changelog.d/)

Every PR that edited CHANGELOG.md's [Unreleased] section conflicted with
whichever PR merged first, and the conflict-resolution push voided the PR's

first_commit_message:
Add triage skill for unpack_forward_output FE failures (#4549)

> [!NOTE]
> This PR complements
[tenstorrent/tt-forge-models#637](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-forge-models/pull/637),
which contains the model-side fixes (registry handlers + per-loader
overrides) produced by running this skill. The YAML status updates here
reflect the new failure stages observed once those fixes are in.

### Ticket
Refs: [#4293](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-xla/issues/4293) (kept
open — this is only the first pattern of FE failures being triaged).

### Problem description
A large block of training tests was stuck at \`FAILED_FE_COMPILATION\`
with reason:

> \`tt-forge-models doesn't implement unpack_forward_output for this
model.\`

Triaging these by hand is mechanical: run the model on CPU, inspect the
forward output structure, then either register the output class in
\`training_utils.py\` or write a per-loader \`unpack_forward_output\`
override. Repeated dozens of times across yolov6, yolov9, retinanet,
fpn, swin, dpr, segformer, mgp_str, yolos, opt, albert, bert, bge_m3,
distilbert, etc.

### What's changed
- **New Claude Code skill
\`.claude/skills/triage-unpack-forward-output/SKILL.md\`** that handles
exactly one failure pattern (the one above), invoked with a YAML key or
\`model_info.name\`. The skill:
1. Resolves the test name to a YAML entry + loader path. The YAML
\`reason:\` is read for context but is not authoritative — Step 3 (CPU
triage) is the real gate, since reasons can be stale.
2. Runs the model on CPU via the bundled
\`scripts/triage_forward_output.py\` and prints the forward output
structure, gathers model docs, and decides between a registry entry vs a
per-loader override (rule of thumb: registry for HuggingFace
\`ModelOutput\` subclasses with a single loss-relevant attr; override
for bare \`list\`/\`tuple\`/\`dict\` outputs, structural transforms, or
when a registry entry exists but is wrong — i.e. its registered
attribute is itself a tuple/list/dict).
3. Writes the fix in tt-forge-models, then verifies with \`pytest
--force-run --runxfail --junitxml=<path>\` to bypass the current YAML
status and capture the real outcome. The YAML is updated once, after
observing the real outcome.
4. When the registry path is chosen, re-checks every other model that
returns the same output class — registry is global by class name, so the
fix affects all of them and the YAML must reflect that.
- **YAML updates** in
\`tests/runner/test_config/torch/test_config_training_single_device.yaml\`
reflecting the new failure stages observed after the companion
tt-forge-models PR is in: most entries advance from
\`FAILED_FE_COMPILATION\` to \`INCORRECT_RESULT\` (PCC drops, recorded
as \`EXPECTED_PASSING\` + \`assert_pcc: false\`),
\`FAILED_TTMLIR_COMPILATION\` (e.g. \`ElementsAttr::getValues
UNREACHABLE\` for retinanet/yolov9/fpn ResNet50), or \`FAILED_RUNTIME\`
(segformer, swinv2, mgp_str CB page sizing). A few unrelated environment
errors are also surfaced now that FE compilation no longer hides them
(\`'_has_torch_function' already has a docstring\`,
\`is_torch_fx_available\`, MapTR boolean-tensor ambiguity).

### Checklist
- [x] New/Existing tests provide coverage for changes — the affected
training tests are the ones whose YAML statuses are updated; each was
re-run as part of the skill's verification step.

first_commit_message:
feat(catalog-sync): single end-to-end onsen update pipeline

Aggregate the scattered update tools behind one orchestrator skill —
`catalog-sync` — so "update the onsen information" has a single entry point
that runs detect → publish → retire/mint → advance-baseline, gating every
write. It composes the focused tools (catalog-diff, recurate-hours, the
publisher scripts) rather than replacing them.

New driver `.claude/skills/catalog-sync/catalog_sync.py` (stdlib, offline by
default) supplies the missing mechanical glue:
- `status`  — offline coverage snapshot (baseline / id-map / curated).
- `sample`  — scrape-health preflight.
- `detect`  — ONE scrape → changelog report + a staging scrape
  (data/snapshot.next.json) + triage routing each change to its phase.
- `mint`    — assign kyuhachiId(s) for new onsens (this repo owns ids).
- `promote` — advance the previously-FROZEN snapshot.db baseline from the
  staging scrape (UPDATE/INSERT, optional --prune). Fixes the long-standing
  gap where every diff was "vs the original scrape" instead of "since last
  update". Gated by --commit; idempotent.

Clarify schedule ownership: apply.py no longer derives a regex

first_commit_message:
Add zellij-agent-manager skill (#13)

Sibling of the existing `tmux-agent-manager` skill, for users running
their Claude Code agents under [Zellij](https://zellij.dev) instead of
tmux.

Originally proposed as shader-slang/slang#11187; closing that PR in
favor of landing here, mirroring the path `tmux-agent-manager` took
(shader-slang/slang#11184 → this repo).

## Summary

- Same command surface as the tmux variant: `status`, `send <session>
<message>`, `monitor [interval]`, `new <issue_or_prompt>`.
- Same state-detection (idle / working / needs_approval /
pending_message / stuck) and ETA heuristics — those match Claude Code's
pane output, not the multiplexer, so they port verbatim.
- Multiplexer primitives swapped one-for-one:
  - `list-sessions -s -n` for `tmux list-sessions`
  - `action list-panes --json` for `tmux list-panes -a -F`
  - `action dump-screen -p <pid>` for `tmux capture-pane`
- `action write-chars` + `action send-keys "Enter"` for `tmux
load-buffer` / `paste-buffer`
  - `attach -b` (create-background) for `tmux new-session -d`
- Pane targeting uses a small Python helper. Zellij uses opaque numeric
pane IDs (not tmux-style `SESSION:W.P`), so the helper extracts the
first non-plugin pane in tab 0 from `list-panes --json` and emits
`terminal_<id>`. The helper returns non-zero on no-pane, and every
caller checks the exit status so a missing pane surfaces immediately.
- Linux/macOS only; refuses to run on Windows (Zellij has no first-class
Windows story).

The README "General developer skills" table gets a new row next to
`tmux-agent-manager`. The skill is picked up automatically by the
existing `install.sh` / `install.ps1` directory discovery; no installer
changes needed.

## Testing

Smoke-tested locally against Zellij 0.44.3:

- `zellij attach -b test-zam` → session created and listed by `zellij
list-sessions -s -n`.
- `zellij --session test-zam action list-panes --json` → emits the
documented flat-array JSON shape; helper extracts `terminal_0`.
- `zellij --session test-zam action write-chars -p terminal_0 -- "echo
hello"` + `send-keys "Enter"` → `dump-screen` shows the echoed output as
expected.

End-to-end exercise from a Claude Code session (status / send / monitor
/ new) was done while iterating on shader-slang/slang#11187.

feat(init-gate): add agent-files bootstrap gate for CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md

Purpose: the init gates enforced project-config + reference-doc freshness
but never guarded the two most foundational artifacts — the root
agent-instruction files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md). A copied .claude install
could run with no root instructions, or with a stale hand-written file
lacking the portable framework guides, and nothing flagged it. This adds a
bootstrap gate that detects missing OR incomplete root files and routes the
AI to the generator skills.

What changed:
- New lib lib/agent-files-state.cjs — single source of truth for "is a root
  agent file missing/incomplete and what fixes it". Pure detection (no
  process.exit), consumed by both gates below.
- New PreToolUse/Skill hook agent-files-skill-gate.cjs — blocks non-meta
  skill calls when a root file needs attention; allowlists meta + the
  fixing routes (claude-md-init, codex-sync, project-config, scan-*, ...).
- init-prompt-gate.cjs — handleAgentFilesGate wired into the config-populated
  fast path, ahead of the staleness/graph gates; allowlist extended with the
  claude-md-init and codex-sync routes.
- generate-claude-md.cjs — stamps a CK:UNIVERSAL-GUIDES sentinel and
  back-fills drifted portable-guide sections into marker-managed files.
- project-config-schema.cjs — new portability.requireUniversalGuides opt-out;
  ck-paths.cjs — new .agent-files-dismissed flag; settings.json registers the
  new Skill hook; 904-line agent-files-gate.test.cjs suite.
- Skill-doc sweep across scan-*/workflow-*/understand/commit/codex-sync and
  the .agents mirror; codex context + hooks.json mirror; inventory count
  reconcile (CLAUDE.md, SKILLS.yaml, docs/README.md, structure reference);
  lessons.md.

How it works / why this way:
- Two-gate design: UserPromptSubmit catches it at prompt time, PreToolUse/Skill
  catches the "skill fired before bootstrap" path. Both share one dismiss flag
  so "skip init" silences the whole nag for 24h and the Skill gate never nags
  per call.
- Gate is dormant unless hasProjectContent() AND config is populated:
  claude-md-init reads docs/project-config.json to generate CLAUDE.md, so
  offering it earlier would produce a meaningless file; config enforcement
  stays owned by init-prompt-gate. Agent-files runs FIRST in the fast path
  because root instructions are the most foundational artifact.
- "Complete" check is the sentinel-or-anchors contract: a current/newer
  CK:UNIVERSAL-GUIDES sentinel wins, else every static portable-guide heading
  must be present (covers legacy/hand-written-complete files). The sentinel is
  a content-presence promise — the generator stamps it ONLY when the guides are
  actually in the file and strips it when absent, so the gate can never be
  fooled into reading a project-only file as complete. UNIVERSAL_GUIDES_VERSION,
  SENTINEL_RE, and REQUIRED_ANCHORS are kept in lockstep across the lib and the
  generator by a sync test.
- All fs reads fail-open (unreadable/unparseable -> allow) so an unexpected
  error never traps the user behind the gate.

description: Detect and resolve un-managed (out-of-band) changes to this dotfiles repo's `shell-startup` script — the kind a tool installer makes by writing into ~/.bashrc / ~/.bash_profile, which symlink to `shell-startup` (e.g. the grok/xAI CLI installer re-adding its PATH+completion block). Compares `shell-startup` against a committed `shell-startup.md5` checksum; on drift, shows what changed since the last blessed state and offers to approve, restore, relocate the stray block into a proper module/wrapper, or defer. Use during push-pr's first half (before commit) and at merge-finalization, or whenever you suspect `shell-startup` was modified outside the repo's own edits.
first_commit_message:
feat(shell-startup): relocate grok block + add md5 drift guard (#154)

* feat(shell-startup): relocate grok installer block to its own module

The grok (xAI) CLI installer writes its PATH + bash-completion block into
~/.bashrc, which symlinks to shell-startup, so the block landed at the end
of shell-startup (after Cleanup). Move it to a guarded
config/shell-startup/grok module like every other tool integration.

The installer's config-file target is hardcoded to ~/.bashrc with no
override (GROK_BIN_DIR only relocates the binaries), so a reinstall will
re-add the block to shell-startup; that limitation is recorded as an ICEBOX
note in the module, and the follow-up md5 drift guard detects the re-add.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <<redacted>>

* feat(shell-startup): add md5 drift guard for out-of-band changes

shell-startup is what ~/.bash_profile and ~/.bashrc symlink to, so any tool
installer that "adds itself to your shell profile" (the grok CLI being the
known case) writes into shell-startup without going through git or the
agent. Add a tripwire so that drift is caught and resolved deliberately:

- shell-startup.md5: a committed checksum baseline at the repo root.
- shell-startup-guard skill (.claude/skills/): check -> diff-since-last-
  blessed -> approve / restore / relocate / defer. The diff is taken against
  shell-startup's content at the last commit that touched shell-startup.md5
  (the two move in lockstep), so it captures all drift accumulated since.
- md5-guard.py PostToolUse hook: auto-regenerates a git-tracked <name>.md5
  sibling after the agent edits its file, so the agent's own edits stay
  blessed and only un-managed changes look like drift. Dormant where no such
  sibling exists, so it is safe as global config.

Add problem-analyser and user-story-writer agents to cadre

Introduce two focused requirements agents. `problem-analyser` handles
vague or incomplete requests: it applies Impact Mapping, contradiction
analysis, NFR probing, and a premortem to produce a confidence-scored
problem analysis before any story writing begins. `user-story-writer`
takes a clear problem analysis and applies INVEST, Elephant Carpaccio,
SPIDR splitting, and Story Mapping to produce granular, independently
deployable stories with Given/When/Then acceptance criteria.

feat(history): ref-scoped log — browse & cherry-pick from unmerged refs (#40)

GitBackend::log/log_filtered gain an optional refspec walk start (None =
HEAD, any revspec otherwise; InvalidRef when unresolvable). get_log /
get_log_filtered commands accept an optional refspec param. useRepoStore
gains logRef + setLogRef; refreshAll and backend searches stay scoped to
the browsed ref (falling back to HEAD if it vanishes). The History
toolbar gets a ref selector (HEAD + local branches), so unmerged-branch
commits become viewable and cherry-pickable via the detail action row.
Unskips the cherry-pick e2e test blocked on this.

Why: every commit surface read the same HEAD-only log array, so commits
on unmerged branches could never be displayed or cherry-picked in-app.
Scoping the single shared array (rather than adding a second list) gives
every consumer — History, palette pickers, context menus — the browsed
ref's commits for free.

feat(ios): medical citations per section + tighten default thresholds (#157)

* build(ios): tighten High and Critical default glucose thresholds

High: 14.0 → 13.9 mmol/L (250 mg/dL) — directly citable from the ADA
and ISPAD 2022 CGM guideline that less than 5% of readings should exceed
this value (TAR >13.9 mmol/L <5%).

Critical: 20.0 → 16.7 mmol/L (300 mg/dL) — conventional severe
hyperglycaemia reference point; DKA risk territory where ketone testing
is strongly recommended.

Tightening Critical from 20.0 to 16.7 catches a wider range of severe
highs as undismissable — more protective for children. Moving from 20.0
to 16.7 still leaves a comfortable gap above the High threshold (13.9)
so normal post-meal highs are not locked out.

Both values are now directly defensible in the MedicalInfoView citations
added in the follow-up commit (App Store Review guideline 1.4.1).

Updates all comments and doc strings that referenced the old values.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <<redacted>>

* feat(ios): change High and Critical glucose slider step to 0.1 mmol/L

Previously 0.5 mmol/L, which meant the new defaults (13.9 and 16.7)
were not native slider positions — users dragging away from the default
would snap to 13.5/14.0 or 16.5/17.0 instead.

With step 0.1 (matching the existing Low threshold slider), 13.9 and
16.7 are exact slider positions. The mg/dL step stays at 5 since
250 and 300 mg/dL are already multiples of 5.

criticalStep inherits from highStep so no separate change needed there.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <<redacted>>

* feat(ios): restructure MedicalInfoView with per-section citations

Addresses Apple App Store Review guideline 1.4.1 rejection:
"include citations of the sources of the recommendations or information,
such as links to those sources; citations should be easy for the user
to find."

Changes:

- Section 2 (Where Your Data Comes From): add Link() rows for Apple
  Health, Nightscout, and EasyView by Medtrum so users can learn about
  each data source.

- Section 3 (About Thresholds): update text to name the new defaults
  explicitly (4.0 / 13.9 / 16.7 mmol/L) and explain each threshold's
  basis. Add Sources sub-section with seven Link() rows: four ADA pages
  (Low Blood Glucose, Hyperglycemia, Blood Sugar Targets, Managing
  Ketones), ISPAD 2022 Guidelines, Diabetes Fonds NL, and DVN.

- Section 4 (Glucose Units — new): explain the mmol/L ↔ mg/dL
  conversion formula (× 18.018, based on glucose molecular weight
  180.18 g/mol) and link to the ADA targets page which lists values in
  both units.

- Section 5 (About Check-in Actions — new): explain that defaults are
  reminders not prescriptions, describe the 15-15 rule for low glucose
  and correction steps for high/critical glucose, link to ADA hypo and
  hyper pages plus Diabetes Fonds NL.

All new string keys provided in both EN and NL. International source
labels kept in English (official names); Dutch sources labelled in
Dutch. The "Sources" sub-section header is shared across sections.
