chore(.claude): resync .claude/ from core/ via build-release.sh (item #4)

Resolves the core/.claude drift flagged in the earlier architecture
review. Investigation found .claude/ is not a personal sandbox — it's
this repo's own dogfood install target (plugin.json's install.target is
".claude/", and core/scripts/build-release.sh packages core/ into a zip
explicitly meant to be unzipped into a target project's .claude/, this
repo included). It had drifted badly: .claude/skills/ had only 402 of
core/'s 1990 skill dirs, several hooks/scripts/rules existed on only one
side, agents count differed by one.

Ran build-release.sh (which gates on a 100% hook-test pass — see the
separate hook-portability-fixes commit that unblocked it), then unzipped
the resulting pack over .claude/{agents,commands,config,docs,gates,hooks,
prompts,rules,scripts,skills,templates,tests}/ as a pure overlay (adds/
updates, does not delete). .claude/assistant/, .claude/state/, and
.claude/settings.json were excluded from the source zip already (not part
of build-release.sh's include list) and are confirmed untouched — that's
this repo's genuinely local/personal state, not build output.

Pre-existing files unique to .claude/ (a handful of hooks/rules/agents
core/ doesn't have) were intentionally left in place, not deleted, since
this pass didn't establish whether those are stray drift or deliberate
local additions — a separate decision, not blocking this resync.

Verified: bash .claude/tests/hooks/run-hook-tests.sh → 104/104 pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <<redacted>>

rewrites [[paper-foo]] to [[foo]] (and [[paper-foo|label]] to
[[foo|label]]) only when the unresolved target starts with paper-, the
audit reports exactly one suggestion, and that suggestion is the
canonical prefix-stripped slug on the manifest. Defaults to dry-run;

code spans (placeholder samples like `[[slug]]` and `[[paper-foo]]`

  refused (all-inline-code)   : 6

The remaining 56 unresolved targets are honest curation debt -- 39 have
no canonical-slug suggestion at all, 17 have a single suggestion the
repair pass refused for safety (not a paper-prefix strip, e.g.
separator drift, or every occurrence sits inside inline-code). Closing
them is a content-level question rather than a mechanical one and is
left for follow-up PRs.

first_commit_message:
refactor: template-scoped KG extraction + magic-string elimination + KG-backed timeline ETL

## Knowledge graph

- Split infobox classification into hand-curated FieldSemantics (label → semantic/
  relationship/property) intersected with auto-generated TemplateFields at lookup
  time via InfoboxDefinitionRegistry. Adds LabelDefinition/TemporalFieldDefinition/
  InfoboxDefinition and DefaultLabelSelector.
- Era.Years now parses into era.start/end/point TemporalFacets via a range-aware
  parser on TemporalFieldDefinition.IsRange (ParseAllGalacticYears).
- GraphNode.StartYear/EndYear envelope picks up era facets automatically.
- New KGAnalyticsToolkit with describe_entity_schema, find_by_lifecycle_transition,
  count_lifecycle_transitions, list_labels_by_category, get_relationships_by_category.
- GraphRAGToolkit.GetEntityRelationships now bidirectional.

## Magic-string elimination

- New constants classes in Models: KgNodeTypes, KgLabels, InfoboxFieldLabels,
  MongoFields, PageBsonFields, InfoboxBsonFields, GraphNodeBsonFields,
  RelationshipEdgeBsonFields, TimelineEventBsonFields, TemporalFacetBsonFields,
  ArticleChunkBsonFields. FactionColorPalette and GalacticRegions deduped from
  GalaxyMapETLService + TerritoryInferenceService.
- Misplaced DTOs (EdgeDto, SemanticSearchResult) moved from Services into Models.
- ~250 BSON field literals + ~50 node type/label literals replaced across
  Services/ApiService/Admin.

## KG-backed timeline ETL

- New KgTimelineBuilderService reads kg.nodes (galactic facets only), joins
  raw.pages for the info-panel Properties payload, writes denormalised
  TimelineEvent rows to timeline.{Template} collections. Replaces the legacy
  InfoboxToEventsTransformer path (kept behind a separate admin endpoint for
  side-by-side comparison). Calendar-aware by construction: real-world publication
  years no longer pollute the galactic timeline.
- Admin endpoint POST /api/admin/mongo/create-timeline-events-from-kg and
  matching AppHost HTTP command "3a-KG. Build Timeline Events (from KG)".

## Galaxy map + timeline page fixes

- Added UseResponseCaching middleware required by [ResponseCache(VaryByQueryKeys)]
  on GalaxyMapUnifiedController (was throwing InvalidOperationException at
  request time).
- Fixed three raw-BSON (int)Continuity filters in GalaxyEventsService and
  TimelineService that didn't match the string representation written by the
  global EnumRepresentationConvention. Density pipeline also now filters by
  continuity.
- Fixed GalaxyMapReadService $addFields pipeline using nameof(Eras) instead of
  the [BsonElement("eras")] lowercase name — was writing a duplicate "Eras"
  field and crashing deserialisation.
- /Timeline/eras endpoint now takes [FromQuery] Continuity? and reloads on
  global filter change; EventTimeline.razor prunes stale era selections.
- Era chip bar on galaxy map removed hardcoded .Take(8) (was dropping Imperial,
  New Republic, Era of war from Canon view) — now horizontally scrollable.
- Faction legend overlay bumped bottom: 80px → 140px to clear the timeline bar.
- KnowledgeGraphQueryService.GetAllEdgesForEntityAsync for bidirectional entity
  edge display with label reverse resolution.
- FindByLifecycleTransitionAsync + CountLifecycleTransitionsAsync service methods.
- Fixed FindByLifecycleTransitionAsync projection that was aliasing
  GraphNode.PageId as "\$pageId" (broken because [BsonId] maps to _id).
- Fixed pre-existing CS8601 null-ref warning in QueryGraphAsync.

## Other

- Design docs 001-temporal-facets, 002-edge-quality, 003-galaxy-map-temporal
  updated with post-refactor notes.
- Skills reorganised from .claude/skills/ → .agents/skills/; added atlas-stream-
  processing, likec4-dsl, dotnet-best-practices, microsoft-agent-framework,
  mongodb-*, mudblazor, claude-d3js-skill.
- eng/scripts/generate-template-fields.mongodb.js generator for the
  auto-generated TemplateFields.g.cs whitelist.

first_commit_message:
Initial commit: agent-driven workbench for infrastructure project finance

Multi-agent system for monitoring infrastructure debt: borrower-submission
ingestion, covenant testing, notice drafting, sensitivity analysis, and
portfolio rollup. Designed for a CIB-style monitoring desk.

What's included:

  fmcli/            Python CLI for deterministic spreadsheet ops, with
                    auto-snapshot on every mutation, append-only audit
                    trail, and Python-side recalc (no Excel/LibreOffice
                    dependency).
  .claude/agents/   Seven specialist subagents — orchestrator, model
                    updater, output extractor, covenant checker, notice
                    drafter, reconciler, audit logger.
  .claude/skills/   Twelve skills covering the day-to-day: update-model,
                    extract-outputs, draft-notice, covenant-check,
                    new-drawdown, quarterly-monitoring, sensitivity-
                    analysis, portfolio-rollup, reconcile-versions,
                    amendment-impact, annual-review, rate-reset,
                    backup-restore, deal-onboarding.
  .claude/commands/ Slash commands for the common end-to-end plays.
  data/templates/   Seven Jinja2 notice templates: drawdown confirmation,
                    quarterly monitoring, covenant breach, interest
                    payment, rate reset, waiver acknowledgement, annual
                    review.
  data/deals/       Two sample deals with realistic project finance
                    models — Highway 407 East Extension (availability-
                    payment P3) and Oneida Energy Storage (battery
                    storage senior debt).

Highway 407 baseline is intentionally on the watchlist; running the
included borrower submission tips it into a covenant breach to
demonstrate the breach-notice workflow.

description: Phase 4 of LLM deployment — apply the shared optimization skillset to a Phase-3-correct prefill pipeline (multi-launch merge, BO pre-loading + intermediate buffer reuse, seq-first layout). Thin orchestrator that dispatches `opt-merge-multi-launch-kernels`, `opt-buffer-object-reuse`, and `opt-layout-alignment`. first_commit_message:
[.claude/skills] Agent skill system for end-to-end LLM deployment on NPU2 (#1688)

* [.claude/skills] LLM-on-NPU2 deployment skill chain (kernel-first, registry-aligned)

13-skill chain for deploying decoder-only LLMs on NPU2 via the 7-phase
deploy-new-llm orchestrator, aligned to the upstream programming_examples/llms/
layout, the per-kernel kernel_registry (details/<Kernel>_bf16.md), and the
shared llms/verify/ subsystem (per-model verify_adapter.py).

Methodology:
- Phase 1 gate is the registry's GPU/vLLM-aligned standard: harness
  element-wise atol/rtol vs FP32 reference where a harness exists, with
  diagnosis cosine vs HF bf16 as the no-harness fallback.
- Phase 6/7 end-to-end gate is the shared verify subsystem's top-k token-set
  check (mirrors vLLM), re-run independently in Phase 7.
- Kernel-first is the default integration path (compose registry leaf kernels
  via the shared llama_kernel_builder); inheritance from llama32_1b is a
  bit-for-bit-match shortcut, with single-block-validation owning that rule.

Track .claude/skills/ in git (.gitignore un-ignore rule).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4 (1M context) <<redacted>>

* [.claude/skills] align Phase 4/5/6 gate wording with the real verify subsystem

The verify subsystem retired threshold-based diagnosis: comparators.py's
compare_pair reports per-layer cosine with NO pass/fail, and only
`make verify` (--prompts topk_token, GATE_K=5, 32 tokens, mirrors vLLM
check_logprobs_close) exits non-zero. The optimization/finalize skills
still treated "diagnosis per-layer cosine >= 0.85" as a co-equal hard gate.

- prefill-optimization / decode-optimization: PASS criterion #1 is now
  "make verify token-set still PASSES"; diagnosis is the informational
  localization lens run only when verify FAILs (decode skill notes
  diagnosis probes prefill only, so decode regressions surface in verify's
  32-token generation, not diagnosis).
- finalize-and-learn: criterion #5 demoted from a 0.85 gate to an
  informational eyeball check; verify (criterion #4) is the gate.
- deploy-new-llm: orchestrator phase table + knowledge-base note no longer
  imply cosine is a co-equal gate.

Phase 2/3 keep cosine as the documented interim intermediate-activation
lens (no token to score mid-stack) per the existing standardization note.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4 (1M context) <<redacted>>

* [.claude/skills] align with PR #1687 GEMM split + machine-readable registry

PR #1687 (Xilinx/mlir-air, about to merge) splits the BF16 GEMM example by
output dtype, splits the registry GEMM detail page, makes the registry
machine-readable, and drives llama prefill GEMM tile configs from it.

- kernel-validation: GEMM harness is now matrix_multiplication/bf16_in_bf16_out
  + bf16_in_fp32_out (legacy bf16/ kept for NPU1); GEMM detail page split into
  GEMM_bf16_in_{bf16,fp32}_out.md; document registry_lookup.py gemm_config()
  as the machine-readable half (raises on unmeasured shapes — recording a
  shape in Phase 1 unlocks the Phase 4 lookup).
- single-block-validation: GEMM production path is now the registry
  high-precision tier (~9.3e-3, FP32-accumulate + single cast) not the old
  0.005-0.025 MAE wording; Down-GEMM failure row points at the
  high vs low precision tier.
- prefill-optimization: Pattern A gains a registry-driven-config sub-point —
  look tile sizes up via gemm_config(precision="high") instead of hardcoding
  (removes the Gate/Up tile_k_l2 drift bug #1687 fixed).
- deploy-new-llm: knowledge-base registry entry now covers both the human
  (md) and machine (json + registry_lookup.py) halves.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4 (1M context) <<redacted>>

* [.claude/skills] number the 8 phase skills (phase-0 … phase-7)

Rename the per-phase deployment skills with a phase-N- prefix so the
.claude/skills/ directory sorts in pipeline order and each skill's place in
the 0→7 flow is obvious at a glance:

  build-cpu-reference        -> phase-0-build-cpu-reference
  kernel-va

Breaking change. The single `pnge` plugin (76 skills / 12 agents / 12 commands) is
retired. `claude.pnge` now ships `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` listing 8

  endpoints only and defers install-inventory to the built-in /plugin command.

  `claude plugin install <redacted>` installs v1.0.0 clean.

review. Investigation found .claude/ is not a personal sandbox — it's
this repo's own dogfood install target (plugin.json's install.target is
".claude/", and core/scripts/build-release.sh packages core/ into a zip
explicitly meant to be unzipped into a target project's .claude/, this
repo included). It had drifted badly: .claude/skills/ had only 402 of
core/'s 1990 skill dirs, several hooks/scripts/rules existed on only one
side, agents count differed by one.

Ran build-release.sh (which gates on a 100% hook-test pass — see the
separate hook-portability-fixes commit that unblocked it), then unzipped
the resulting pack over .claude/{agents,commands,config,docs,gates,hooks,
prompts,rules,scripts,skills,templates,tests}/ as a pure overlay (adds/
updates, does not delete). .claude/assistant/, .claude/state/, and
.claude/settings.json were excluded from the source zip already (not part
of build-release.sh's include list) and are confirmed untouched — that's
this repo's genuinely local/personal state, not build output.

Pre-existing files unique to .claude/ (a handful of hooks/rules/agents
core/ doesn't have) were intentionally left in place, not deleted, since
this pass didn't establish whether those are stray drift or deliberate
local additions — a separate decision, not blocking this resync.

fix(auth): authStateReady race fixes + context-aware landing CTAs (#131)

* fix(auth): await authStateReady() before guest sign-in to prevent race condition

APP_INITIALIZER runs before Firebase restores the persisted session from
IndexedDB. Previously, currentUser was null in this window, causing
signInGuestIfNeeded() to fire an anonymous sign-in that overwrote a
real (Google/email) session on every page reload.

Fix: await auth.authStateReady() so Firebase has fully resolved the
initial auth state before deciding whether guest sign-in is needed.

Adds AuthAdapter.authStateReady() as a thin wrapper around the
Firebase Auth.authStateReady() API.

* fix(auth): remove auto guest sign-in from APP_INITIALIZER

Guest login should only happen on explicit user action (clicking
'Als Gast ausprobieren'), not automatically for every visitor.

The automatic sign-in was causing all users to get an anonymous session
on startup, which also contributed to the race condition on page reload.

Guest flow now: user clicks button → signInGuestIfNeeded() → navigate to /app
Unauthenticated users navigating directly to /app → redirected to /login

* fix(auth): await authStateReady() in guards to prevent reload redirect

authGuard and publicOnlyGuard were synchronous — on page reload Firebase
hadn't restored the persisted session yet, so isAuthenticated() and
currentUser were both falsy, causing a redirect to /login even for
authenticated users.

Both guards now await firebaseAuth.authStateReady() before checking
auth state, ensuring the decision is made on the settled session.

* feat(landing): show context-aware CTA buttons based on auth state

- Unauthenticated: show all 3 buttons (Register, Login, Als Gast)
- Authenticated as real user: show only 'Zum Dashboard'
- Authenticated as guest: show 'Zum Dashboard' + 'Konto erstellen'

Adds AuthStore to LandingPageComponent for isAuthenticated/isGuest signals.

Updates spec to cover all 3 auth states.

description: Computes the six benchmark-relative metrics that drive consolidation decisions for an Indian MF portfolio — Sortino ratio, rolling 3Y alpha (annualized excess return), max drawdown + recovery, downside capture, rolling 3Y beat-%, and beta. Reads cached NAVs and TRIs; emits one wide row per fund at data/metrics/<date>/per_fund_metrics.csv. Use whenever scoring funds, comparing performance vs benchmark, or refreshing the metrics that feed the consolidation decision. Don't use for debt or hybrid funds in v1.
first_commit_message:
mf_analyze: implement compute-core-metrics — the headline-value skill

The six benchmark-relative metrics that drive consolidation decisions
(per CLAUDE.md "Decision Lens"): Sortino (5Y), rolling 3Y alpha + beat-%
(7Y), max drawdown + recovery (all-available), downside capture (5Y),
beta (5Y). Computed at monthly frequency from end-of-month NAV.

- lib_metrics.py: pure-function metric implementations. Each metric
  takes a clean pandas Series/DataFrame and returns a number — testable
  in isolation, no I/O.
- compute_metrics.py: orchestrator. Imports resolve_benchmark() from
  benchmark-mapper (single source of truth for the category→TRI rules,
  no duplication). Loops over latest holdings snapshot, loads cached
  NAV + TRI per fund, emits one wide row per in-scope fund.
- Lookback policy from CLAUDE.md: drawdown all-available, Sortino/
  capture/beta 5Y, rolling-alpha/beat-% 7Y. Short-history funds
  produce per-fund warnings via the lookback_warnings column rather
  than being silently dropped.
- Alpha defined as simple annualized excess return (3Y fund CAGR -
  3Y bench CAGR), per user preference. Beta emitted as a side metric
  so unusual-beta funds can be interpreted.
- formula_choices.md: rationale for every formula choice (Sortino vs
  Sharpe, simple vs Jensen alpha, ratio-of-sums capture, etc.) so
  future maintainers don't have to re-derive the conventions.
- End-to-end validated on the real 10-fund equity portfolio:
  * Every max-drawdown date clusters at 2020-03-23/24 (COVID bottom)
  * Index funds correctly come in at β≈1.000 and beat-%≈0
  * Active funds show β = 0.65-0.93 with dispersion in alpha (PPFAS
    +4%, Kotak Flexicap -1%; Nippon Small Cap +6.6%, Kotak Small
    Cap -2.8%) — surfacing real consolidation candidates.

first_commit_message:
Fix removal in identity views and widen hill-climber counters

values().remove(o): for weak/soft value caches now uses identity
equivalence (matching IdentityHashMap's semantics) rather than Guava's
accidental equals-based behavior (inherited from AbstractCollection).

keySet()/entrySet().removeAll: the size optimization picks between
iterating the cache vs. iterating the user collection, but for weak
keys the cache compares by identity. Iterating the user collection
calls cache.remove(item) with a possibly equal-but-distinct instance,
which misses by identity. Always iterate the cache when collectKeys()
is true, matching IdentityHashMap.KeySet.removeAll's defensive comment.

hitsInSample and missesInSample widen from int to long to avoid
counters overflowing before the hill climber reset triggered, leaving
requestCount stuck negative and permanently disabling adjustment.

Expanded the internal consistency checks in the test assertions for a
more thorough verification.

- 專案將長期由 AI agent 維運，需要把「怎麼正確地做事」從隱性知識變成可執行的制度
- 既有規範偏原則性描述，缺少逐步驟、附真實範例檔路徑的任務 recipe，容易做出不一致的實作

- 新環境有已知假失敗（packages 未 build 時 typecheck 必炸），每個 session 都要重新踩一次
- 架構慣例（i18n Link、SafeAreaView 來源、schema/migration 同步）靠人工 review 把關，成本高且會漏

- 新增 5 個任務 playbook skills（add-api-endpoint / add-db-migration / add-web-page /

fix(compute): close commons settlement durability gap and repair core/ledger boundary (#1485)

Closes the durability and auditability gaps in commons-scope compute settlement.

**What changed:**
- Wire commons compute completion to ledger settlement (earn+spend entries) with sled-backed dedup
- Add settlement query endpoints: by task_id and by receipt-hash (restart-safe)
- Fix commons scope routing: commons-scoped FederationClearingNotification now defers instead of entering bilateral clearing
- Extract all compute→ledger callbacks from icn-core to daemon composition root (bins/icnd/src/compute_wiring.rs)
- Introduce SettlementQueryService trait in icn-kernel-api; remove concrete SettlementEngine from passthrough structs
- Update meaning firewall ratchet 21→5
- Add ops truth spine (policy.json, agents.json, skills.json, sources.json) and CI drift-check workflow

**Why:**
Commons-scope task completion previously had no ledger consequence (callback wired to None), no dedup (earn could double-settle on retry), no audit surface (no query endpoint), and scope-leaked into bilateral clearing. The kernel/app boundary was also broken: icn-core built ledger-backed callbacks directly, violating the meaning firewall.

**Validation:**
- cargo fmt / clippy / test: all passing
- All 11 required CI checks: passing
- Meaning firewall ratchet test: 12/12
- icnd integration test: 1/1
- icn-gateway lib tests: 488/488

**Known boundaries / not included:**
- Non-atomic earn+spend (documented limitation — requires batch-append ledger support)
- Federation cross-cluster commons clearing (deferred by design)
- Broader governance→execution dispatch (not in scope)

# 사용자 피드백 3가지

## 1. 좌우 pane 독립 스크롤
**증상**: 학습지 pane 스크롤 시 도전 pane도 함께 위로 사라짐 (한 컨테이너 스크롤)
**해결**:
- .aft-modal-body: overflow-y:auto → overflow:hidden + flex column
- .aft-problems-pane-wrap: flex:1 + min-height:0
- .aft-problems-pane: 자체 overflow-y:auto + min-height:0
- 좌·우 pane이 각자 독립 스크롤. 한쪽 길어도 다른 쪽 헤더·내용 그대로 유지.

## 2. sticky 헤더 위 빈 공간 + 스크롤 시 내용 헤더 뒤로 비침
**증상**: 헤더와 본문 사이 공간 / 스크롤 시 글자 헤더 뒤로 지나가는 게 보임
**해결**:
- modal body padding 제거 → pane이 padding 보유
- pane title에 padding-top:18px (modal 위쪽 여백을 헤더에 직접 부여)
- 헤더 box-shadow 추가 → 스크롤 시 헤더 아래 그림자로 자연스러운 분리
- z-index 5로 격상 → 스크롤되는 내용 위에 확실히 올라옴

## 3. 그룹 헤더(🟡 기본 / 🔴 심화)가 카드 내용과 안 맞음
**증상**: "02. 수준별 훈련" 위에 "🟡 기본" 헤더, "03. 형성평가" 위에 "🔴 심화" 헤더

**해결**:
- widgets.js: 그룹 헤더 element 생성 제거. GROUPS 순서 유지하되 카드만 stacking
- 카드 자체 제목(02. 수준별 훈련 / 03. 형성평가)이 콘텐츠 구분으로 충분
- 학습지_01 03 카드 마킹: l3 → l2 (형성평가는 심화가 아닌 단원 마무리 평가)

# 모바일 (800px 이하)
- pane 세로 stack — 각 pane이 절반 높이로 독립 스크롤 (flex:1 1 50%)

feat(mcp): Merge jaegermcp extention into jaegerquery extension (#8894)

## 🛑 Breaking change

The `jaegermcp` extension that used to run on an MCP server on a
separate port has been merged into the `jaegerquery` extension and the
MCP tools are not available from the main query port under `/api/ai/mcp`

## Which problem is this PR solving?
- Resolves the first phase of #8890: serve the Jaeger telemetry MCP
tools
in-process from `jaeger-query` instead of via the standalone
`jaeger_mcp`
extension, so all MCP traffic lands on the query port and the tool
library
  can be shared with the AI gateway.

## Description of the changes
- Move the MCP tool library out of the `jaeger_mcp` extension into
`jaegerquery/internal/mcptools/` — a sibling of `jaegerai`, since
telemetry
tools are a query capability, not an AI-gateway one (the endpoint serves
  Cursor/IDE clients with no AI involved).
- Add `mcptools.NewHandler(telset, queryService, tenancyMgr, cfg)`:
builds the
MCP server (tools + tracing/metrics middleware + tenancy + otelhttp) and
returns an `http.Handler`. It takes `*querysvc.QueryService`
**directly**
  rather than via the component host, which avoids the import cycle a
  host-based lookup would create under `jaegerquery/internal`.
- `jaeger-query` mounts it at `<basePath>/api/ai/mcp/`, gated by a new
`ai.enable_mcp` boolean (default `false`). `ai.agent_url` is now
optional;
config validates when `agent_url` **or** `enable_mcp` is set, enabling
the
  three deployment modes from #8890 (chat-only / MCP-only / both).
- **Retire the `jaeger_mcp` extension**: delete the extension and its
two
re-export wrappers, and drop it from `components.go`,
`telemetryfactory`,
  and the `all-in-one.yaml` / `config.yaml` / `builder.yaml` samples.

## Breaking change
`jaeger_mcp` (experimental) is removed. MCP clients (Cursor, IDE
plugins)
that pointed at `jaeger_mcp:16687` must switch to the query port and set
`ai.enable_mcp: true`; tools are served at `<basePath>/api/ai/mcp/`.

## How was this change tested?
- New `mcptools/server_test.go` drives the full HTTP serving stack with
a real
MCP client (ListTools + CallTool end-to-end); `initRouter` subtests
cover the
`enable_mcp` mount (with and without base path) and MCP-only validation.
- `go build ./...`, `make lint`, and the full `cmd/jaeger/...` suite
pass.
- Coverage stays above the 95% gate (mcptools 98.2%,
jaegerquery/internal 98.9%).

https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING_GUIDELINES.md
- [x] I have signed all commits
- [x] I have added unit tests for the new functionality

description: Auto-generates a visual_test_plan.json for a given game + level. Reads the GDD's aesthetic targets, the level's entities.json, the session's git diff, the assertion library, and the priors library — emits a concrete list of 10-15 visual tests that the ADR 0056 runner can execute. Distinct from yume-visual-designer (which is a subjective rubric reviewer) — this skill produces objective binary pass/fail assertions specific to the game's actual contents. Phase B of ADR 0056 / 0057.
first_commit_message:
yume-visual-tester skill — auto-generates visual_test_plan.json

Phase B of ADR 0057. Three pieces ship together:

1. godot/data/lib/visual_qa/priors.json — 11 starter priors
   covering common-sense world facts (trees > characters, structures
   rest on ground, animated chars use foot-pivot, water biome is
   shiny, etc.). Each prior declares: trigger (tag/property match),
   emit (assertion + params with token substitution), priority,
   max_pairs cap. Plus guard semantics (e.g. distinct_silhouettes
   only fires for Fellowship/Narrative-aesthetic GDDs) and the
   git_diff_touches_def special trigger for recently-changed
   entities.

2. .claude/skills/yume-visual-tester/SKILL.md — describes the
   procedure: load inputs (GDD aesthetics, level entities, biome
   set from scene.json, recently-changed defs from git diff),
   walk priors + match against entities, cap pairs per max_pairs,
   validate emitted tests against assertion schemas, order by
   priority + recently-changed, cap at max_tests. Plus token
   resolution reference.

3. tools/visual_qa/generate_plan.py — deterministic Python
   implementation of the procedure. Reads priors.json, walks
   entities, emits tests, validates, orders, caps, writes plan +
   report. NO LLM calls (priors are declarative enough that
   pattern matching covers Phase B). CLI: --level, --diff-base,
   --max-tests, --no-cache. Cache key: hash(game, level,
   diff_base, entities.json content). Output:
   tools/visual_qa/plans/<game>_<level>_<diff>.json + .md.

End-to-end verified on demo_aldenmere:
- Generator emits 12 tests from 11 priors (after cap from 13
  pre-cap). Mix of high (9) + medium (3). Touches recently-
  changed: 0 (no entity defs in HEAD~1 diff).
- Plan format compatible with the ADR 0056 runner — runner
  consumes the auto-gen plan as-is.
- Dry-run all 12 tests through run_plan.py: poses computed,
  entities resolved, prompts rendered.
- Live capture of 2 tests: NE sanity cube sweep landed cleanly
  (no checker, no orphan cubes). Tree-vs-player capture revealed
  a known framing-math limitation — camera placed inside foliage
  cluster (occlusion not checked). Tracked as task #96; the
  generator + runner are correct, the limitation is in the
  perpendicular-offset framing rule.

Phase B is COMPLETE: the auto-gen → runner → captures pipeline
works without any per-test human authoring. yume-visual-tester
becomes the entry point; humans only update priors.json when
post-mortems reveal new visual bug classes.

Add operations-sentry notebook; introduce Design Topic (DT-XXX) convention

Closes the exploration phase of the operations-sentry project. Captures
eight Design Topics (DT-001 through DT-008) covering Sentry SDK + OTel
agent coexistence, common-module SDK init placement, AppError-based
filtering policy via `reportable(): List<Throwable>`, session-based
release health with sample rates aligned to the frontend, PII scrubbing
in `beforeSend` (opaque user IDs, headers allow-list with HMAC-hashed
tenant tag, request-body redaction, DB-statement literal redaction),
boundary capture topology with JVM-level last-resort handler, frontend
`tracePropagationTargets` configuration, and backend Sentry Logback
forwarding. accounts-component adoption tracked separately as PDEV-533.

The notebook drove three workbook-convention refinements, applied in
this commit so future projects inherit them by default:

- Single `DT-XXX` Design Topic numbering scheme (3-digit zero-padded,
  hierarchical sub-topics as `DT-XXX.YY`) shared across threads and
  decisions, replacing the prior `T<N>`/`D<N>` split-numbering in the
  templates.
- Inline `- [ ] #proposed-topic <title>` callout convention for new
  topics surfaced mid-writing. Promoted on triage to a real DT-XXX
  file, or discarded with reason; the work-board surfaces open
  proposals via a Dataview TASK query.
- Project-wide Dataview views (`FROM "notebooks/<project>"` filtering
  on the `design-topic` frontmatter field) so any file carrying a
  Design Topic appears regardless of subdirectory. Use
  `link(file.path, title)` instead of bare `file.link` so threads
  living in `<dt>/index.md` directories render with meaningful titles.

first_commit_message:
refactor [BP-0009]: rename all skills to assess-<domain>

The original ticket proposed a three-prefix taxonomy (coverage- / review- /
assess-) to telegraph what each skill does. Discussion surfaced two name
collisions that would mislead users:

- "coverage" is overloaded with the deterministic "test coverage %" meaning,
  the opposite of what the additive skills do (qualitative gap analysis).
- "review" evokes a PR-review bot (Greptile, CodeRabbit), which BP-0008 just
  declared this repo is NOT.

Decision: drop the taxonomy as a naming axis and use a uniform `assess-<domain>`
pattern. Mechanical, predictable, no collision with adjacent tooling concepts,
and lines up with the future plugin namespace planned in BP-0003
(best-practices:assess-secure-coding, etc.).

Renames:

  secure-review          -> assess-secure-coding
  principles-review      -> assess-coding-principles
  observability-review   -> assess-observability
  configuration-review   -> assess-configuration
  testing-review         -> assess-testing
  ci-cd-review           -> assess-ci-cd
  iac-review             -> assess-iac
  contract-design-review -> assess-contract-design
  system-design-review   -> assess-system-design
  data-design-review     -> assess-data-design

The `overview` skill keeps its name — it's a discovery entrypoint, not an
assessment. Two of the assessment skills get expanded names to disambiguate
their domain ("secure-coding" not just "secure", "coding-principles" not just
"principles").

Updates:
- 10 directories renamed via git mv (history preserved).
- Frontmatter `name:` and `/<old-slash>` references in every SKILL.md.
- `.skills/overview/SKILL.md` catalog table and sample invocations.
- `.claude-commands/best-practices.md` description.
- Root README:
  * "Available skills" line.
  * Quick start examples (/secure-review -> /assess-secure-coding, etc.).
  * "About the skills" section: dropped the coverage/review/assess
    taxonomy paragraph (Option A discussed in the issue comment) since it
    no longer maps to skill names. Replaced with a "Predictable naming"
    bullet describing the assess-<domain> pattern.
  * Determinism section: skill examples updated.
- Makefile help example.

This is a breaking change. Anyone who installed previously needs to
reinstall — the old skill names no longer exist. Acceptable per ticket
(alpha stage).

Verified end-to-end: make install-claude and install-cursor produce
11 entries each (10 assess-* + overview).

The "tool-backed / hybrid / LLM-pure" categorization introduced in BP-0008
is unaffected — orthogonal to naming, stays in the README.

Closes #9

  Flow Summary, Node Inflow Summary, and Outfall Loading Summary on the tracked

chore(agents): share workflow rules and skill library with the team (#3988)

* chore(agents): codify worktree, rebase, no-stack, no-debt, and test rules

Promotes four workflow non-negotiables from personal agent memory into
the repo so every contributor (human or agent) gets the same playbook:

- Always start in a new worktree branched from `origin/main` (not local
  `main`, which can be stale).
- Always `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main` before every
  `git push` (use `--force-with-lease`, never `--force`).
- Never stack PRs — every PR targets `main`. Combine dependent features
  into one bigger PR with delineated commits, instead of splitting and
  basing one PR's branch on another's.
- No technical debt — fix issues in the PR that touches them; no
  deferral via `// TODO`, `@Skip`, or commented-out code (transitional
  TODOs with tracking-issue links remain allowed per code_style.md).
- Failing tests are never acceptable and always your fault. `origin/main`
  always passes, so any red test on a feature branch is caused by that
  branch's diff. Never blame flakiness, never `@Skip` to silence, never
  push red.

The detailed reference and rationale live in `.claude/rules/agent_workflow.md`.
`AGENTS.md` and `self_review_checklist.md` get the operational summary at
the gates where they apply (start of task, before commit, before PR).

feat(slurm): per-submission immutable job-spec files

Job specs move from a mutable .remake/jobs/<rule>.json to write-once
.remake/jobs/<rule>.<run_seq>.json, pinned by the generated sbatch
scripts via `run-array-task --specs`. The jobids sidecar records the
submission's run_seq, so last_submission/task-info map array indices
against the spec that was actually submitted, and manual
run-array-task (no --specs) resolves the last SUBMITTED spec through
the sidecar — never a dry-run plan. _write_job_specs enforces
write-once (raises on an existing path).

This is the root fix for the 2026-07-09 review findings 1-4/12: a
replan, dry run, or fail-open queued-guard can no longer corrupt the
indices a queued array reads — worst case is now a duplicate
submission. Legacy fallbacks keep pre-0.9 sidecars (no run_seq) and
in-flight jobs working across the upgrade.

Adversarially reviewed (/code-review high on the executor + medium on
this diff); findings addressed, incl. sidecar-first spec resolution
and the write-once guard.

last_commit_message:
chore(workflow): gate the BRIEF against the code, and make the review verdict durable (#884)

* chore(workflow): gate the BRIEF against the code, and make the review verdict durable

Two structural gaps in the builder lane, both filed from the 2026-07-17 pipeline run and
both demonstrated by that same run.

task_587984d1 — THE BRIEF HAD NO GATE.
Every gate in the lane (sol refine, cross-vendor review, the Architect audit) judges CODE
against BRIEF. Nothing judged BRIEF against CODE. So a factually wrong brief yields
well-tested, green-on-every-gate work on a false premise, and no downstream reviewer can
catch it BY CONSTRUCTION — the code genuinely does match the brief. Measured on the first
full pipeline run: 4 of 5 briefs were factually wrong (chips filed weeks earlier; the code
moved underneath them), and task_a86f2d17 burned an entire build before review killed its
premise. Verifying chips during recon was a HABIT, and habits get skipped under time
pressure and on autonomous runs — exactly when nothing else is watching.

Adds STEP 0 to build.tpl: verify every load-bearing claim (file:line cites, "X currently
does Y", "there is no Z", every named symbol/column/config-key spelled exactly) against the
CURRENT tree BEFORE writing code, and open the receipt with BRIEF-CONFIRMED /
BRIEF-CORRECTED (proceed against the code, list what changed) / BRIEF-INVALID (STOP). The
same in refine.tpl — sol must not inherit the drafter's premises, and where a claim is
cheap to test for real (an HTTP GET, a SQL query, a grep) it must TEST rather than read:
this run produced a fetcher built against a URL that 404s WHILE ITS OWN WIREMOCK TEST
STUBBED THE SAME WRONG PATH — five green tests validating a fiction, caught only because
sol made a real request. SKILL.md tells the Architect how to act on each verdict (fold
BRIEF-CORRECTED back into the chip; re-file on BRIEF-INVALID; a missing verdict = an
incomplete receipt). Kept cheap on purpose: it rides the reading the builder must do anyway
— an expensive gate gets skipped, which IS the failure mode.

task_07199525 — THE REVIEW VERDICT WAS NOT DURABLE, AND ONE IS ALREADY LOST.
Verdicts are written to .claude/skills/*/state/*.review.txt; everything under state/ is
gitignored — per-run scratch on one machine, deleted with the worktree. The PR body is the
only durable record. ship-a-change asked for a vague "review outcome" in a bullet list and
it did not bind: of three PRs shipped the same night through the same lane, #878 carried the
verdict, #877 carried a review FINDING but no verdict, and #879 carried nothing — that
review is permanently unrecoverable.

Gives it a fixed greppable shape in ship-a-change + delegated-ship:
  Cross-vendor review: APPROVED | REQUEST_CHANGES (resolved) | NEEDS_REWORK (resolved) | SKIPPED (<reason>)
plus the reviewer's vendor/model. SKIPPED (<reason>) is FIRST-CLASS — ROUTING.md legitimately
allows skipping trivial/docs, and a rule that cannot express the legitimate case gets ignored
in the illegitimate one.

Adds ci-review-verdict.yml — a body-only check (no checkout, no build, ~2s). hotfix/*
branches are exempt BY DESIGN (a live incident must never wait on a doc gate) and it is not
a required check, so --admin merges past it: the point is to make an omission VISIBLE, not to
hold the repo hostage to a regex. Regex proven against the real bodies before commit: #878
PASS, #877/#879 FAIL correctly, all four legitimate shapes accepted, `SKIPPED ()` with an
empty reason REJECTED, vague prose REJECTED.

It immediately caught two of my own PRs — #881 and #883 — written hours after reading this
chip's evidence, both Opus-reviewed, both missing the line. Their bodies now carry it. That
is the argument for the check over another instruction to remember.

Deliberately NOT done: no per-change review doc (upstream TRIP writes docs/3-code-review/CR_*.md;
in a solo repo the PR IS the record, GitHub retains it, and CLAUDE.md forbids proactive doc
files). No duplication of codex/check

Initial pi-toolbox workspace

A workspace that bundles custom pi extensions, subagent templates,
prompt templates, and skills for use with the pi coding agent.

Contents
  - extensions/: 20 custom pi extensions plus config wrappers for
    pi-rtk-optimizer and pi-tool-display, and a guardrails.json
    policy file.
  - agents/: 9 subagent definitions. Their extensions frontmatter
    is intentionally omitted so each subagent inherits the host
    user's extension set.
  - prompts/: 13 slash-command prompt templates.
  - skills/: 4 skills.
  - tests/: three vitest suites covering the extensions layout,
    guardrails config, and the pi-update-extensions tooling.
  - scripts/pi-update-extensions.ts: pins pi-* sibling packages to
    the globally installed pi CLI version, applies the pi-coding-
    agent resolver patch, and refreshes gitchamber source
    snapshots.

Tooling
  - Private package; no npm keywords.
  - mise.toml exposes one-shot check, test, knip, and pi-update
    tasks.
  - Single auto-fixing check command (oxlint --fix --deny-warnings
    then oxfmt). knip is advisory only because knip --fix removes
    pi extension default-export entry points and genuine runtime
    dependencies.

chore(.claude): resync .claude/ from core/ via build-release.sh (item #4)

Resolves the core/.claude drift flagged in the earlier architecture
review. Investigation found .claude/ is not a personal sandbox — it's
this repo's own dogfood install target (plugin.json's install.target is
".claude/", and core/scripts/build-release.sh packages core/ into a zip
explicitly meant to be unzipped into a target project's .claude/, this
repo included). It had drifted badly: .claude/skills/ had only 402 of
core/'s 1990 skill dirs, several hooks/scripts/rules existed on only one
side, agents count differed by one.

Ran build-release.sh (which gates on a 100% hook-test pass — see the
separate hook-portability-fixes commit that unblocked it), then unzipped
the resulting pack over .claude/{agents,commands,config,docs,gates,hooks,
prompts,rules,scripts,skills,templates,tests}/ as a pure overlay (adds/
updates, does not delete). .claude/assistant/, .claude/state/, and
.claude/settings.json were excluded from the source zip already (not part
of build-release.sh's include list) and are confirmed untouched — that's
this repo's genuinely local/personal state, not build output.

Pre-existing files unique to .claude/ (a handful of hooks/rules/agents
core/ doesn't have) were intentionally left in place, not deleted, since
this pass didn't establish whether those are stray drift or deliberate
local additions — a separate decision, not blocking this resync.

Verified: bash .claude/tests/hooks/run-hook-tests.sh → 104/104 pass.

  load). Qualify codex-exec's resume as "only with new work" and point bare
  resume at codex-session.

.claude/settings.json were excluded from the source zip already (not part
of build-release.sh's include list) and are confirmed untouched — that's
this repo's genuinely local/personal state, not build output.

Pre-existing files unique to .claude/ (a handful of hooks/rules/agents
core/ doesn't have) were intentionally left in place, not deleted, since
this pass didn't establish whether those are stray drift or deliberate
local additions — a separate decision, not blocking this resync.

## Summary

Storybook Autodocs **Show code** snippets and MCP manifest snippets are
what agents and developers copy from docs, but nothing in CI caught when
those outputs drifted after story edits. Dev Storybook also differs from
the production build (e.g. React Compiler), so manual checks against
`pnpm start` were unreliable.

dedicated Vitest `storybook-docs` project. Global setup builds and
serves `storybook-static` on an ephemeral port (same artifact as GitHub
Pages), then tests verify both outputs per story:

- **Show code** — Playwright opens Autodocs, expands **Show code**,
snapshots the panel text
- **MCP manifest** — fetches `components.json` and snapshots the story
`snippet`

Shared helpers live under `tests/storybook/`. `test:storybook-docs` runs
the project explicitly; default `pnpm test` excludes it (like
`requires-build`). CI builds Storybook and runs docs tests on PRs.

workflows are updated to point authors at the new pattern.

first_commit_message:
🔧 Skill Tools — agent evolution creates executable tools

The missing piece for true closed-loop evolution: agents can now
create, evolve, and execute their own tools through SKILL.md.

## How it works

1. Agent fails a task (e.g., 'what's the weather?')
2. SkillEvolver analyzes failure → CAPTURED suggestion
3. LLM generates SKILL.md with `tools:` section in frontmatter:
   ```yaml
   tools:
     - name: get-weather
       command: 'curl -s "wttr.in/{{input}}?format=3"'
       timeout: 10s
   ```
4. Next time: builtin runtime loads skill tools dynamically
5. Agent uses `get-weather Shanghai` → gets real data

## New files
- engine/skill_tool.go: SkillTool wraps SKILL.md tool defs as engine.Tool
  - Shell command templates with {{input}} interpolation
  - Configurable timeout, interpreter, workdir
  - Shell injection prevention (auto-quoting dangerous chars)
- engine/skill_tool_test.go: 7 tests (execute, timeout, injection, failure)

## Changes
- SkillMeta: added `tools` field ([]SkillToolMeta)
- SkillEvolver capture prompt: now instructs LLM to generate tools
- SkillEvolver derive: inherits parent tools + LLM can add new ones
- Builtin runtime: collects all skill tools before task execution
- Agent.collectSkillTools(): scans SkillFS for tool definitions

## Evolution chain (complete)
```
Task failure → Analysis → SKILL.md with tools → IPFS publish →
P2P broadcast → Peer learning → Next task uses evolved tools ✅
```

Tests: 234 total (7 new skill tool tests)

- AUR: chalkak-ocr-models companion package, cmake makedep,
  optdepends on ocr models

  preview/shell (moved to #[cfg(test)] or removed)

* ✨ Introduce Color newtype for editor tools

instead of inheriting parent scope via glob imports. Clean up

Tab works regardless of modifier state and avoids conflict

Compute ocr_available flag at startup via resolve_model_dir()

Add results path, clean skill, loop rename, SUCCESS fix

Increment 7. Four orthogonal fixes shipped together:

- Rename loop → run to eliminate the name collision with the built-in
  loop scheduler skill. All stage skills now reference /run.

- Migrate results path from repo-root results/ to {app-path}/sunwell-results/
  in all skills (profile, analyze, improve, experiment, run). Each skill
  derives results-dir = {app-path}/sunwell-results immediately after reading
  sunwell.yml, then uses that variable throughout. Scripts are unaffected —
  they receive fully-resolved paths as arguments.

- Add clean skill: reads experiments.json for all files-changed entries,
  presents a confirmation summary, then git-restores each file and deletes
  sunwell-results/ on explicit confirm. No destructive action before confirm.

- Fix SUCCESS termination condition from ANY benchmark to ALL benchmarks.
  The old ANY semantics fired too eagerly — a single benchmark doubling would
  end the session. ALL means every benchmark has converged, which is the
  correct definition of done.

Root .gitignore: replace results/ + per-app .gitignore with a single
**/sunwell-results/ pattern. App-level duplication violates DRY — the root
catchall covers all apps at any depth, same as Maven's target/ convention.
Deleted the legacy results/ directory (old run data, superseded by new path).

Also fixed stale /sunwell:* skill references in improve/SKILL.md — all
user-facing messages now use short form (/profile, /analyze, /improve)
consistent with every other skill.

last_commit_message:
Fix clean skill — replace ! code blocks with prose instructions

The skill framework executes ```!``` fenced blocks as literal shell
commands before Claude runs, with no template substitution. This caused
two failures: git restore ran with the literal string "{file}" and the
permission checker rejected "rm -rf {results-dir}" because curly-brace
placeholders look like glob patterns in write operations.

Fix: replace both ```!``` blocks with prose instructions that tell
Claude to use the Bash tool with the actual resolved path. Also removed
Bash(rm -rf *) from allowed-tools since the glob wildcard is rejected
by the write-operation permission check — rm -rf will prompt for tool
approval, which is appropriate for a destructive delete.

first_commit_message:
chore(.claude): resync .claude/ from core/ via build-release.sh (item #4)

Resolves the core/.claude drift flagged in the earlier architecture
review. Investigation found .claude/ is not a personal sandbox — it's
this repo's own dogfood install target (plugin.json's install.target is
".claude/", and core/scripts/build-release.sh packages core/ into a zip
explicitly meant to be unzipped into a target project's .claude/, this
repo included). It had drifted badly: .claude/skills/ had only 402 of
core/'s 1990 skill dirs, several hooks/scripts/rules existed on only one
side, agents count differed by one.

Ran build-release.sh (which gates on a 100% hook-test pass — see the
separate hook-portability-fixes commit that unblocked it), then unzipped
the resulting pack over .claude/{agents,commands,config,docs,gates,hooks,
prompts,rules,scripts,skills,templates,tests}/ as a pure overlay (adds/
updates, does not delete). .claude/assistant/, .claude/state/, and
.claude/settings.json were excluded from the source zip already (not part
of build-release.sh's include list) and are confirmed untouched — that's
this repo's genuinely local/personal state, not build output.

Pre-existing files unique to .claude/ (a handful of hooks/rules/agents
core/ doesn't have) were intentionally left in place, not deleted, since
this pass didn't establish whether those are stray drift or deliberate
local additions — a separate decision, not blocking this resync.

Verified: bash .claude/tests/hooks/run-hook-tests.sh → 104/104 pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <<redacted>>

first_commit_message:
Add skill definitions and PR/commit guidelines (#399)

Add three new skill definitions for common GitHub workflows and update
project conventions to clarify PR and commit message standards.

**Changes:**

- **`.claude/skills/review-pr/SKILL.md`** — New skill for reviewing pull
requests by number. Provides a structured workflow to fetch PR metadata
and diff, understand intent, evaluate against project conventions, and
report findings with actionable recommendations. Read-only; does not
modify code or post comments unless explicitly requested.

- **`.claude/skills/fix-issue/SKILL.md`** — New skill for resolving
GitHub issues end-to-end. Guides the workflow from reading the issue,
preparing a clean branch, implementing the fix, validating with build
and test commands, committing, and opening a pull request that closes
the issue.

- **`.claude/skills/publish-pr/SKILL.md`** — New skill for publishing
local changes as a pull request. Handles branch creation, staging,
committing, validation, pushing, and PR creation from current working
changes.

- **`.github/copilot-instructions.md`** — Add explicit guidance on pull
request titles, descriptions, and commit message attribution. Clarify
that PR text must always be in English, never mention AI assistance or
session links, and follow the repository's PR template.

- **`CLAUDE.md`** — Mirror the same PR and commit message guidelines,
with cross-reference to the new skills in `.claude/skills`.

All three skills enforce the no-AI-attribution rule: no `Co-Authored-By`
trailers, "Generated with" footers, session URLs, or mentions of
Claude/Copilot/AI assistance in PR titles, bodies, or commit messages
unless explicitly requested by the user.
last_commit_message:
Harden skills against AI-attribution leaking into PR text (#401)

## Summary

- PR #400 shipped with a trailing `_Generated by Claude Code_` footer
and session link, violating the `CLAUDE.md` rule against AI-attribution
in PR text.
- `fix-issue` and `publish-pr` already told the agent not to add such a
footer, but nothing forced a check on the final text before submitting.
- Added a final self-check step to both skills: scan the finished PR
title/body for "Claude", "Anthropic", "Generated with"/"Generated by",
"Co-Authored-By", `claude.ai`, or a session URL, and strip any match
before creating the PR — even if a default template or tool prefill
suggests adding one.
- `review-pr` now includes an "AI-attribution check" and reports any
such footer found on an existing PR as a **Blocking** finding.

## Test plan

- [x] Reviewed the updated `SKILL.md` files for consistency with the
rest of each skill's workflow.
- N/A — documentation-only change to `.claude/skills/*`; no build or
test suite applies.

✨feat: 크로스 플랫폼 지원 구조 추가 (Windows/Linux)

## 개요
Windows와 Linux/macOS 플랫폼 간 스크립트 및 설정 차이를 해결하기 위해
플랫폼별 디렉토리 구조를 도입했습니다.

## 추가된 구조

### platforms/ 디렉토리
- **platforms/linux/**: Linux/macOS용 파일
  - scripts/*.sh: Bash 스크립트 (git-helper, python-runner, study-note-helper)
  - .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md: Bash 명령어 예시
  - .katarc.patch: Linux 플랫폼 설정

- **platforms/windows/**: Windows용 파일
  - scripts/*.bat: 배치 스크립트 (git-helper, python-runner, study-note-helper)
  - .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md: CMD 명령어 예시
  - .katarc.patch: Windows 플랫폼 설정

- **platforms/README.md**: 플랫폼 설정 가이드

## 주요 변경사항

### 1. 플랫폼별 스크립트 작성
- **Linux용 (.sh)**: 기존 스크립트를 platforms/linux/로 이동
- **Windows용 (.bat)**: 동일 기능의 배치 스크립트 신규 작성
  - UTF-8 인코딩 지원 (chcp 65001)
  - Windows 경로 구분자 (\) 사용
  - cmd.exe 환경 최적화

### 2. 플랫폼별 SKILL.md
- **Linux**: `bash` 코드 블록, `./scripts/*.sh` 경로
- **Windows**: `cmd` 코드 블록, `scripts\*.bat` 경로
- 명령어 예시를 플랫폼에 맞게 작성

### 3. .gitignore 업데이트
플랫폼별로 생성되는 파일들을 추적하지 않도록 설정:
- .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md
- scripts/*.sh, scripts/*.bat
- .katarc

이를 통해 서로 다른 플랫폼 사용자 간 Git 충돌 방지

### 4. .katarc.patch 파일
플랫폼별 환경 변수 추가:
- PLATFORM (windows/linux)
- SCRIPT_EXT (.bat/.sh)
- VENV_ACTIVATE (가상환경 활성화 경로)

## 사용 방법

### Linux/macOS 사용자
```bash
cp -r platforms/linux/scripts/* scripts/
cp -r platforms/linux/.claude/skills/* .claude/skills/
cat platforms/linux/.katarc.patch >> .katarc
chmod +x scripts/*.sh
```

### Windows 사용자
```cmd
xcopy /E /I /Y platforms\windows\scripts scripts
xcopy /E /I /Y platforms\windows\.claude\.skills .claude\skills
type platforms\windows\.katarc.patch >> .katarc
```

## 장점

1. **명확한 플랫폼 분리**: 각 플랫폼에 최적화된 구현
2. **Git 충돌 방지**: .gitignore로 생성 파일 무시
3. **확장 가능**: 새 플랫폼 추가 시 platforms/{platform}/ 추가만 필요
4. **문서화**: platforms/README.md에 상세 가이드

## 파일 통계
- 16개 파일 변경
- 2,546줄 추가
- Windows용 배치 스크립트 3개 신규 작성
- 플랫폼별 SKILL.md 6개 작성

Update execution contract and skill guidelines to enforce "problem is fixed" default outcome

The execution contract has been strengthened to eliminate ambiguity around when work can stop. The default outcome is now explicitly "the problem is fixed" with only four legitimate blockers (B1-B4) that require formal proof. All other conditions that previously allowed stopping are now classified as work to be done. This change affects every skill and agent by requiring them to pursue root causes fully, expand scope when needed, and avoid workarounds or dodging behaviors. New hooks enforce these rules at the tool use level, blocking forbidden commands and temp file policies. The skill documentation has been updated consistently across all skills to reflect this new discipline, removing allowances for stopping on uncertainty and emphasizing that low confidence means "read more" rather than "stop."

first_commit_message:
Chem-tape v2 chronicle: §v2.4-alt / §v2.4-proxy / §v2.6 results + skill updates

Three chronicle entries appended to docs/chem-tape/experiments-v2.md
(commit 0230662 anchor):

- §v2.4-alt INCONCLUSIVE: thr=5 solves 17/20, thr=10 solves 1/20.
  Decode-position is NOT the universal blocker; the failure is the §v2.4
  max>5 proxy attractor (max>5 alone scores 100% on thr=5 task and 92%
  on thr=10 task — exactly the asymmetry observed). 1 BOTH-solve
  (seed 2) found a non-canonical compositional route.
- §v2.4-proxy FAIL-proxy-generalises: 3/20 solves under decorrelation.
  Evolution shifted away from max>5 (only 2/17 stuck there) but immediately
  found sum>10 (0.91 acc) as the next-best proxy. Attractor framing
  generalises beyond max>5 specifically. 3 solvers found genuine AND.
- §v2.6 PASS-narrow-positive: Pair 2 (sum r12) and Pair 3 (reduce_max)
  scale at 20/20 BOTH; Pair 1 (string-count) at 4/20 with components
  present but not chained — 6-token body topology vs 4-token bodies
  is the search-landscape edge.

Plus combined v2-suite verdict: reframes "compositional depth doesn't
scale" to "single-predicate proxy basin attractor dominates greedy
search whenever a near-perfect single-predicate exists in training data."

Methodology updates:
- Principle 16b (mechanism rename can go broader, not just narrower)
- Principle 20 (sampler design is a first-class experimental axis;
  prereg must measure class balance, primary proxy accuracy, and
  non-degeneracy when changing training distribution)
- Principle 21 (attractor-category classification required for any
  too-clean OR threshold-adjacent outcome — broader than just 20/20)

Research-rigor skill:
- Prereg mode: added Gate 5 (sampler-design audit) wiring principle 20
- Log-result mode: broadened too-clean trigger to include
  threshold-adjacent results (principle 21); added bidirectional
  mechanism-rename check (principle 16 + 16b)

Add §25b/§25c to methodology; delete v5 retrospective scratch

Folds lessons from §v2.5-plasticity-2a v1→v8 amendment cycle into the
durable methodology ledger:

- §25b — Routing-critical metric discipline. Three treatments for
  routing-critical clauses: (a) axis-specific occupancy guard, (b) CI
  bound with bootstrap-reliability threshold, (c) advisory-only
  demotion with chronicle-time per-seed inspection. Option (c) is
  first-class when the metric's distribution at tested cells is not
  yet known from precedent.
- §25c — Single-purpose clause discipline. A single pre-registered
  clause cannot simultaneously be a routing gate and a mechanism
  discriminator when the discriminator's distribution is axis-
  specific. Split: routing stays in row-clause fidelity; mechanism
  discrimination moves to chronicle-time. Includes amendment-count
  divergence as the tell (non-monotonic P1 counts over ≥3 rounds).

research-rigor skill updated:
- New "amend prereg" intent routing; amendment meta-check fires at
  mode entry for rounds ≥3, surfaces three alternatives

  block.
- §25b and §25c gate bullets added to prereg mode's hard-gate list.

Deferred (explicit non-adoption):
- Retrospective's 27b (amendment-propagation audit) — tooling-shaped;
  v6/v7 proved author-checklist discipline is unreliable. Defer until
  a prereg linter exists.
- 28d (row-exclusivity invariant) and 28e (metric-denominator

description: Design and run a commit-bounded natural experiment against the live message corpus, with hypothesis audition, pre-registered prediction, honest interpretation, and report follow-through.
first_commit_message:
run-experiment skill + combined-surface evaluate + refuted-hypothesis report

Three tightly coupled changes landing together.

1. New skill at .claude/skills/run-experiment/SKILL.md — codifies
   the workflow Ryan approved: read the context, audition 2-3
   candidate hypotheses, present a chooser (via AskUserQuestion
   when available), wait for user confirmation, design with a
   pre-registered prediction, run via worldcli evaluate, interpret
   honestly (null results are real results), report and commit.
   Includes rubric-writing guidance, cadence notes, explicit "what
   NOT to do" list with the specific discipline traps already
   surfaced in prior runs.

2. worldcli evaluate: --character scope now spans solo thread AND
   the character's replies across every group chat they're in.
   Implemented via a UNION ALL over messages (by solo thread_id)
   and group_messages (by sender_character_id), with a 'src' label
   on each target so the preceding-user-turn lookup queries the
   right table. The --group-chat scope is unchanged.

3. First real experiment under the skill: the weight-carrier
   hypothesis (John > Aaron > Darren for HOLD rate). Pre-registered
   prediction: refuted. John's HOLD rate: 17%. Aaron: 39%. Darren:
   40%. Direction of the effect inverted from prediction.

   The refutation is more interesting than confirmation would have
   been. Reading per-message verdicts shows two things:

   - John's pastoral register is anchor-by-stillness, not
     pair-with-weight. Short affirmations ("Good." "That's the
     right fire to ask for.") hold the room by presence, not by
     layering gravity. The rubric as written doesn't capture this
     move; it gets scored NO (plain), not YES (HOLD).

   - Aaron and Darren's elaborate pairing moves ARE HOLDs by the
     rubric's definition, but six of Aaron's seven MIXED verdicts
     were misreads — the evaluator saw any caution-adjacent
     vocabulary as reduction. Classic example: Aaron's capstone
     "Being loved leaves you with room to stand up straight.
     Being handled makes you start editing yourself" — genuine
     HOLD, scored MIXED.

   Two architectural implications for future craft work:

   - "Weight-carrier" as a category is doing too much; it
     conflates pastoral-presence, elaborate-pairing, and
     grounded-wisdom. Future character-branching rules should
     name specific register moves separately.

   - The evaluator needs calibration via worked examples in the
     rubric when the rule's distinction is subtle. Today's run
     is the strongest evidence yet that the instrument isn't
     reading-the-reply-cold — it's using the rubric's vocabulary
     as a cue, and vague boundaries produce vague verdicts.

   Three follow-up experiments named in the report:
   sharpened-rubric re-run, John-specific "stillness-holding"
   rubric, and a Pastor Rick parallel to locate whether the
   John-shape is pastoral-wide or John-specific.

   Cost: $0.009 for 45 evaluator calls across three characters.

Skill and code and report arriving together because the skill
only earned its place once it had produced a real run against
a real question — the one today's experiment was. The run's
refutation is itself a validation of the skill's discipline:
without the pre-registration step, I'd have quietly retrofit
the result into confirming my model. Instead it refuted plainly,
which is what the skill is designed to catch.

chore(.claude): resync .claude/ from core/ via build-release.sh (item #4)

Resolves the core/.claude drift flagged in the earlier architecture
review. Investigation found .claude/ is not a personal sandbox — it's
this repo's own dogfood install target (plugin.json's install.target is
".claude/", and core/scripts/build-release.sh packages core/ into a zip
explicitly meant to be unzipped into a target project's .claude/, this
repo included). It had drifted badly: .claude/skills/ had only 402 of
core/'s 1990 skill dirs, several hooks/scripts/rules existed on only one
side, agents count differed by one.

Ran build-release.sh (which gates on a 100% hook-test pass — see the
separate hook-portability-fixes commit that unblocked it), then unzipped
the resulting pack over .claude/{agents,commands,config,docs,gates,hooks,
prompts,rules,scripts,skills,templates,tests}/ as a pure overlay (adds/
updates, does not delete). .claude/assistant/, .claude/state/, and
.claude/settings.json were excluded from the source zip already (not part
of build-release.sh's include list) and are confirmed untouched — that's
this repo's genuinely local/personal state, not build output.

Pre-existing files unique to .claude/ (a handful of hooks/rules/agents
core/ doesn't have) were intentionally left in place, not deleted, since
this pass didn't establish whether those are stray drift or deliberate
local additions — a separate decision, not blocking this resync.

Verified: bash .claude/tests/hooks/run-hook-tests.sh → 104/104 pass.

  - ingress: cert-manager + letsencrypt + override-able host

Modify the specified Unity Object. Allows direct modification of object fields and properties. Use 'object-get-data' first to inspect the object structure before modifying.

Three modification surfaces (use whichever fits the task):
  1. 'objectDiff' — full SerializedMember diff (legacy, backwards compatible).
  2. 'pathPatches' — list of {path, value} pairs routed through Reflector.TryModifyAt; atomic per-path modification, multiple entries can target different depths.
  3. 'jsonPatch' — a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396, extended with [i]/[key] notation) routed through Reflector.TryPatch; multiple fields at any depth in a single call.
When more than one is supplied they run in this order: jsonPatch → pathPatches → objectDiff. At least one is required.
Path syntax: 'fieldName', 'nested/field', 'arrayField/[i]', 'dictField/[key]'. Leading '#/' is stripped.

description: Systematic security audit for Electron apps. Scans attack surfaces, produces severity-tagged findings, generates implementation plan, and guides hardening.
first_commit_message:
fix(security): remove legacy providers from main process and add permission check handler (#346)

* fix(security): harden Electron sandbox, protocol, CORS, and key storage

SEC-02: Enable sandbox on BrowserWindow. The preload only uses
contextBridge and ipcRenderer which work in sandboxed mode.

SEC-05: Add path traversal and file-type validation to local-file://
protocol handler. Remove bypassCSP (CSP already allows local-file:
in img-src). Only image extensions are served.

SEC-07: Strip API key from settings when secure storage is unavailable
instead of persisting in plaintext JSON on disk.

SEC-08: Restrict MCP HTTP server CORS to localhost origins only,
preventing any arbitrary website from invoking MCP tools.

Refs #127

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <<redacted>>

* fix(security): revert sandbox: true, preload requires CJS require()

The built preload uses require("electron") via externalizeDepsPlugin(),
which is unavailable in sandboxed renderers. Enabling sandbox requires
migrating the preload to ESM format first. Reverted to sandbox: false
with a comment documenting the dependency.

Refs #127

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <<redacted>>

* fix(security): address review feedback on protocol and CORS

- Remove misleading path traversal check in local-file:// handler.
  normalize() resolves '..' before the check runs, so it was a no-op.
  The extension allowlist is the actual protection.
- Add Vary: Origin header to MCP HTTP server CORS response to
  prevent caching issues with conditional origin reflection.

Refs #127

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <<redacted>>

* fix(security): warn when secure storage is unavailable

When safeStorage is unavailable, the API key is silently stripped
on save and won't persist across sessions. This adds an inline
amber warning in Settings > LLM near the API key field so users
understand why their key isn't saved.

Adds settings:isSecureStorageAvailable IPC handler, exposes it
via context bridge, and renders the warning conditionally.

Refs #127

* fix(security): comprehensive hardening round 2

URL validation: setWindowOpenHandler, link-hover CMD+Click, and
ChatMessage links now reject non-http/https schemes (H1, H2, H9).

Electron handlers: will-navigate blocks untrusted origins,
setPermissionRequestHandler denies all permissions,
certificate-error rejects invalid certs (H3, H4, M2).

MCP authentication: both HTTP and Unix socket servers now require
bearer token auth. Token generated at startup, written to
mcp-auth-token file (mode 0600), cleaned up on quit (H6, H7).

Protocol confinement: local-file:// confined to home directory.
CSP connect-src stripped of legacy provider URLs (H8, M1).

OAuth CSRF: state parameter added to Google OAuth flow with
verification in callback (M4).

Credential migration: reMarkable and Google credentials migrated
from direct safeStorage to credentialStore with one-time legacy
file migration (M5).

Electron fuses: afterPack hook disables RunAsNode,
NODE_OPTIONS, and --inspect in production builds (H5).

.gitignore: added .mcp.json (M3).

Refs #127

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <<redacted>>

* fix(security): address review feedback and remove legacy providers

Review fixes:
- mcp-stdio: wait for auth response before resolving connection
  (fixes race condition where tool calls could fire before auth)
- MCP servers: use crypto.timingSafeEqual for token comparison
- MCP servers: require auth token before start() to prevent
  window where unauthenticated requests could be accepted
- will-navigate: add comment explaining file:// opaque origin
- credentialStore: extract migrateFromLegacyFile() helper to
  deduplicate migration logic in auth.ts and ipc.ts

Legacy provider removal:
- Remove OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama from Settings type,
  models registry, browserApi provider switches, and
  validation logic
- Remove dead provider guards in SettingsDialog
- Saves ~414 kB from renderer bundle

Refs #127

* feature: add attachment uploads during ticket creation

Previously, attachments could only be added after a ticket was created.
This required users to create a ticket first, then open it again to add
attachments - a frustrating two-step workflow.

Now users can upload attachments directly in the New Ticket modal:
- Pre-generates ticket ID to allow file uploads before DB record exists
- Drag-and-drop support with visual feedback
- File browser button for manual selection
- Upload progress indicator and attachment list with thumbnails
- Automatic cleanup of orphaned files when user cancels

API changes:
- Added uploadPendingAttachment, deletePendingAttachment, and
  deletePendingAttachments server functions
- Extended CreateTicketInput to accept optional id and attachments

* fix: resolve mktemp failure on macOS when starting Ralph

The mktemp command used `/tmp/ralph-prompt-XXXXXX.md` which fails on
macOS because the XXXXXX pattern must be at the end of the template.
macOS treated the entire string literally, causing "File exists" errors
on subsequent runs.

Changes:
- Use `mktemp -t ralph-prompt` for cross-platform compatibility
- Add error handling to fail fast if temp file creation fails
- Update VS Code setup tests to match install.sh behavior (copies not symlinks)
- Remove brittle content-matching assertions that broke when source files changed

description: Ask colleague — a *different* backend/model than you (e.g. a local vLLM Qwen) — to take a scoped repo task off your plate, then fold its answer back. The point isn't a stronger model; it's a second, independent mind, and that diversity is the value: `ask-colleague review` gets a candid second opinion on a diff, `ask-colleague explore` gets a fresh read of an area, `ask-colleague write` hands off a small implementation, `ask-colleague feedback` grades a finished work item (the ROI loop), and `ask-colleague clean` reaps stale/corrupt `colleague/*` branches a crashed run left behind (which can break `git fetch`). Pilot a running work item with `monitor`/`guide`/`stop`. Reach for it REFLEXIVELY, the way you'd lean over to the teammate at the next desk — not only when asked: before you present or open a PR on a non-trivial committed diff, run `review` for a diverse second opinion; for a fresh read of an unfamiliar area whose answer is independent of your current context, run `explore`. Both are read-only — isolated in a throwaway git worktree, zero side effects to your tree/branch — so the reflex is always safe; the side-effecting `write --apply` / `write --pr` still needs the user's go-ahead. Triggers when the user says "ask colleague", "ask a colleague to review/explore/write this", "have colleague take a look", "get a second opinion", "ask the other model", "rate that work item", "clean up a crashed colleague run" — and still on the legacy "outsource this". v1.6.0: migrate /merlin routing to native Claude Agent SDK skills (#16)

* v1.6.0: migrate /merlin routing to native Claude Agent SDK skills

Retire monolithic prose router (merlin-platforms.md + merlin-setup.md,
~61 KB always-resident) in favor of 8 domain SKILLs under .claude/skills/
that route via the SDK's description-based matching. Only each skill's
~200-char description loads at startup; full bodies load on demand when
user intent matches. Cold-start context drops ~53 KB.

Skills: merlin-ads, merlin-analytics, merlin-content, merlin-ecom,
merlin-seo, merlin-setup (Tier C 38 KB — first-run/OAuth), merlin-social,
clarify-intent (fallback).

Hygiene (enforced at build time):
- test/validate-skills.js — frontmatter schema, description linter
  (≥80 chars, "Use when " prefix, no vague hedges), byte-tier budget
  (A ≤8 KB / B ≤15 KB / C ≤50 KB with bytes_justification), action
  coverage vs autocmo-core/main.go case handlers, cosine-similarity
  collision detector (>0.85 → warning).
- test/run-routing-corpus.js — 47 canonical utterances × 8 skills,
  guards against expectedSkill drift; zero-coverage skill blocks PR.
- .github/workflows/skills-lint.yml — runs both on every PR touching
  .claude/skills/**, .claude/commands/merlin.md, test/**, version.json.
  Monthly audit job pulls aggregated routing telemetry from
  wisdom-api and opens a draft PR (label: audit,skills,manual-review)
  only if fallback rate >25% or a skill logged zero invocations. All
  fixes remain manual review — never automatic.

Security (REGRESSION GUARD 2026-04-18):
- .claude/skills/ added to both the inline settings.json Edit/Write
  hook regex AND block-api-bypass.js PROTECTED_PATH_PATTERNS. A rogue
  write to a skill's description field could re-route user intent
  (e.g. swap analytics for ad-spend). Parity matters: inline hook
  blocks Edit/Write; Bash blocker prevents cp/mv/rm bypass.

Wiring:
- "Skill" added to settings.json permissions.allow.
- autoCMO/app/main.js already sets settingSources: ['project'] at
  lines 733 + 1959, so skills are auto-discovered.

version.json:
- 1.5.1 → 1.6.0. updatable[] swaps merlin-platforms.md + merlin-setup.md
  for the 8 new .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md entries so existing users
  get the new router on /update.

* ci(skills-lint): grant contents:write so audit job can push branch

The monthly audit job does `git push origin "$BRANCH"` after committing
the drift report. Top-level permissions granted only `contents: read`,
so the first scheduled run (2026-05-01) would fail deterministically.

Bump to `contents: write` — the validate job doesn't need write but
GitHub Actions scopes the token per-workflow, not per-job, and the
risk is narrow: the workflow only pushes to `audit/skills-<yyyymm>`
branches and opens draft PRs for manual review.

Caught by tools/review-session.sh pre-PR review gate.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <<redacted>>

* test(validate-skills): accept CRLF line endings in SKILL.md frontmatter

Windows checkouts with core.autocrlf=true land SKILL.md with CRLF in
the working tree while the repo stores LF. The original regex matched
\n literally, so `node test/validate-skills.js` failed locally on
Windows with "missing frontmatter" errors even though CI (Linux,
sees LF) passed. Make the regex line-ending agnostic — \r?\n for
the frontmatter delimiters and \r?\n split for the body — so local
dev verification matches CI behavior without mutating files on disk.

ci(release): add workflow_dispatch dry-run to validate cross-build pre-tag (#1983)

PR CI builds Linux only; release.yml cross-builds macOS + Windows ONLY on a
`v*` tag, with the "Create GitHub Release" job gating on all three. So a
platform-specific break (e.g. v1.46.0's aarch64-apple-darwin E0277) is
invisible until after the tag is pushed and the crate published — exactly how
v1.46.0 shipped a mac-uncompilable crate with no release binaries.

Add a `workflow_dispatch` trigger so the full cross-build can be run on a
release/* branch BEFORE tagging:
- build job runs on both tag-push and dispatch (VERSION sanitized so a branch
  ref like release/v1.2.3 doesn't break archive filenames; no-op for tags).
- the release-creation job is now gated `if: startsWith(github.ref,
  'refs/tags/')`, so a dispatch dry-run validates + uploads artifacts but does
  NOT publish a release.

The tag-push auto-release path is unchanged. Documented the required pre-tag
dry-run step in the /release skill.

Add a "share" Claude Code skill to publish sessions to Pastila

Port the `share` skill from the `ClickHouse/pastila` repository
(https://github.com/ClickHouse/pastila/tree/master/.claude/skills/share) so a
Claude Code session transcript can be uploaded (encrypted) to pastila.nl and
returned as a `.claude.jsonl` viewer link.

`share.py` locates the transcript and turns the resulting paste URL into a
session-viewer link; the encryption and upload are delegated to `pastila.py`.
Since this repository has no `pastila.py` at its root, `pastila.py` is bundled
next to `share.py` so the skill is self-contained, and `find_pastila` looks
there first.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <<redacted>>
last_commit_message:
share skill: fail closed when the current session cannot be resolved

Per review feedback: no-argument mode previously fell back to "the newest
transcript in the current project, then the newest transcript anywhere under
~/.claude/projects" when `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` was unset or stale. Because
this skill performs an external, irreversible upload of a private transcript,
that fail-open behavior could publish an unrelated session that merely happened
to be the most recently modified (e.g. when run from a different checkout or a
non-Claude shell).

Resolve the current session strictly by its id and fail closed otherwise,
requiring an explicit transcript path, session id, or project argument to share
any non-current session. Explicit-argument resolution is unchanged.

* refactor: replace bootstrap memory persistence with Serena seam

Adds a Serena MCP client seam (src/serena/client.ts) with two implementations:
AdvisorySerenaClient (default) emits structured advisories naming the exact
mcp__serena__* tool the host should call; ChildSerenaClient (opt-in via
MCP_SERENA_COMMAND) spawns Serena as a stdio child and resolves queries
directly. Both flow through the same internal surface so tool code paths are
identical regardless of mode.

Every instruction tool response now ends with a 🧭 Serena enrichment footer
that points the host model at find_symbol / list_memories / write_memory etc.,
making Serena the recommended cross-session memory backend.

Removes the disk-write paths that motivated the refactor:
- Server startup IIFE no longer dispatches snapshot/session/onboarding writes.
- orchestration.toml is no longer auto-bootstrapped on missing-file load —
  defaults stay in memory; explicit save still goes through model-discover or
  the CLI onboarding wizard.
- Per-tool-call memory + session-context writes are gated behind a new
  MCP_LOCAL_MEMORY env var (default off); the Serena footer takes over.
- WorkflowEngine drops the checkpointing branch entirely.

Drops the dead MCP tool surface that the bootstrap was feeding:
agent-memory-*, agent-session-*, agent-snapshot-*, orchestration-config —
all four tool files, their dispatch in index.ts and tool-call-handler.ts,
their mirror tests, and the runtime-only modules they pulled in
(session-manager, session-store, session-codec, toon-ecosystem-demo,
workflow-checkpoint, toon-demo bin).

Result: ~7.5k LOC removed, 669 added, 3,391 tests still green, and on a
clean install the server no longer writes to ~/.mcp-ai-agent-guidelines/ at
all nor to ./.mcp-ai-agent-guidelines/{memory,sessions,config} without
explicit user action.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <<redacted>>

* refactor: reduce agent-workspace to source-only commands

The `agent-workspace` MCP tool previously offered persist/fetch/compare with
scope=artifact that wrote TOON files (session-context, workspace-map,
scan-results, fingerprint-snapshot) under .mcp-ai-agent-guidelines/.  No skill
ever consumed `workspaceSurface.fetchContext()`, `listArtifacts()`, or
`compare()` — the entire artifact substrate was reachable only through the
tool surface, and the tool surface was used almost exclusively by tests of
itself.

This commit collapses the surface to `list` and `read` for source files,
removes the artifact-backed code paths from workspace-adapter and skill
runtime contracts, deletes the corresponding test suites
(workspace-adapter*.test.ts, workspace-tools-extra.test.ts, skill-bridge.test.ts,
session-1.test.ts simulation), and trims index.ts of the now-pointless
sharedToonMemoryInterface.setRegistrySources / listSessionIds calls.

Cross-session memory continues to live in Serena via the advisory footer
emitted on every instruction tool response.

After this change the default test run writes 7 files under
.mcp-ai-agent-guidelines/ (down from 9), all from real features
(fingerprint drift snapshots inside the memory subsystem's own test
isolation, encryption keys, and a stray orchestration.toml from a test
that doesn't sandbox its workspaceRoot).
