description:
The always-on Genie pause for ad-hoc commands. Lighter than /divecode-prd —
no PRD file required. Takes any user request ("build me a thing", "fix this
bug", "add caching here") and runs three Genie questions before any code is
generated:
  1. What you literally asked for is X — confirm.
  2. Things you didn't specify but X depends on: A, B, C.
  3. Specify those now, or grant X literally and accept the consequences?

Pattern packs supply A, B, C — same trigger matcher as /divecode-prd, just
fed the user's ad-hoc request instead of a PRD file. Use when the user
drops a one-line or paragraph-long command and you're tempted to just
execute it.

description:
Use this skill when the engineer has decided that an `acknowledged` (or `open`) kernel-fit finding warrants a kernel change captured as an ADR. The Skill seeds the finding's Evidence + Kernel surface + Proposed direction into an ADR Context section and routes through `/hstack:adr-new --from-kernel-fit <id> --slug <slug>`, where `spec-author` runs the normal Nygard interview — the human gate the kernel's "AI writes, humans confirm" contract requires at the kernel-modification layer. After the ADR lands, the Skill writes the reciprocal `promoted-to` back-reference on the finding and flips it to `status: promoted`. Two commits in v1 — the ADR commit (from `adr-new`) and the back-reference commit (from this Skill); see Failure modes for the recoverable-two-commit carve-out (analogous to the `/hstack:finalize` in-progress carve-out). Examples:

<example>
Context: The engineer reviewed KF-0001 (KF-P1, Category-A claim spans production paths), acknowledged it via triage last week, and now wants to land an ADR tightening the SP-13 guidance.
user: "/hstack:kernel-fit-promote KF-0001 --slug sp-13-prose-guidance-tightening"
assistant: "I'll read KF-0001, verify status (open or acknowledged), construct the ADR Context seed from Evidence + Kernel surface + Proposed direction, and invoke `/hstack:adr-new --from-kernel-fit KF-0001 --slug sp-13-prose-guidance-tightening`. spec-author runs the Nygard interview — Title, Status, Context (seeded), Decision, Consequences (with the challenge prompt), Alternatives Considered. After the ADR lands at terminal status, I'll write `promoted-to: adr:ADR-NNNN-...` on KF-0001, flip status to `promoted`, append a Triage Log entry, and commit. The ADR commit and the back-reference commit are separate — see Failure modes for the recoverable carve-out."
<commentary>
The promote Skill is the only path that elevates a kernel-fit finding to an ADR. The kernel's "AI writes, humans confirm" contract is preserved because `/hstack:adr-new`'s spec-author interview is the human gate; the engineer reviews and confirms every Nygard section before the ADR lands. The promote Skill itself performs no field-level interview — it is a mechanical wrapper plus a reciprocal back-reference write per ADR-0001.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: The engineer wants to route a finding to tech-debt instead of an ADR — the kernel surface is not yet ready for revision but the team wants to track the gap.
user: "/hstack:kernel-fit-promote KF-0004 --target tech-debt --slug halt-enum-missing-figma-mcp-case"
assistant: "I'll route through `/hstack:tech-debt-new --from-kernel-fit KF-0004 --slug halt-enum-missing-figma-mcp-case`. spec-author runs the six-section TD interview (Title, Why we took the shortcut, What it costs us, Fix sketch, Pre-conditions, Acceptance). After the TD lands, I'll write `promoted-to: tech-debt:TD-NNNN-...` on KF-0004 and flip status to `promoted`."
<commentary>
The `--target tech-debt` flag is the secondary promotion path — useful when the engineer recognizes the kernel-fit gap but does not yet have a defensible Decision section for an ADR. Tech-debt captures "we know about this; here's what fixing it would look like; here's what's blocking us from fixing it now." Same reciprocal write contract as the ADR path.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: A scan-Skill run between `/hstack:kernel-fit-promote` invocations has superseded the finding the engineer is now trying to promote.
user: "/hstack:kernel-fit-promote KF-0001 --slug internal-tooling-split"
assistant: "I'll halt — KF-0001 is at `status: superseded` (`superseded-by: KF-0007`). Promote KF-0007 instead; its body restates the same pattern with newer evidence. The promote Skill never promotes a superseded finding because the audit trail would route the ADR back to a stale body."
<commentary>
Promote refuses on terminal-from-promote statuses (`promoted`, `dismissed`, `superseded`, `archived`). The Skill is conservative — re-running on a superseded finding would write the back-reference on the wrong artifact and the audit trail would skew. The engineer's recovery is to promote the superseding finding.
</commentary>
</example>
first_commit_message:
feat(kernel-fit): closed-loop system for detecting kernel-vs-practice drift

Five-layer post-hoc system that observes hstack usage and surfaces kernel
gaps as durable findings — without auto-modifying the kernel. The user
explicitly required a human gate on every promotion to an ADR.

- L1 Detection: `scripts/telemetry/insights/kernel_fit.py` with three
  starter patterns (KF-P1 internal-tooling conflation, KF-P2 halt-reason
  cluster, KF-P3 missed-gate recovery). Pure read; reconstructible from
  git + frontmatter.
- L2 Synthesis: new `kernel-fit-analyst` subagent (model: opus). Loads
  kernel + shipped artifacts + prior findings; explicitly NOT implementer
  transcripts (same rule as adversarial-reviewer). Mandatory two-bullet
  counter-explanation; auto-downgrades confidence to low if absent.
- L3 Artifact: `templates/kernel-fit-finding.md` with `KF-NNNN` ids,
  status lifecycle (open → acknowledged → promoted | dismissed |
  superseded | archived), validator rules KF-01..KF-05.
- L4 Skills: `/hstack:kernel-fit-scan` (detection + synthesis + Slack),
  `/hstack:kernel-fit-triage` (mechanical status flip per ADR-0001),
  `/hstack:kernel-fit-promote` (routes to /hstack:adr-new with the
  finding's Evidence + Kernel Surface + Proposed Direction as Context
  seed; spec-author runs the Nygard interview — the human gate).
- L5 Notification: Slack via MCP, threshold-gated (medium/high only),
  14-day dedup, graceful degradation when MCP unreachable.

Kernel integration: new `## How hstack improves itself` section before
`## References`; new `kernel-fit-analyst` entry in the subagent
load-at-session-start list; `promoted-from-kernel-fit: []` field added
to adr.md template (schema-version bump 1 -> 2) so reciprocity is
mechanically checkable.

Wiring: new `kernel-fit/` entry in `src/manifest.ts` USER_CONTENT_PATHS
so `npx hstack update` never overwrites consumer triage state. New
Skills propagate via per-skill symlinks; new subagent propagates via
dir-level symlink. `/hstack:adr-new` gains `--from-kernel-fit` flag
mirroring the existing `--from-research` pattern.

v1 honesty: detector patterns are hand-written Python rules;
`validate-spec.ts` is still a placeholder so KF-01..KF-05 are
bypassable via direct frontmatter edit until it ships; the promote
two-commit pattern is documented as a recoverable carve-out
analogous to /hstack:finalize in-progress.

See ADR-0003 for the design rationale.
last_commit_message:
chore(kernel-fit): reconcile with PR #5 (enables schema split)

Three reconciliations needed after merging origin/main:

1. ADR renumbering. PR #5 introduced its own ADR-0003
   (category-b-enables-field); our ADR-0003 renamed to ADR-0004.
   ~12 references updated across kernel, Skills, subagent, template,
   render, and the ADR body itself.

2. KF-P1 retargeted to the post-PR-#5 schema. The old trigger was
   "internal-tooling: true + no user-stories" — closed structurally by
   PR #5's SP-09 expansion. New trigger: "internal-tooling: true +
   production-path in-scope + empty enables" — catches the engineer
   mis-classifying Category B as Category A. Pattern renamed:
   internal-tooling-conflates-categories → category-a-claim-spans-production-paths.

   stripping leading dots from `.github/` and similar; replaced with a
   literal `./` prefix strip).

3. ADR-0004 Alternatives Considered rewritten. Option A was framed as
   "rejected" because the original framing was "which one fix?"; PR #5
   shipped Option A while we built Option C. Both shipping is the right
   answer: A closes one named case, C ships the general detector that
   catches future cases of the same shape (including the post-PR-#5
   failure mode KF-P1 now targets). Context section updated with a
   "Status update (post-PR-#5)" paragraph.

Resolves the core/.claude drift flagged in the earlier architecture
review. Investigation found .claude/ is not a personal sandbox — it's
this repo's own dogfood install target (plugin.json's install.target is
".claude/", and core/scripts/build-release.sh packages core/ into a zip
explicitly meant to be unzipped into a target project's .claude/, this
repo included). It had drifted badly: .claude/skills/ had only 402 of
core/'s 1990 skill dirs, several hooks/scripts/rules existed on only one
side, agents count differed by one.

Ran build-release.sh (which gates on a 100% hook-test pass — see the
separate hook-portability-fixes commit that unblocked it), then unzipped
the resulting pack over .claude/{agents,commands,config,docs,gates,hooks,
prompts,rules,scripts,skills,templates,tests}/ as a pure overlay (adds/
updates, does not delete). .claude/assistant/, .claude/state/, and
.claude/settings.json were excluded from the source zip already (not part
of build-release.sh's include list) and are confirmed untouched — that's
this repo's genuinely local/personal state, not build output.

Pre-existing files unique to .claude/ (a handful of hooks/rules/agents
core/ doesn't have) were intentionally left in place, not deleted, since
this pass didn't establish whether those are stray drift or deliberate
local additions — a separate decision, not blocking this resync.

Verified: bash .claude/tests/hooks/run-hook-tests.sh → 104/104 pass.

* fix(worktree): make WorktreeCreate hook actually create the worktree

The WorktreeCreate hook replaces git's worktree creation: it must create
the worktree and print its path on stdout. We had bootstrap.sh wired in,
which creates nothing and only installs deps + syncs the wiki, so the
harness read bootstrap's last stdout line ("pull: up to date") as the
worktree path and failed to chdir into it. This also broke agent and
workflow `isolation: "worktree"`, which use the same hook.

payload, create the worktree under the primary checkout's
.claude/worktrees/, base it on origin/<base> to match the `fresh` baseRef
default, run bootstrap.sh for setup with all output on stderr, tear down a
half-built worktree on setup failure, and print only the path on stdout.
Point WorktreeCreate at it; SessionStart keeps calling bootstrap.sh.

description: Symbiote react-native-import testability — read BEFORE writing any NEW file in core/engine, core/components, or an adapter (adapters/react|vue|angular) that imports from 'react-native' directly (processColor, DeviceEventEmitter, Image, AppRegistry, a deep RN internal path, etc.), or before adding a new package.json 'exports' subpath, or when a Vitest run throws 'RolldownError: Parse failure: Flow is not supported' / 'Cannot find package react-native'. Covers: (1) WHY — react-native's own source is Flow syntax; Vitest's Rolldown/Vite transform cannot parse it, so a file that imports 'react-native' must stay OUTSIDE every package's main index.ts barrel and outside anything a test transitively imports. (2) THE PATTERN — export such a file via a separate package.json 'exports' subpath (precedent: './metro-css-parser', './runtime-helpers', './bootstrap') instead of the main barrel; Metro resolves these subpaths fine (unstable_enablePackageExports is on by default in this repo's metro-config). (3) THE TEST RECIPE — vi.mock('react-native', factory) (+ any deep RN subpath actually imported) fully shields a module under test, verified empirically. (4) UNTYPED DEEP RN IMPORTS — use a local `// @ts-expect-error` comment at the import site (existing precedent: adapters/react/src/create-portal.ts, host-config.ts, render.ts), NOT a standalone ambient .d.ts file — an ambient declare-module shim silently fails to be picked up by a DIFFERENT package's separate TypeScript program (e.g. the Angular adapter's own ngc compile), because ambient declarations are only visible within the SAME tsconfig 'include' set, not merely 'reachable via import chain'. (5) a new package may not inherit @types/node (process/console) resolution the way a sibling package does — verify with a real tsc build, add an explicit 'types': ['node'] to that package's tsconfig.json if it doesn't. For the Angular-specific twist on subpath exports (conditional exports shape, ngc/AOT), see angular-adapter-build instead. For workspace: vs catalog: protocol on @symbiote-native/* deps, see symbiote-dependency-catalog.

agents(kira): scaffold Tier 1 docs skills + name them in identity

Tier 1 of kira's docs-maintenance skill set:

- docs-validate (0.1.0) — runs the same markdownlint + Prettier
  toolchain CI uses; applies safe auto-fixes; reports remaining
  diagnostics for memory-log.
- docs-links (0.1.0) — validates internal markdown links,
  anchors, and cross-doc references. Auto-fixes when git-rename
  history makes the new target unambiguous; otherwise logs to
  deferred-findings memory.
- docs-scan (0.1.0) — top-level orchestrator. Verifies source
  presence (stands down if absent — iris's domain), pins git
  identity, runs each focused skill, commits per category so the
  log stays bisectable, then publishes via git-push.

Each skill is split rather than fused into one mega-skill so:
  * lint and link-checking can be invoked independently for
    one-offs;
  * autonomy can be dialed per category as Tier 2 (docs-verify,
    docs-consistency) lands;
  * the runtime profiles diverge (lint = fast/deterministic,
    link-checking = slower) and shouldn't be conflated.

Two identity touchups so kira's mental model resolves correctly:

  * CLAUDE.md responsibility 2 now names docs-scan as the entry
    point + lists the subordinate skills (mirrors iris's pattern
    of naming skills in her responsibilities).
  * agent-card.md drops the stale "handed to iris" phrasing —
    kira publishes her own batches via git-push now.

Tier 2 (docs-verify, docs-consistency) is deliberately not in
this commit; sequence those after Tier 1 has a track record.

first_commit_message:
feat(platform-integrations): add provenance usage audits (#251)

* feat(platform-integrations): add provenance usage audits

Restores and extends the PR 239 usage-provenance flow on top of the unified plugin source.

Adds offline provenance analysis for recalled guidelines, stores trajectories for the supported harnesses, and adds Docker e2e coverage for Claude and Codex learn/recall/provenance flows.

The audit path now writes recall and influence events under the configured EVOLVE_DIR instead of deriving a parent project root, so custom evolve data directories keep recall, entities, and provenance together. Influence writes are also idempotent per session/entity so rerunning provenance does not double-count usage.

* fix(subscribe): roll back clone and config when audit append fails

Addresses review feedback from visahak

Restores the all-or-nothing contract: if audit_append raises after a
successful clone + config save, the new repo entry and cloned directory
are removed before exiting non-zero with a "failed to record subscription"
diagnostic on stderr. Previously the command swallowed the failure and
reported success, leaving the clone and config mutation in place even
though tests and callers expect rollback on partial failure.

* fix(subscribe): persist config rollback when audit append fails

Addresses review feedback from visahak

The previous commit popped the repo entry from the in-memory list but
did not call set_repos(cfg, repos), so the subsequent save_config call
re-wrote the same state to disk and the config still contained the new
subscription. Update the in-memory cfg before the compensating
save_config and align the codex-sharing test, which previously expected
the old warn-and-succeed behavior, with the all-or-nothing contract
asserted by test_rolls_back_clone_if_audit_write_fails.

* fix(sync): emit invalid-subscription rejections on stderr

Addresses review feedback from visahak

Rejected subscription entries (invalid names, missing remotes, unknown
scopes) and path-traversal guard trips were being folded into the
stdout "Synced N repo(s):" summary, making diagnostics indistinguishable
from normal sync output and breaking the platform-integration tests
that assert diagnostics appear on stderr. Route each rejection through
stderr instead and exclude rejected entries from the stdout summary
count.

* fix(save-trajectory): embed session_id in trajectory filename for provenance

Addresses review feedback from visahak

The provenance skill advertised deterministic session-to-trajectory
matching via session_id, but save-trajectory wrote files as
trajectory_<timestamp>.json with no persisted session identifier, so
two back-to-back codex sessions produced indistinguishable files and
the e2e test had to pass the target session id in through the prompt.

Extend the envelope to include session_id (Step 4 of save-trajectory)
and thread that id into the output filename as
trajectory_<timestamp>_<session-id>.json so provenance can resolve a
recall event to exactly one trajectory by inspecting the filename.
The filename slice is sanitised to filesystem-safe characters and
capped at 64 chars. When no session id is available the filename
falls back to the original trajectory_<timestamp>.json form.

Provenance SKILL Step 2 now documents a three-step matching strategy
(claude transcript filename; session-id suffix on trajectory files;
envelope session_id field as a last resort) so agents do not have to
guess from content alone.

* fix(subscribe): warn on rollback save_config failure instead of silently swallowing

Addresses CodeRabbit review finding: Silent rollback-save failure leaves config and filesystem inconsistent

The compensating save_config call in the audit-failure rollback path
previously swallowed every exception with a bare `except Exception:
pass`, which could leave the on-disk evolve.config.yaml still listing
the freshly-added repo even though the clone was removed. Print a
clear stderr warning that names th

* feat(platform-integrations): detect silently-disabled Claude EVOLVE.md import

Claude's CLAUDE.md @import needs a one-time per-project approval; a declined

description:
AST-grounded PR / diff review. One workflow → per-file risk ranking, blast
radius per changed symbol, the exact pytest command to gate merge, any
architecture-constraint violations, and a final BLOCK / REVIEW / APPROVE
verdict — in ~1–2k tokens and 4–6 MCP calls.

Goes beyond a generic LLM diff-read because only TSA's `edit action=impact`
returns a deterministic `verification_command` + `queue_ledger`, and only the
persisted call graph can enumerate true callers/callees of changed symbols.
(Per `docs/internal/COMPETITOR_HEAD_TO_HEAD_2026-05-23.md`: CodeGraphContext
silently indexes 0 files, grep-ast crashes on Python 3.14, wrale miscounts
imports. A pure-LLM diff reader has none of these guard-rails — it cannot
reach the AST cache to enumerate callers, cannot consult
`architectural-constraints.yml`, and invents a pytest command instead of
reading the one TSA computed.)

feat(skills): ui-* design posture family + ui-bakeoff orchestrator

Replace the single ui-design skill with a family of UI-design posture skills,
each producing a deliberately different *type* of result so the trigger picks
the approach:

- ui-sharp     lean, inviting, trust-your-taste refresh (everyday default)
- ui-reimagine bold from-scratch reinvention; highest variance / idea generator
- ui-refine    improve what exists without reinventing; safest, most consistent
- ui-dense     max information density + hierarchy; power-user / admin
- ui-bakeoff   orchestrator: runs the four in parallel, then pick + graft winner

Shared floor (.claude/ui-skills/shared/): ground-rules.md + design-system-anchors.md.
Each posture carries a short targeted interview (asked in prose) hitting its own
blind spot; ui-bakeoff runs the merged interview once up front since subagents
can't ask the user, then injects answers.

Hard rule across all: BUILD IT REAL, never fake — no mock data / stubbed buttons /
fake streams for real feature work; handle the real loading/empty/error/stalled
-stream paths a mock hides.

Removes superseded .claude/skills/ui-design and .claude/ui-design-bakeoff.

first_commit_message:
refactor: Claude Code Skills構造のリファクタリング (#165)

* 作成しました。これで `/self-review` コマンドが使えるようになります。

## 使い方

```bash
/self-review
```

## スキルの内容

1. **変更内容の確認** - git diff で何を変更したか確認
2. **ローカルCI実行** - テスト、lint、型チェック
3. **コードレビュー観点チェック** - 機能性、エラーハンドリング、セキュリティなど
4. **プロジェクト規約チェック** - Canonical Pattern、ドキュメント更新
5. **よくある指摘パターンの事前防止** - 未使用import、console.log残りなど

## カスタマイズ

このファイル（`.claude/commands/self-review.md`）を編集することで、プロジェクト固有のチェック項目を追加できます。例えば：

- 特定のファイルパターンのチェック
- 特定のAPIやライブラリの使用ルール
- チーム固有のコーディング規約

必要に応じて内容を調整してください。

* 完了しました。以下が変更内容のサマリーです。

## 変更内容

### CLAUDE.md
- **316行 → 93行**に削減（約70%削減）
- 最小限のプロジェクト情報のみ残す
- ワークフロールールはスキルへの参照に変更

### 新しいスキル構造

```
.claude/skills/
├── self-review/SKILL.md    # コード自己検証（Use proactively after code changes）
├── update-docs/SKILL.md    # ドキュメント更新
├── create-pr/SKILL.md      # PR作成
├── add-test/SKILL.md       # テスト追加
├── fix-bug/SKILL.md        # バグ修正
├── add-feature/SKILL.md    # 新機能追加
├── add-block/SKILL.md      # ブロック追加
└── review-pr/SKILL.md      # PRレビュー待機
```

### スキルの自動選択

各スキルの`description`に適切なトリガーワードを含めたため、Claudeは：

1. コード変更完了後 → `self-review`を自動選択
2. ドキュメント更新が必要な変更時 → `update-docs`を自動選択
3. PR作成時 → `create-pr`を自動選択
4. バグ修正依頼時 → `fix-bug`を自動選択

### 削除したもの

- `.claude/commands/` ディレクトリ（`.claude/skills/`に移行）

* 完了しました。最終的な構造をまとめます。

---

## 完成した構造

### 変更サマリー

| 項目 | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| CLAUDE.md | 93行 | **50行** |
| ルール | CLAUDE.md内に混在 | `.claude/rules/`に分離 |
| スキル | `.claude/commands/` | `.claude/skills/` |
| コンテキスト効率 | 全ルール常時ロード | パス固有ルールは条件ロード |

### ファイル構造

feat: unified shell gate — one content-based runner, dogfooded (#348) (#356)

The lint gate was three divergent implementations (pre-commit glob+exclude,
CI shebang-filter, verify-fleet --all-files) that disagreed, and release
shipped tools it never linted with the config it also ships. Result: the
gh-task-status Python shim broke consumers' shellcheck (SC1071), and per-file
exclude patching never landed cleanly across lefthook modes.

First cut (shellcheck), per docs/proposals/unified-gate.lex:
- templates/commons/bin/check-shell: the single runner. Selects shell by
  CONTENT (shebang / .sh|.bash, vendored share/ exempt), never path glob, so
  non-shell files under bin/ (the shim, Dockerfiles) fall out structurally and
  in every invocation mode.
- commons lefthook shellcheck step now calls `bin/check-shell {staged_files}`
  — no glob/exclude gymnastics. Mode-invariant.
- Release DOGFOODS it: the templates-bin CI job runs check-shell over its own
  distributed tools; a gate-unified.bats dogfood runs it over a synced fixture
  (shim skipped, real tools pass). A distributed-tool lint bug is caught at the
  source, not at N consumers.
- release-sync-tests installs shellcheck so the dogfood runs.

Tests: check-shell behavior (lint real shell, skip shim/Dockerfile/vendored,
follow symlinks) + the synced dogfood. engine-distribution test updated for the
new wiring.

Part of #348.

Make JSON Schema test-suite generator emit OS-independent fixtures (#801)

* test(jsonschema): make the test-suite generator emit OS-independent fixtures

The Corvus.JsonSchemaTestSuite.CodeGenerator emitted MSTest fixtures whose
embedded literals depended on the host OS, so regenerating on Linux vs Windows
produced ~650 spurious diffs and made the suite un-regeneratable off Windows:

- Embedded virtual paths used the OS separator (Path.GetRelativePath/Path.Combine)
  -> tests\\draft... on Windows vs tests/draft... on Linux. Now normalised to '/'
  via EmbeddedLiteral.ForwardSlash (the runtime helpers normalise separators anyway,
  so this is source-only and behaviour-neutral).
- Embedded schema/instance JSON carried the submodule files' line endings
  (\r\n on a Windows checkout vs \n on Linux). Now normalised to LF via
  EmbeddedLiteral.Json.
- The annotation generator embedded an *absolute* remotes path (the runner's machine
  path, e.g. D:\source\...), via Program.cs Path.GetFullPath. It now resolves an
  absolute path only for reading and embeds the same relative remotes path as the
  type/evaluator generators.

Also: update-json-schema-test-suite.ps1 ran the generator via a Windows-only
'.exe'; it now uses 'dotnet <dll>' so the script works on every OS. The
corvus-test-suite-regeneration skill is corrected (right output projects + run
command + a note on the now-deterministic output); catalog refreshed.

Regeneration is now idempotent and byte-identical across operating systems.

semantics change. The submodule is NOT bumped (the JSON-Schema-Test-Suite update

## 5 つの Hooks (settings.json で自動定義)

| Hook | 動作 |
|------|------|
| PostToolUse (Edit/Write) | Python ファイル編集後に ruff format + check --fix を自動適用 |
| PreToolUse (Bash) | force push、--no-verify、/data/piper 削除等の危険コマンドをブロック |
| UserPromptSubmit | "PR 作成"/"コミット"/"学習開始"等のキーワードで CLAUDE.md ルールをリマインド |
| Stop | セッション終了時に未コミット変更を 1 回だけ警告 |

| Skill | 用途 |
|-------|------|
| /precheck [scope] | lint + format + test 一括実行 (scope: python/rust/cs/go/js/cpp/all) |
| /check-pr-ready | PR 作成前の最終チェック (lint/test/docs/CHANGELOG/未コミット) |
| /commit | CLAUDE.md 準拠のコミット (--no-verify 禁止、HEREDOC、prefix 強制) |

checks whether an agent following a flagship skill produces correct, referee-proof
empirical work.

evals/ — rubric harness (stdlib only: tomllib + json + re)
  - run_evals.py: lint (CI gate) / --grade / --judge-prompts modes
  - lib/checks.py: machine-checkable primitives (regex_any/all/none, count,
    word/char count, numeric tolerance/sign) + manual items routed to a judge
  - 8 scenarios over 6 flagship skills (StatsPAI staggered-DiD/weak-IV/RDD,
    AER abstract-100w/identification/submission, mixtape TWFE trap, zh de-AIGC),
    each pinned to verified skill content
  - _example fixtures prove the grader discriminates: the deliberately weak
    weak-IV answer is gated (21%, 3 required fails); good answers pass

benchmark/ — reproducible LaLonde recovery (pure stdlib, no numpy/pandas)
  - golds computed from the vendored data: naive ATT -$635, 5/8 covariates
    |SMD|>0.25, OLS-adjusted ATT +$1,548 near the +$1,794 experimental benchmark
  - checker recomputes data-derived golds each run; a fabricated balance/effect
    table fails the honest-reported-numbers cross-check (2/15)

(runnable via `python3 -m unittest`, also pytest-compatible).

    count, word/char count, numeric tolerance/sign, section scoping, errors)
  - test_eval_scenarios: all shipped scenarios validate; validator catches
    malformed scenarios; grader gates the weak-IV fixture and passes good ones
  - test_benchmark: golden-value regression (naive -635, adjusted +1548, SMDs)

  - test_repo_tools: frontmatter parser + catalog/provenance/audit freshness
    and validate-repo clean (mirrors `make validate`)

  no pip), complementing validate-catalog.yml

Also fixes a file-handle leak in benchmark/lib/lalonde.load.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <<redacted>>

* fix(catalog): detect YAML frontmatter after the vendored HTML comment banner

The catalog/audit/validate parsers required `---` on line 1, so they missed the
frontmatter on every vendored skill whose file opens with the CoPaper.AI
provenance banner (`<!-- ... -->`). That mislabeled 32 skills as "missing
frontmatter / missing description" in the catalog and search index.

frontmatter upstream); 28 skills regain real name/description in the catalog,
audit, and search. Regenerated catalog/skills.json, skill-audit.json, and the
rendered docs. Adds regression tests for the banner case.

last_commit_message:
feat(spacing): closed spacing-role vocabulary + design-lint enforcement

The consistency "engine" was missing two halves: spacing wasn't a closed set
of named roles (raw gap-2/px-1.5/p-1 scattered across components, each an
unenforced, illegible decision about whether it scales with density), and
nothing prevented drift. This adds both.

Vocabulary (src/app.css) — every spacing is now a role that encodes air (scales
with --density) vs fixed:
- gap tiers gap-tight/field/group/section (reusable on any flex OR grid, any
  axis); stack-* refactored to flex-col + a tier.
- pad-box(+-x/-y) air box inset; pad-control-x/-sm and pad-chrome-y as NAMED
  fixed roles, so a control's own padding and a chrome bar read as deliberately
  fixed, not a forgotten air role.

Enforcement — scripts/audit/design-lint.js (pnpm lint:design) bans raw spacing
utilities in components; a generic rule harness (type/palette/hover-alpha rules
slot in next). Its allowlist is the ledger of every deliberately-fixed intrinsic
exception (slider track, segmented-field cells, tuned icon gaps, satellite gaps),
each with a reason. 46 components, 0 violations.

Migration audit of all ~120 raw usages: most are legitimately-fixed control
anatomy (recorded in the allowlist, unchanged). The genuine composition/air and
standard-padding spots became roles: Note/Statistic bodies p-1 -> pad-box (they
now breathe with density), Panel/CollapsibleSection title bars py-0.5 ->
pad-chrome-y, Menu rows px-1.5 -> pad-control-x. The field<->reset-satellite gap
stays FIXED (a reset belongs to its field; it must not drift as the form breathes).

Docs (AGENTS/design-spec/SKILL/llms) carry the vocabulary table + the lint rule.
Verified: default byte-identical (22px controls, 12.5px, 6px field gap, 4px box);
roles scale correctly under density (gap-field 6->12, gap-group 4->8, gap-section
16->32; gap-tight/pad-control fixed); control-height audit 77/0; svelte-check 0
errors.

first_commit_message:
feat(brandkit): wire design-agent — WCAG palette correction + application templates

Wires the new @orb/design-agent package into the existing brand-kit
pipeline. Two pure-code phases now run alongside the existing
LLM-tuned logo + graphics generation (which stays untouched per the
parked-brand-kit memory — that prompt was tuned over 3-5 days):

- ensureWcagPalette() runs every Sonnet-generated palette through the
  AA contrast validator. If any text/bg pair fails (ink/bg, ink/surface
  at 4.5; primary/bg, accent/bg at 3.0), we re-derive deterministically
  from the LLM's primary as anchor. The LLM keeps its directional
  taste; the math guarantees readable output.

- renderBrandTemplates() returns 5 application templates (favicon,
  social avatar, business card, email header, instagram post) from
  the kit's palette + the inner contents of its mark SVG. Pure code,
  cheap enough to compute on every getMine read — added to the tRPC
  return shape so the UI can render mockups without a separate query.

Templates are inlined as TS string exports rather than fs.readFileSync
of .svg files — Next.js doesn't trace non-JS assets from workspace
packages by default, which would silently break templates on Vercel.
The .svg files in src/templates/ are kept as canonical authoring
format only.

description:
Modify a specific Component on a GameObject in opened Prefab or in a Scene. Allows direct modification of component fields and properties without wrapping in GameObject structure. Use 'gameobject-component-get' first to inspect the component structure before modifying.

Three modification surfaces (use whichever fits the task):
  1. 'componentDiff' — full SerializedMember diff (legacy, backwards compatible).
  2. 'pathPatches' — list of {path, value} pairs routed through Reflector.TryModifyAt; atomic per-path modification, multiple entries can target different depths.
  3. 'jsonPatch' — a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396, extended with [i]/[key] notation) routed through Reflector.TryPatch; multiple fields at any depth in a single call.
When more than one is supplied they run in this order: jsonPatch → pathPatches → componentDiff. At least one is required.
Path syntax: 'fieldName', 'nested/field', 'arrayField/[i]', 'dictField/[key]'. Leading '#/' is stripped.

first_commit_message:
v0.8.0 — Multi-provider (Claude + Codex), Telegram bridge, git panel (#2)

## Summary

This PR cuts **v0.8.0**, a substantial release that takes MultiTable
from "Claude-only chat dashboard" to "multi-agent cockpit with remote
approval, full git workflow, and a notification stack." 57 commits, ~52k
LOC.

### Headline changes

- **Multi-provider architecture.** Introduced a `ProviderAdapter`
contract under `packages/daemon/src/agent/providers/`. Claude logic
extracted from `agent/manager.ts` into a dedicated `ClaudeAdapter`.
Codex is now a peer adapter (`CodexAdapter`) speaking line-delimited
JSON-RPC directly to `codex app-server` — no PTY, no `@openai/codex-sdk`
dependency. Generated TS bindings live under
`agent/providers/codex-protocol/` (codex-cli 0.128.0 pinned).
`AgentSessionManager` is now a thin, provider-agnostic orchestrator with
a 5-min no-progress watchdog and capability advertisement.
- **Telegram bridge.** New `notifications/telegramBridge.ts` +
`telegramApi.ts` + `telegramFormat.ts`. Permission prompts,
ask-questions, and session alerts forward to a Telegram chat with inline
keyboards; tapping Allow / Deny / Always-Allow flows the answer back to
`PermissionManager` and resolves the SDK's `canUseTool` Promise.
Configure via `/api/integrations/telegram` (token from env
`MULTITABLE_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` or `~/.multitable/secrets.yml`).
- **Full git panel** — not just diffs. Status, staging, commit composer,
branch picker, branch create/switch/delete, stash/pop, fetch/pull/push.
Live-updated by a per-project `GitWatcher` (debounced chokidar) over the
new `git:status-changed` WS event. `git_baseline_commit` per session
lets you see exactly what *that agent* changed.
- **Modes per agent** — `default`, `plan`, `accept-edits`, `auto`,
`chat`, `read-only`. Each adapter translates appropriately (Claude →
`permissionMode`; Codex resets the thread because options are immutable
post-start).
- **Live reasoning + tool deltas.** `session:assistant-delta`,
`session:reasoning-delta`, `session:tool-delta`, `session:tool-progress`
over WS. Chain-of-thought renders into a collapsible `ReasoningCard`;
tool I/O streams mid-execution.
- **Elicitation forms.** New `ElicitationManager` for MCP-style
schema/url prompts (distinct from `PermissionManager`). UI renders
schema-driven JSON forms.
- **Notification center + browser/audio alerts.** Per-category +
per-severity prefs, tab badge, OS notifications, in-app history with
severity icons.
- **Past Agents browser.** Resume any past Claude or Codex thread from
disk; both transcripts parse into the same `Message[]` shape.
- **Live model picker.** `GET /api/providers/models` discovers via
`codex debug models` + Anthropic `/v1/models` with fallback to canonical
aliases.
- **Dev log panel.** In-app daemon-event ring buffer (timers,
permission, watchdog, codex, agent, ws).
- **UI rename:** "session" → "agent" throughout the user-facing copy.
`PastSessions.tsx` → `PastAgentsList.tsx`. Internal type names
(`AgentSession`, `Session`) unchanged.
- **Docs:** `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md` fully rewritten to reflect the
above. New design docs: `docs/CODEX_APP_SERVER_MIGRATION.md`,
`docs/THREE_PROVIDER_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md`.

### Retired (don't reintroduce)
- `@openai/codex-sdk` npm dependency — replaced by direct app-server
JSON-RPC.
- "Claude logic inline in `manager.ts`" — Claude is now an adapter, peer
to Codex.
- `PastSessions.tsx` — replaced by `PastAgentsList` (sidebar) +
`PastAgentsBrowser` (modal).

### Migration notes

- DB schema additions on `sessions`: `agent_provider`, `model`,
`agent_session_id`, `agent_session_id_history`, `mode`, `scratchpad`,
`tags`, `loader_variant`, `git_baseline_commit`, `terminal_alerts`. New
tables: `claude_session_loaders`, `session_events`. SQLite `CREATE TABLE
IF NOT EXISTS` makes this forward-compatible on existing DBs.
- Codex auth: install `codex-cli`, run `codex login`. The daemon spawns
one `codex app-server` child lazily on first Codex turn.
- Telegram is opt-i
last_commit_message:
feat(providers): GitHub Copilot as the sixth agent provider (#61)

Adds GitHub Copilot as a fully live provider alongside Claude / Codex /
Hermes / Grok / Cursor, driven by `@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.5
(exact-pinned).

## Architecture

- **`agent/providers/copilot.ts`** — `CopilotAdapter`: ONE long-lived
bundled-CLI JSON-RPC child per daemon (lazy `start()` on first Copilot
turn, `stop()` on shutdown), many `CopilotSession`s multiplexed on it.
Session cache keyed by {copilot id, model, effort}; model/effort flips
disconnect + `resumeSession` over preserved history.
- **Native modes** — Copilot 1.0.5 exposes `MessageOptions.agentMode`
per send: `interactive` / `plan` / `autopilot` pass through verbatim, no
session rebuild on flip. Plan mode's execute gate
(`onExitPlanModeRequest`) routes through the same ExitPlanMode
permission card Claude/Grok use.
- **Permissions** — kind-discriminated `PermissionRequest`s (shell
carries full command text + intention, write carries fileName + diff,
etc.) map onto rich `PermissionManager` prompts. `onUserInputRequest`
(choices → AskUserQuestion; freeform → elicitation form) and
`onElicitationRequest` (1:1 `ElicitationManager`) are both wired — the
agent hangs on any unwired channel.
- **Streaming** — additive deltas, canonical `assistant.message`
supersedes previews, `session.idle` (never `assistant.turn_end`) ends
the turn, `session.abort()` for stop.
- **Transcripts** — `transcripts/copilotParser.ts` parses
`~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl` (the checkpoints are
compaction summaries, not history) for restart hydration; validated
against 67 real local sessions.
- **Catalog** — `COPILOT_BASELINE` seed + live `discoverCopilot()` via a
short-lived `client.listModels()` probe (per-model effort levels).
- **Usage limits** — `client.rpc.account.getQuota` → premium-request
window + credits; never spawns the CLI just to poll. `costUsd: false`
(SDK cost is a billing multiplier, not USD).

## Hardening found during live testing

- `reasoningEffort` on a non-supporting model hard-fails
`session.create` → one retry without it.
- `reasoningText` repeats across a turn's `assistant.message` events →
deduped (adapter + parser).
- Exit-plan approvals with a wrong-provider target mode are coerced to
the adapter's first non-plan mode in the manager; the web ExitPlanMode
picker now covers `autopilot`/`interactive`.

## Docs

CLAUDE.md provider sections brought current (they also predated
Grok/Cursor), `docs/reference/USAGE_LIMITS.md` Copilot row filled in,
and the `github-copilot-sdk` skill corrected to verified 1.0.5 reality
(native agentMode, `events.jsonl` persistence, new pitfalls #31).

## Verification (all live against the local daemon + real Copilot
account)

- Streaming turn with tool calls (view/create/powershell) → deltas,
canonical messages, tool cards, token usage.
- Interactive mode: shell + write permission prompts with real
command/diff payloads → approve → run.
- Autopilot: no prompts. Plan: runtime-native behavior, writes still
permission-gated.
- Mid-stream Stop → `cancelled`, partial text flushed, session reusable.
- Multi-turn history preserved; daemon restart → hydration from
`events.jsonl`; `/clear` → fresh provider conversation id with history
tracked.
- Usage-limits badge shows live premium-request quota.
- `npm run build` + `npm run lint` green.

description:
Fix JavaScript regex failures when matching CJK (Chinese/Japanese/Korean) text using \b word
boundaries. Use when: (1) Regex pattern with \b silently fails to match Japanese, Chinese, or
Korean text, (2) Pattern works for Latin/ASCII text but not CJK, (3) hasDriverLicenceCue or
similar text-detection function returns false for CJK input despite correct characters,
(4) inferIssuerFromTitleText or pattern-matching functions fail on non-Latin scripts.
Root cause: JavaScript \b only recognizes [a-zA-Z0-9_] as "word characters" — CJK characters
are classified as \W (non-word), so \b before/after CJK always sees a non-word/non-word
boundary and fails to match.

chore(agents): share workflow rules and skill library with the team (#3988)

* chore(agents): codify worktree, rebase, no-stack, no-debt, and test rules

Promotes four workflow non-negotiables from personal agent memory into
the repo so every contributor (human or agent) gets the same playbook:

- Always start in a new worktree branched from `origin/main` (not local
  `main`, which can be stale).
- Always `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main` before every
  `git push` (use `--force-with-lease`, never `--force`).
- Never stack PRs — every PR targets `main`. Combine dependent features
  into one bigger PR with delineated commits, instead of splitting and
  basing one PR's branch on another's.
- No technical debt — fix issues in the PR that touches them; no
  deferral via `// TODO`, `@Skip`, or commented-out code (transitional
  TODOs with tracking-issue links remain allowed per code_style.md).
- Failing tests are never acceptable and always your fault. `origin/main`
  always passes, so any red test on a feature branch is caused by that
  branch's diff. Never blame flakiness, never `@Skip` to silence, never
  push red.

The detailed reference and rationale live in `.claude/rules/agent_workflow.md`.
`AGENTS.md` and `self_review_checklist.md` get the operational summary at
the gates where they apply (start of task, before commit, before PR).

.claude/settings.json were excluded from the source zip already (not part
of build-release.sh's include list) and are confirmed untouched — that's
this repo's genuinely local/personal state, not build output.

Pre-existing files unique to .claude/ (a handful of hooks/rules/agents
core/ doesn't have) were intentionally left in place, not deleted, since
this pass didn't establish whether those are stray drift or deliberate
local additions — a separate decision, not blocking this resync.

first_commit_message:
Docs updates (#181)

* Disable pedantic lints on faer

* Added clippy CI checks

* Restructure workspace: pwdft/{pwdft-core,pwdft-benches,faer} + validation/

Consolidate Rust crates under pwdft/ and merge scripts/ + qe_validation/
into a proper Python uv package under validation/.

Layout
------
.                              (workspace root)
├── Cargo.toml                 (pure workspace; pwdft-core, pwdft-benches, faer/*)
├── .cargo/config.toml         (CARGO_WORKSPACE_DIR env var for test paths)
├── inputs/                    (was pwdft/examples/: YAML calculation inputs)
├── outputs/                   (new scratch dir, gitignored)
├── pseudopotentials/          (user-facing PP library, root-level)
├── pwdft/
│   ├── pwdft-core/            (library + pwdft binary; renamed from pwdft-rs)
│   ├── pwdft-benches/         (criterion benches extracted to own crate)
│   └── faer/                  (vendored, now a workspace member group)
└── validation/                (merged scripts/ + qe_validation/)
    ├── pyproject.toml         (uv + hatchling + ruff + mypy + pytest)
    ├── src/pwdft_validation/
    │   ├── _paths.py          (REPO_ROOT, QE_REF_DIR, CSV_REF_DIR, ...)
    │   ├── cli.py             (pwdft-validate dispatcher)
    │   └── scripts/           (was scripts/validate/*.py)
    ├── reference/
    │   ├── csv/               (was scripts/validate/*.csv)
    │   └── qe/                (was qe_validation/)
    └── tests/

Rust changes
------------
- Crate rename: `pwdft-rs` → `pwdft-core`; binary still named `pwdft`.
- Benches moved to their own crate so criterion stays out of pwdft-core's
  dev-deps; `cargo bench -p pwdft-benches` from workspace root.
- Workspace lints/profiles centralized at root Cargo.toml.
- Faer unpatched (no more `[patch.crates-io]`); workspace path dep instead.
- All 32 test/src references `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR.join("pseudopotentials/…")`
  etc. retargeted to `CARGO_WORKSPACE_DIR` so data dirs stay at the root.
- `"qe_validation/…"` → `"validation/reference/qe/…"` in Rust tests.
- `"scripts/validate/…csv"` → `"validation/reference/csv/…csv"`.

Python validation package
-------------------------
- PEP 621 pyproject.toml, hatchling build backend, ruff + mypy + pytest.
- `pwdft-validate <script>` CLI dispatcher; each script keeps its own
  `main()` and remains runnable via `uv run python -m pwdft_validation.scripts.<name>`.
- `_paths.py` replaces the brittle `Path(__file__).parents[N]` chains.
- Existing scripts updated for the new depth (parents[2] → parents[4]).
- Symlinks `reference/qe/pseudo{,_pbe}` re-pointed to
  `../../../pseudopotentials/nc/{lda,pbe}` from the new location.

Infrastructure
--------------
- `.cargo/config.toml` exposes `CARGO_WORKSPACE_DIR` (relative to the
  workspace root) so tests locate top-level data without `..` walks.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` gains a `validation` job running
  ruff check + ruff format + mypy + pytest via `uv sync --extra dev`.
- `.claude/bin/check-worktree.sh` main-checkout guard retargeted from
  `src/`, `tests/`, `benches/`, `build.rs` to `pwdft/pwdft-core/`,
  `pwdft/pwdft-benches/`, `pwdft/faer/`, `validation/`.
- `.gitignore` updated: faer/ → pwdft/faer/, outputs/* except .gitkeep,
  Python tooling caches for validation/.
- CLAUDE.md paths updated throughout (examples → inputs, src → pwdft/
  pwdft-core/src, qe_validation → validation/reference/qe, etc.).

History preserved
-----------------
~370 renames detected by git (source-code moves + in-file rewrites for
pwdft_rs → pwdft_core and CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR → CARGO_WORKSPACE_DIR).
`git log --follow` traces every file through the move.

Known follow-ups (deferred)
---------------------------
- Clippy on vendored faer trips `eq_op` from defaults — not regressed by
  this PR, but now visible since faer joined the workspace. Needs either
  a file-level `#![allow]` in faer or an exclusion mechanism.
- A handful of ruff warnings remain in validation scripts (minor, doc-
  character choices); tracked for

fix: apply codex review on set bundled main model — refresh SettingsSectionView bindings + honest docs

Codex caught a real semantic bug in the prior commit (348951b) that
I missed in my own verification: the new scripting command wrote to
`LocalModelConfig.save()` but the Settings picker's `@State`
bindings in `SettingsSectionView` are initialized once on view
mount via `LocalModelConfig.load()` and never automatically
refreshed. The failure mode when Settings is already open:

1. User opens Settings — `localMainModel @State` = "gemma-3-4b-it-4bit"
   from the initial `.load()`.
2. `tell app "Mosspath" to set bundled main model
   "mlx-community/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-4bit"` fires → the command
   saves the new value to UserDefaults.
3. `SettingsSectionView.localMainModel` stays pinned at
   "gemma-3-4b-it-4bit" — the @State wasn't notified of the
   external change.
4. `LocalInferenceSettingsCard.body` rebuilds:
   - `persistedConfig = LocalModelConfig.load()` → sees the new
     Llama value.
   - `draftConfig` from picker bindings → still gemma.
   - `hasPendingChanges = draftConfig != persistedConfig` → true.
5. Card flips to "Pending change" state with the top card showing
   Llama and the picker section still showing gemma. Apply button
   becomes affordant.
6. User clicks Apply → `applyLocalModelConfig()` saves the gemma
   draft back on top of Llama, silently reverting the command's
   change.

That's a full semantic reversal of the command's intended effect.
Worse, it made the scripting command USELESS for its stated
purpose — it would not actually persist the new model if Settings
was open.

The fix is a notification that `SettingsSectionView` observes
whenever the command (or any other non-UI code path) mutates
`LocalModelConfig`, so the picker's draft `@State` stays coherent
with persisted state:

- `HooksSectionView.swift`: add
  `.mosspathLocalModelConfigChanged` notification name alongside
  the other `mosspathNavigate*` names, with a comment explaining
  its purpose.

- `ScriptingCommands.swift`:
  `SetBundledMainModelCommand.apply()` now posts the notification
  after a successful `.save()`. Does NOT post on the error path
  (empty / whitespace-only ID) because nothing was persisted.

- `SettingsSectionView.swift`: add a new `.onReceive` observer for
  `.mosspathLocalModelConfigChanged` that re-reads
  `LocalModelConfig.load()` and copies the three picker bindings
  (`localMainModel`, `localVisionModel`, `localUseSeparateVision`)
  from the fresh config. After the command fires, draft ==
  persisted and the Settings card's Apply button goes back to
  "No Pending Changes" — correct, because the persistence
  already happened.

- `SetBundledMainModelCommandTests.swift`: add two new tests.
  `applyPostsLocalModelConfigChangedNotification` verifies the
  happy path posts at least one notification;
  `applyDoesNotPostNotificationOnError` verifies the error path
  does not post (so UI observers don't needlessly re-read config
  when the save was rejected). Adds a small
  `NotificationExpectation` helper that counts posts via a
  thread-safe observer so the test is Sendable-safe under Swift
  6 strict concurrency (NSLock around the counter, observer
  on `.main` queue).

Also updates `.claude/skills/ui-test/SKILL.md` to accurately
describe what the command does and — importantly — what it does
NOT do:

- ✓ persists new main model to `LocalModelConfig`
- ✓ refreshes open Settings picker bindings via notification
- ✗ does NOT restart the local engine
- ✗ does NOT drive the "Pending change" UI state (because
  draft ends up == persisted after the command runs)

The old SKILL.md copy claimed the command would "drive the
Settings picker" and produce the pending-change state, neither
of which is true now. If a future session needs to test the
pending-change / unsupported-model gate UI specifically, that
needs a separate `set bundled main model draft "<id>"` variant
that only mutates the in-memory @State via notification wit

docs(skills): bind feature-branch histories to main before fixup commits

Fixes the recurring add/add merge conflict on the handoff doc whenever
a pause-window baton sync to main (per [[feedback_next_session_main_authoritative]])
collides with a subsequent fixup commit on the feature branch.

Root cause: when /nextsession close-out commits the handoff doc to
both the feature branch AND main, the two branches add the same file
path independently. Any later edit to the doc on the branch (typical:
/fixall after a code review) creates an add/add conflict that
squash-merge does NOT silently resolve — the PR goes CONFLICTING / DIRTY
and `gh pr merge` refuses.

Permanent fix: bind the histories at the start of every fixup pass by
`git fetch && git merge origin/main` BEFORE editing files. This puts
main's sync commit into the branch's ancestry, so subsequent edits are
3-way-mergeable. Conflict-on-merge is the typical case (branch has the
same doc with the same content); resolution is one line:
`git checkout --ours <handoff-path>` because the in-flight fixup is
strictly newer than main's snapshot.

Changes:
- .claude/skills/fixall/SKILL.md: pre-edit fetch+merge step + conflict
  resolution recipe.
- .claude/skills/commit-push/SKILL.md: pre-push fetch+merge step gated
  on "branch has open PR" so main-branch commits are unaffected.
- .claude/skills/nextsession/SKILL.md: new "fixup-time merge discipline"
  section explaining the failure mode + symptoms + the recipe. Updated
  the prior "Why this avoids conflicts" bullet to note the gap that
  the new section closes.

Surfaced by PR #119 (C.2 Task 6) review-fixup hitting CONFLICTING /
DIRTY after a clean first push; resolved manually that one time, then
codified here so it stops recurring.

locked fs run-store with legacy run-dir compatibility.

council.toml ships documented defaults for the new sections: [watchdog]

plus prompt/schema assets and excludes council/ts sources from the

validate_manifest now enforces skill-target parity against each skill's

Autonomous build loop: stabilise, guest email lifecycle, perf, a11y/tablet polish

Sets up an agent-driven build system (.claude/agents, BUILD_PLAN.md, SYSTEM_MAP.md,
PROJECT_CONTEXT.md, /build-loop skill) against a fixed, owner-approved scope checklist,
then runs it end to end:

Phase 0/1 (safety net + audit): mapped the full codebase into SYSTEM_MAP.md; extended
scripts/smoke_test_booking.php with availability/pricing coverage and added
scripts/smoke_test_finance.php for money-sequence logic; standardized POS cash-tendered
comparisons on BALANCE_TOLERANCE; fixed admin/backup-management.php's CSRF scheme to use
the standard validator; fixed a genuinely broken api/blocked-dates.php endpoint that was
404ing on every call before reaching its own logic; added an explicit visibility guard +
rate limiting to api/page-content.php; closed a public-facing info leak where
includes/db-error.php printed raw DB exception detail to the browser console on every
connection failure, and hardened .user.ini's display_errors/log_errors for PHP-FPM.

Phase 2 (guest communication + performance): added pre-arrival reminder and post-stay
review-request guest emails (scripts/guest_lifecycle_emails.php +
admin/includes/guest-lifecycle-lib.php + config/email.php + a booking-settings.php admin
toggle, both defaulting off); extracted booking.php's ~2200-line inline script into a
cacheable js/booking.js.

Phase 3 (polish): fixed a WCAG contrast failure across the booking flow, added 44px
touch targets to check-in and housekeeping admin screens, and converged two public
pages' off-palette text colors onto the site's existing warm-brown vocabulary.

Owner decisions: kept includes/seo-meta.php (found to be a live dependency of
booking-confirmation.php, not dead code as initially scouted); kept manual payment
settlement at check-in rather than adding an online gateway.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <<redacted>>

last_commit_message:
MaaS improvements: PVC, observability, settle-gated install, GPU-aware models (#7)

Persistent MaaS storage, RHOAI Observability dashboard backend, and the
install/script tooling needed to deploy them safely on reasonably-sized
clusters. Driven by the cluster-hm2fl OOM on 2026-04-20 where the
DSCI-monitoring cascade tipped 16 GiB masters past their memory ceiling
during a previously-working `make maas` flow.

Storage and observability:
- MaaS PostgreSQL gains a 20Gi PVC (gp3-csi default; size and storage class
  configurable via Helm values). PVC and Deployment in the same sync-wave
  to avoid an ArgoCD WaitForFirstConsumer deadlock.
- DSCI `monitoring.metrics.storage` populated so the rhods-operator's
  Monitoring controller provisions Perses, TempoStack,
  OpenTelemetryCollector DaemonSet, NodeMetricsEndpoint, MonitoringStack
  and ThanosQuerier — but only on the maas-observability overlay (see
  next section), not by default.
- Cluster Observability Operator subscribed in its canonical namespace
  `openshift-cluster-observability-operator` (provides Perses CRDs).
- OpenTelemetry Product operator subscribed (provides
  OpenTelemetryCollector CRD that the Monitoring controller requires).
- MaaS-side observability GitOps Kustomize: Kuadrant TelemetryPolicy
  (model/user/subscription/org/cost-center labels on gateway metrics) and
  Istio Telemetry (per-subscription request-duration). KServe ServiceMonitor
  scrapes vllm:* metrics from LLMInferenceService pods.
- Kuadrant `spec.observability.enable: true` moved into GitOps (no more
  imperative patch racing with self-heal).

Install tooling — settle-gate and decoupling:
- `make maas` and `make observability` are now independent. `install-maas.sh`
  no longer calls `install-observability.sh`. The monitoring cascade is
  heavy on the control plane and now runs only when explicitly requested.
- `components/instances/rhoai-instance/` split into `base` + `overlays/maas`
  + `overlays/maas-observability`. Base is the no-cascade safe baseline.
  Default ApplicationSet entry points at `overlays/maas`. `make observability`
  flips `instance-rhoai` to `overlays/maas-observability`; reversible.
- `install-observability.sh` runs a settle-gate before flipping: required
  CSVs Succeeded, DSC Ready=True + DSCI Available=True/Degraded=False, no
  non-terminal pods in core namespaces, etcd Available + Degraded=False,
  and all masters under 75% memory. Refuses (does not override) if the
  cluster isn't ready.
- UWM ownership moved to `make infra` via new `scripts/enable-uwm.sh`.
  `install-observability.sh` verifies UWM is on and fails fast pointing
  at `make uwm` if not.

Preflight, diagnose, scripts:
- New `scripts/lib/cluster-health.sh` provides shared control-plane checks:
  master sizing (<32 GiB FAIL, 32-63 WARN, >=64 PASS), master memory/CPU
  pressure, ClusterOperators (Available/Degraded). Wired into preflight
  (--fail-hard) and diagnose (read-only). PREFLIGHT_SKIP_SIZING=1 and
  PREFLIGHT_SIM_INSTANCE_TYPE=<type> hooks for testing.
- `scripts/restart-catalog.sh` extracts the Makefile target body to a
  script, and after bouncing pods, deletes the rhods-operator Subscription
  so OLM re-resolves a fresh InstallPlan against the new catalog. Required
  workaround when the floating `:rhoai-3.4-nightly` tag is regressed
  (currently pinned to `:rhoai-3.4` for that reason).
- `setup-maas-model.sh` autodetect default: no GPU -> simulator;
  `nvidia.com/gpu.memory` >=40 GiB -> gpt-oss-20b; otherwise
  granite-tiny-gpu. Reads NVIDIA GPU operator labels from the cluster.
- `validate-config.sh` and `preflight-check.sh` downgrade pre-install
  inventory checks (no GPU yet, no .env yet) from FAIL/WARN to INFO.

Skills and docs:
- `.claude/skills/install-rhoai/SKILL.md` and `install-maas/SKILL.md`
  rewritten: drop the `cp .env.example .env` auto-create, add UWM phase,
  drop the hardcoded model decision table (script autodetects), document
  observability as opt-in (--with-observability), add set

first_commit_message:
chore(.claude): resync .claude/ from core/ via build-release.sh (item #4)

Resolves the core/.claude drift flagged in the earlier architecture
review. Investigation found .claude/ is not a personal sandbox — it's
this repo's own dogfood install target (plugin.json's install.target is
".claude/", and core/scripts/build-release.sh packages core/ into a zip
explicitly meant to be unzipped into a target project's .claude/, this
repo included). It had drifted badly: .claude/skills/ had only 402 of
core/'s 1990 skill dirs, several hooks/scripts/rules existed on only one
side, agents count differed by one.

Ran build-release.sh (which gates on a 100% hook-test pass — see the
separate hook-portability-fixes commit that unblocked it), then unzipped
the resulting pack over .claude/{agents,commands,config,docs,gates,hooks,
prompts,rules,scripts,skills,templates,tests}/ as a pure overlay (adds/
updates, does not delete). .claude/assistant/, .claude/state/, and
.claude/settings.json were excluded from the source zip already (not part
of build-release.sh's include list) and are confirmed untouched — that's
this repo's genuinely local/personal state, not build output.

Pre-existing files unique to .claude/ (a handful of hooks/rules/agents
core/ doesn't have) were intentionally left in place, not deleted, since
this pass didn't establish whether those are stray drift or deliberate
local additions — a separate decision, not blocking this resync.

Verified: bash .claude/tests/hooks/run-hook-tests.sh → 104/104 pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <<redacted>>

* refactor(commands): adopt official arguments name-list and argument-hint frontmatter

Convert all 252 command files from the undocumented object-list arguments:
form to the official name-list form (arguments: [a, b, c]), synthesize
argument-hint from required/optional flags (244 files; 8 already had one),
move per-argument descriptions into an '## Arguments' body section where the
body had no Arguments/Parameters section (43 files), and drop the unused
name: frontmatter key. Verified mechanically that every $name placeholder
referenced in a command body still matches a declared argument (13 files
bind arguments; zero undeclared references).

* refactor(skills): fold triggers into official frontmatter fields

Fold the non-standard triggers: list on all 301 skills into the official
fields: append a 'Use when: ...' sentence built from the trigger phrases to
when_to_use (296 skills) or to description where no when_to_use exists
(5 skills), then remove triggers:. Also drop the stray version: and
dependencies: keys carried by the two shared skills
(billing-reconciliation, wyre-gateway-troubleshooting). Body content
untouched; folded re-emission is asserted lossless.

* docs(templates): emit official frontmatter formats in templates and contributor guides

Update the scaffolding so newly generated plugins no longer reintroduce the
deprecated formats: skill-template folds trigger phrases into
when_to_use/description (no triggers: list), command-template and both
llm-prompt generators emit the official arguments name-list plus
argument-hint with per-argument descriptions in the body, CONTRIBUTING's
embedded skill/command templates and checklists match, and
claude-marketplace.md now points $schema at the real SchemaStore entry
instead of the 404 anthropic.com placeholder. agent-template.md already
used only official fields (name, description, tools, model) and is
unchanged.

* fix(agents): make agent frontmatter valid YAML by folding descriptions

All 110 affected agent files carried a single-line unquoted description
containing ': ' (e.g. 'Trigger for: ...'), which is invalid YAML - strict
parsers reject the frontmatter with 'mapping values are not allowed here'.
This was pre-existing on main and silently broke any strict-YAML consumer
of agent frontmatter. Re-emit description as a folded block scalar (>-),
asserted lossless. Trigger text was already merged into description on
every agent, and no agent carries unsupported keys (only name,
description, tools, model), so no other agent changes were needed.

* chore: bump patch versions and regenerate docs data for frontmatter modernization

Bump the plugin.json patch version of all 61 plugins whose command, skill,
or agent files changed in this branch (bump-gate compliance). Teach the
docs generator's minimal frontmatter parser to understand YAML block-scalar
chomping indicators (>-, >+, |-, |+) so folded agent descriptions parse,
and regenerate docs/src/data (plugins.ts, sharedSkills.ts) from the new
frontmatter and versions. marketplace.json intentionally untouched (owned
by a sibling PR).

* chore: rebase version bumps

After rebasing onto main (#136), nine plugins that both branches had
patch-bumped to identical versions no longer registered as bumped
relative to the new base, tripping the bump gate
(scripts/check-marketplace-drift.mjs). Bump each one more patch:
kaseya-quote-manager 1.0.2, autotask 0.4.3, datto-rmm 1.1.3,
it-glue 1.1.3, rocketcyber 0.2.3, salesbuildr 1.1.3, superops 0.2.3,
syncro 0.2.3, wyre-gateway 1.2.2. Docs data regen was a no-op
(plugins.ts does not embed plugin versions).

first_commit_message:
feat(claude): add preflight skill and drop redundant do-lint command

The preflight skill discovers just recipes via a bare `just` invocation
(leveraging the overridden default in our Justfiles), runs quality
gates in a sensible order (lint-fix, lint, typecheck, tests,
integration), and falls back through `pre-commit` → `uvx pre-commit` →
`uv tool run pre-commit` when the tool is not installed locally. It
enforces hard rules against suppressing failures with noqa/type-ignore
pragmas, pyproject ignore entries, or skipped tests — fixes must
address the root cause. The skill reports push-readiness and never
pushes or commits automatically. do-lint is dropped because preflight
now covers lint as part of the broader gauntlet.

refactor(develop): consolidate _internal/ into artifacts skill, adopt MIT

Replace the develop/skills/_internal/<type>/ pseudo-skill structure
with a single skills/artifacts/ skill (user-invocable: false) plus
supporting per-type reference files. Apply review findings against
the current Claude Code skill and subagent specs. Adopt MIT license.

## Architecture: artifacts skill

The previous _internal/<type>/SKILL.md files were not real skills (no
auto-discovery, frontmatter was decorative) but were structured like
skills, leading to spec-validation failures and conceptual drift. The
new shape:

  develop/skills/artifacts/
  - SKILL.md       # registry + dispatcher
  - model.md       # cross-cutting work graph rules
  - guidelines.md  # interaction posture
  - <type>.md      # self-contained per-type guides

Migrate (rename + content edit) develop/skills/_internal/<type>/SKILL.md
to develop/skills/artifacts/<type>.md for adr, epic, milestone, project,
spec, spike, story, task, work-item, workstream. Each loses its
frontmatter and "Write Path" section (path lives in the registry now)
and gains a top-level Schema section (YAML frontmatter example + body
description).

Merge the previous concept.md and schemas.md cross-cutting files into
a single model.md (work graph: hierarchy, frames, common fields, typed
links, lifecycles, naming, traceability, readiness). The three-way
split had fuzzy boundaries; the new two-way split (model = what is
true; guidelines = how to behave) has crisp distinct jobs.

## Agent frontmatter (spec violations)

Per the subagent frontmatter reference, agents support: name,
description, tools, disallowedTools, model, effort, maxTurns, skills,
etc. They do NOT support `when_to_use`, `context`, or `allowed-tools`.
The previous frontmatter on architect, developer, and tech-lead used
skill-only fields, which were silently ignored — meaning declared tool
restrictions did not actually apply.

- Rename `allowed-tools` -> `tools` so restrictions take effect.
- Drop `context: fork` (skill field; agents already have their own
  context window by definition).
- Fold `when_to_use` trigger phrases into `description` so they reach
  Claude's delegation matcher.
- Add `skills: [develop:artifacts]` preload to architect and developer
  so the artifact registry is injected at agent startup.

## Skill frontmatter cleanup

- Drop `model:` and `effort:` from all 6 user-facing skills (spec,
  plan, assess, build, test, survey). They overrode the user's session
  choice on every invocation; inheriting is more respectful of pace
  and cost preferences. Agents keep their model/effort settings.
- Drop unused `Bash` from artifacts/SKILL.md allowed-tools.
- Replace "the core foundation" / "Read X in full and follow its
  instructions" hardening prose across 6 user-facing skills and 2
  agents. Path discipline now lives once in the artifacts registry.

## De-duplication and schema placement

- Drop the inline spec template from agents/architect.md (40 lines
  duplicating artifacts/spec.md). Move architect-only sections

  artifacts/spec.md so the artifacts skill is the single source for

  convention to describe the artifacts-skill pattern.
- Update docs/artifacts/README.md schemas link.

chore(.claude): resync .claude/ from core/ via build-release.sh (item #4)

Resolves the core/.claude drift flagged in the earlier architecture
review. Investigation found .claude/ is not a personal sandbox — it's
this repo's own dogfood install target (plugin.json's install.target is
".claude/", and core/scripts/build-release.sh packages core/ into a zip
explicitly meant to be unzipped into a target project's .claude/, this
repo included). It had drifted badly: .claude/skills/ had only 402 of
core/'s 1990 skill dirs, several hooks/scripts/rules existed on only one
side, agents count differed by one.

Ran build-release.sh (which gates on a 100% hook-test pass — see the
separate hook-portability-fixes commit that unblocked it), then unzipped
the resulting pack over .claude/{agents,commands,config,docs,gates,hooks,
prompts,rules,scripts,skills,templates,tests}/ as a pure overlay (adds/
updates, does not delete). .claude/assistant/, .claude/state/, and
.claude/settings.json were excluded from the source zip already (not part
of build-release.sh's include list) and are confirmed untouched — that's
this repo's genuinely local/personal state, not build output.

Pre-existing files unique to .claude/ (a handful of hooks/rules/agents
core/ doesn't have) were intentionally left in place, not deleted, since
this pass didn't establish whether those are stray drift or deliberate
local additions — a separate decision, not blocking this resync.

fix(macos): make TTS + WEBP work in production builds (Qt selection)

Two regressions that combined to break TTS and Codex pets in the v1.0.0
DMG, plus the build-script fixes that prevent recurrence.

Root cause #1 — Plugin redeploy pass too narrow.
scripts/build_release.py only repaired Contents/PlugIns/imageformats/
after macdeployqt, leaving Homebrew-absolute deps in multimedia/, tls/,
networkinformation/, and iconengines/. multimedia is fatal because Qt has
no fallback for QAudioDecoder; tls is fatal because openssl plugin
references absolute libssl/libcrypto and HTTPS dies. Now repairs all five
dirs.

Root cause #2 — Wrong Qt picked.
find_qt_prefix() queried qmake on PATH before scanning filesystem
candidates. Homebrew's qmake on PATH always won, even when the official
Qt Online Installer was at /opt/Qt. Homebrew's qtmultimedia bottle ships
only the AVFoundation backend; the official installer ships
libffmpegmediaplugin.dylib, which is the only backend that decodes raw
MP3 via QAudioDecoder. Reordered: filesystem candidates first
(/opt/Qt, /Applications/Qt, ~/Qt, C:\Qt), PATH last. Added /opt/Qt to
macOS candidates (was Linux-only). Added an interactive prompt as a
final fallback instead of silently continuing with a broken state.

Root cause #2b — macdeployqt qmake leak.
Even after CMake links against the right Qt, macdeployqt internally
shells out to `qmake -query QT_INSTALL_PLUGINS` and honors $PATH order.
With Homebrew's qmake on PATH, macdeployqt copies Homebrew 6.11.0
arm64-only plugins next to /opt/Qt 6.11.1 universal frameworks; the
plugin loader rejects them on minor-version mismatch (libqwebp fails,
Codex pets don't load). Now prepend <qt_prefix>/bin to PATH for the
macdeployqt subprocess.

Cleanup.
- plug_roots in the redeploy pass: removed hardcoded
  /opt/homebrew/Cellar paths, added <qt_prefix>/plugins for the
  official-installer layout. No more Homebrew-version literals.
- Support-dylib repair (libwebp/libsharpyuv/libpng/...) and the
  libsharpyuv copy fallback now gate on whether qt_prefix is a Homebrew
  install. The official installer doesn't ship these as separate
  Frameworks/*.dylib; the block was previously dead code there but
  hardcoded /opt/homebrew/lib regardless.
- Interactive prompt no longer prints version-numbered example paths
  ('/opt/Qt/6.11.1/macos'); uses '<Qt-install-root>/<version>/macos'
  template.

Skill updates (.claude/skills/seelie-build-deploy/SKILL.md).
- Prerequisites: warn that brew install qt is insufficient on macOS.
- Step 3: document the new auto-discovery order and the macdeployqt PATH
  override.
- Pitfall #8 (Qt kit selection): rewritten with the 4-step resolution.
- Pitfall #15: list now includes multimedia/networkinformation/
  iconengines/tls (the full plugin_dirs_to_repair tuple).
- Pitfall #18 (new): Homebrew-absolute deps in non-imageformats plugin
  dirs; broad /opt/ audit command.
- Pitfall #19 (new): Homebrew vs official Qt installer; FFmpeg backend
  requirement; macdeployqt qmake-leak follow-up; verification recipe
  that compares plugin Qt version to bundled framework Qt version.
- Pitfall #20 (new): build thrashing / serial build with
  CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=1.

user: "/hstack:kernel-fit-triage KF-0001 --action acknowledge"
assistant: "I'll read KF-0001, print it in full, show the proposed-diff (status: open → acknowledged; owner: <git-handle>; updated: today; Triage Log entry appended), wait for Y/n, then Edit + commit `kernel-fit(KF-0001): acknowledge`. No reason is required for acknowledge. If you later decide to promote, run `/hstack:kernel-fit-promote KF-0001 --slug <adr-slug>`."
<commentary>
Acknowledge does not require a `--reason`. It is the "I've seen this, I intend to act, but I'm not promoting yet" state. The Triage Log records the transition. The finding stays at `status: acknowledged` until promote or dismiss happens.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: The engineer reviewed KF-0002 and decided the pattern is engineer-error, not a kernel gap.
user: "/hstack:kernel-fit-triage KF-0002 --action dismiss --reason \"The two changes flagged actually do have downstream consumers; the change-specs simply omitted the user-stories array because the engineer copied an old template. Not a kernel-flag issue, just stale boilerplate.\""
assistant: "I'll verify the reason is ≥50 characters (KF-05), read KF-0002, print the proposed-diff (status: open → dismissed; dismissed-reason: <text>; owner; updated; Triage Log entry), wait for Y/n, then commit `kernel-fit(KF-0002): dismiss`. Dismissal is terminal — re-running on this finding will surface that it's already dismissed and exit no-op."
<commentary>
Dismissal requires a reason of ≥50 characters per KF-05. The check is mechanical at validation time; the Skill enforces it at step 2. Drive-by dismissals are exactly the failure mode the rule exists to catch. The dismissed-reason is itself audit signal — a high rate of dismissals on a given pattern means either the pattern is poorly tuned or the engineer is gaming the gate.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: The engineer tries to dismiss a finding with too-short reason.
user: "/hstack:kernel-fit-triage KF-0003 --action dismiss --reason \"not relevant\""
assistant: "I'll halt — `dismissed-reason` is 12 characters; KF-05 requires ≥50. Drive-by dismissals defeat the audit signal. Either provide a more substantive reason or leave the finding at `open` (open is a legitimate long-term state when triage is genuinely deferred)."
<commentary>
Short-reason rejection is a hard halt. The Skill does not negotiate — write a real reason or leave the finding alone. Same shape as the deferral-check in `hstack-tech-debt-wontfix`.
</commentary>
</example>

feat(kernel-fit): closed-loop system for detecting kernel-vs-practice drift

Five-layer post-hoc system that observes hstack usage and surfaces kernel
gaps as durable findings — without auto-modifying the kernel. The user
explicitly required a human gate on every promotion to an ADR.

- L1 Detection: `scripts/telemetry/insights/kernel_fit.py` with three
  starter patterns (KF-P1 internal-tooling conflation, KF-P2 halt-reason
  cluster, KF-P3 missed-gate recovery). Pure read; reconstructible from
  git + frontmatter.
- L2 Synthesis: new `kernel-fit-analyst` subagent (model: opus). Loads
  kernel + shipped artifacts + prior findings; explicitly NOT implementer
  transcripts (same rule as adversarial-reviewer). Mandatory two-bullet
  counter-explanation; auto-downgrades confidence to low if absent.
- L3 Artifact: `templates/kernel-fit-finding.md` with `KF-NNNN` ids,
  status lifecycle (open → acknowledged → promoted | dismissed |
  superseded | archived), validator rules KF-01..KF-05.
- L4 Skills: `/hstack:kernel-fit-scan` (detection + synthesis + Slack),
  `/hstack:kernel-fit-triage` (mechanical status flip per ADR-0001),
  `/hstack:kernel-fit-promote` (routes to /hstack:adr-new with the
  finding's Evidence + Kernel Surface + Proposed Direction as Context
  seed; spec-author runs the Nygard interview — the human gate).
- L5 Notification: Slack via MCP, threshold-gated (medium/high only),
  14-day dedup, graceful degradation when MCP unreachable.

Kernel integration: new `## How hstack improves itself` section before
`## References`; new `kernel-fit-analyst` entry in the subagent
load-at-session-start list; `promoted-from-kernel-fit: []` field added
to adr.md template (schema-version bump 1 -> 2) so reciprocity is
mechanically checkable.

Wiring: new `kernel-fit/` entry in `src/manifest.ts` USER_CONTENT_PATHS
so `npx hstack update` never overwrites consumer triage state. New
Skills propagate via per-skill symlinks; new subagent propagates via
dir-level symlink. `/hstack:adr-new` gains `--from-kernel-fit` flag
mirroring the existing `--from-research` pattern.

v1 honesty: detector patterns are hand-written Python rules;
`validate-spec.ts` is still a placeholder so KF-01..KF-05 are
bypassable via direct frontmatter edit until it ships; the promote
two-commit pattern is documented as a recoverable carve-out
analogous to /hstack:finalize in-progress.

See ADR-0003 for the design rationale.

Fold the v0.5.0 release lessons into the release skill

The v0.5.0 cut surfaced a handful of gaps the skill should have caught. Adds a
Phase 2.5 root-only prepublish dry-run -- the publish-npm job installs root deps
only, and a root test that imports app/electron code passes a normal local
`npm test` but breaks the gate (third time this has bitten a release). Fixes
the canonical-remote detection to use grep instead of awk (BSD awk chokes on the
char class), makes the PR set come from the commit range with `gh pr list
--limit` (the date search over-includes same-day pre-tag PRs and gh silently
truncates at 30), and documents recovery: `gh run rerun --failed` for a flaky
leg, and reuse-the-tag-only-if-npm-never-published. Also: clean-tree can trip on
smoke/package artifacts, new installer platforms never run their make until a
real release, and notes-file beats inline printf for the body.
